definition_zh: 一（个）；某一个；某一类中的一个；每一（用于频率或单价）；用于职业、身份、国籍之前；用于固定数量短语；某个（叫某名字的）人；用于否定或强调
definition_en: the indefinite article, used before a singular countable noun to mean one unspecified thing, one member of a class, or one for each unit
core_image: 伸出一根手指，从一整排里随手点出其中一个
scene: 清早的月台上人挤人，她头一回来这座城市，怕误了车。On the platform she asked a stranger to check the time.
sceneCN: 这里 a 是「首次提到的某一个」（第 1 个义项：不定指某一个）；句意为她在月台上向一个陌生人询问时间。

pos.zh: 冠词：不定冠词，表示「一个」或「某一个」，用于单数可数名词之前

derivatives.zh: 同一个不定冠词的变体，在元音音素前保留古英语 ān 的词尾 -n
与 a 同出古英语 ān 的数词，义为「一」，重读时仍保留完整形式
由古英语 ǣnig 演变而来，与 ān 同源，义为「任何一个；一些」
由古英语 ān 的属格 ānes 演变而来，与 one 同源，义为「一次」

senses.title: One unspecified thing, mentioned for the first time
senses.definition: used before a singular countable noun for a thing the listener cannot yet identify, because it is being introduced for the first time
senses.definitionCN: 用于单数可数名词之前，指听者尚不能确定、此刻第一次被提到的某个事物
senses.example: I saw a dog in the yard this morning.
senses.exampleCN: 今天早上我在院子里看见一只狗。
senses.why: The article began as the numeral one: one item is picked out, but the speaker does not say which one, so the listener only learns that the thing exists.
senses.whyCN: 这个冠词本来只是数词「一」：说话人点出了其中一个，却不说清是哪一个，于是听者只知道有这么个东西，这就是「不定指」。

senses.title: The quantity one
senses.definition: used before a unit, a fraction or a large round number to express the quantity one, as in a hundred, a dozen or a quarter
senses.definitionCN: 用于单位、分数或整十整百的数字之前，表示数量「一」，如 a hundred、a dozen、a quarter
senses.example: The hall holds a hundred people.
senses.exampleCN: 这个大厅能容纳一百人。
senses.why: This is the numeral showing through: before a counted unit the weakened article still does the old work of counting one.
senses.whyCN: 这是数词本义的残留：在计数的单位前面，弱化后的冠词仍在做「数一个」这件旧事，所以能表示「一」。

senses.title: Each, in rates and frequencies
senses.definition: used between two quantities to mean in each or for every, as in twice a week or sixty miles an hour
senses.definitionCN: 用在两个数量之间，表示「每一」，如 twice a week、sixty miles an hour
senses.example: She visits her mother twice a month.
senses.exampleCN: 她每个月去看母亲两次。
senses.why: If a means one item, then twice a week counts one week against each visit; the same single unit is simply read as per.
senses.whyCN: 如果 a 表示「一个」，那么 twice a week 就是拿一个星期去对一次探望；同一个「一」被读成了「每」，于是有了频率和单价的用法。

senses.title: A kind or sort of something
senses.definition: used before a noun in phrases such as a kind of or a sort of, where a single example stands for a whole type
senses.definitionCN: 用于 a kind of、a sort of 等短语中的名词之前，以单个例子代表整个类别
senses.example: It is a kind of thin, flexible glass.
senses.exampleCN: 它是一种薄而有弹性的玻璃。
senses.why: One member is singled out, but only as a sample of the type behind it; the article slides from the item to the class it stands for.
senses.whyCN: 这里仍是从中挑出一个，只不过它是背后那一类的样本；冠词的落点从「这一个东西」滑到了「这一种东西」。

senses.title: Before a profession or an identity
senses.titleCN: 用于职业、身份、国籍之前
senses.definition: used before a singular noun naming a job, religion, nationality or role, and required where many languages leave the noun bare
senses.definitionCN: 用于表示职业、宗教、国籍或身份的单数名词之前，许多语言此处不用冠词，英语则必须加
senses.example: My brother is a nurse at the city hospital.
senses.exampleCN: 我哥哥是市医院的一名护士。
senses.why: A person in a job is one member of the class of nurses, so the counting article marks the role as one instance of many.
senses.whyCN: 从事某种职业的人，是「护士」这一类里的一个成员；计数用的冠词在这里标注的是「该身份的一个实例」，所以英语不说 she is nurse。

senses.title: In fixed phrases of quantity
senses.definition: used in set phrases such as a few, a little, a lot of and a couple of, where the article no longer means simply one
senses.definitionCN: 用于 a few、a little、a lot of、a couple of 等固定短语，此时冠词已不再表示单纯的「一」
senses.example: We only need a few minutes to finish.
senses.exampleCN: 我们只需要几分钟就能完成。
senses.why: These are frozen chunks: the old one has worn into a quantity word, but the article stays on as part of the whole phrase.
senses.whyCN: 这些是凝固的短语块：原本的「一」已经磨成了一个数量词，但冠词仍作为整个短语的一部分留在里面。

senses.title: A certain person, known only by name
senses.definition: used before a family name to mean someone called, when the speaker does not know that person and expects the listener may not either
senses.definitionCN: 用于姓氏之前，表示「一个叫某名字的人」，说话人不认识此人，也预期听者未必认识
senses.example: A Mr Smith called while you were out.
senses.exampleCN: 你不在的时候，有位史密斯先生来过电话。
senses.why: One particular person is meant, yet the speaker cannot identify him; the article carries both the singularity and the ignorance in one word.
senses.whyCN: 这里确实指某一个具体的人，但说话人认不出他；冠词一个词就把「某一个」和「说不清是谁」同时承担下来，于是有了「一位叫……的」。

senses.title: In negation and emphasis
senses.definition: used in phrases such as not a word and without a doubt, where it strengthens a negative or a claim by naming the smallest single unit
senses.definitionCN: 用于 not a word、without a doubt 等短语，通过指出最小的「一个」来加强否定或肯定
senses.example: He left without a word.
senses.exampleCN: 他一句话也没说就走了。
senses.why: The smallest possible amount is one; denying even that one leaves nothing at all, so the article becomes the floor of a negation.
senses.whyCN: 最小的一份就是「一」；连这一个都被否掉，剩下的就是彻底的零，于是冠词成了否定句的地板，也成了强调的落脚点。

intro.en: The indefinite article is a worn-down form of the Old English numeral for one, and its two shapes still follow the sound that comes next.
intro.cn: 不定冠词是古英语数词「一」被磨弱后的形式，它的两种写法至今仍取决于后面那个音。

items.en: *oi-no- is generally reconstructed as the source of the numeral one; both the exact shape and the deeper origin are uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语重构形式 *oi-no- 是数词「一」的来源；确切形式与更早的来源都不确定。

items.en: The reconstructed Germanic numeral *ainaz meant one and yielded Old English ān, Old Frisian ēn and Old High German ein.
items.cn: 重构的原始日耳曼语数词 *ainaz 意为「一」，演变为古英语 ān、古弗里斯兰语 ēn 与古高地德语 ein。

items.en: Ān was the ordinary numeral and could already stand before a noun with an indefinite force; in unstressed positions it was shortened.
items.cn: ān 是常用的数词，并且已经能放在名词前表示不定指；在非重读位置上它会被缩短。

items.en: Before a consonant the final -n dropped and the weak form a remained; before a vowel the n was kept as an, so that two vowels did not collide.
items.cn: 在辅音音素之前，词尾 -n 脱落，只剩弱读形式 a；在元音音素之前则保留 n 写作 an，以免两个元音撞在一起。

items.en: The choice between a and an is fixed by sound rather than spelling, so we write an hour but a university. The precise first date of the article is uncertain.
items.cn: 现代英语中 a 与 an 的取舍由读音而非拼写决定，所以写 an hour 却写 a university。这个冠词最早出现的确切年代不确定。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the grammatical words that grew from the same Old English numeral; the near-meaning group gathers determiners that answer the same question about how much or which.
note.cn: 形近组收的是从同一个古英语数词长出来的语法词；近义组收的是回答「多少」或「哪一个」这类相同问题的限定词。

entries.definition: The same indefinite article in its vowel-preceding shape, keeping the old final -n of ān.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个不定冠词在元音音素前的写法，保留了古英语 ān 的词尾 -n。

entries.definition: The full numeral that the article was cut down from; it still counts and can be stressed.
entries.definitionCN: 冠词由它削减而来的完整数词，仍能计数，也能重读。

entries.definition: A determiner from Old English ǣnig, built on the same numeral and meaning one or some, no matter which.
entries.definitionCN: 限定词，来自古英语 ǣnig，由同一个数词构成，义为「任何一个；一些」。

entries.definition: An adverb from the old genitive of one, meaning one time.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，来自 one 的古老属格形式，义为「一次」。

entries.definition: The definite article, used when the listener can already identify the thing; the direct opposite of the indefinite choice.
entries.definitionCN: 定冠词，用于听者已经能够确定所指事物之时，正是不定指的对立面。

entries.definition: A determiner for an unspecified amount, used with plurals and uncountable nouns where a cannot go.
entries.definitionCN: 限定词，表示不确定的数量，用于复数和不可数名词，而这些位置不能用 a。

entries.definition: A determiner that picks out every member one by one, close to the per sense of a in rates.
entries.definitionCN: 限定词，逐个点出每一个成员，与 a 在频率表达中的「每一」义相近。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English numeral, the sound rule and the fixed phrases the article actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的古英语数词、读音规则，以及这个冠词实际出现的固定搭配。

normal.en: Old English ān meant one; a is simply ān with the final n worn off before a consonant.
normal.cn: 古英语 ān 意为「一」；a 就是 ān 在辅音前磨掉词尾 n 的结果。

normal.en: The n survives before a vowel sound: an apple, an hour, an idea.
normal.cn: 在元音音素前 n 会保留下来：an apple、an hour、an idea。

normal.en: Twice a week keeps the old counting: one week for each visit.
normal.cn: twice a week 保留了古老的计数方式：一次探望对一个星期。

normal.en: A few, a little and a lot of are frozen chunks; the article is part of the phrase, not a separate choice.
normal.cn: a few、a little、a lot of 都是凝固的短语块，冠词是短语的一部分，不能单独替换。

normal.en: A Mr Smith means someone called Smith whom you do not know.
normal.cn: a Mr Smith 意为「一位叫史密斯的先生」，而你不认识他。

abstract.en: Picture one raised finger in front of a long shelf: one thing is chosen, the rest stay unnamed.
abstract.cn: 想象在一长排货架前竖起一根手指：只点中一个，其余都不点名。

abstract.en: The letter is a single stroke, and the word means a single item; one mark, one thing.
abstract.cn: 这个字母只有一笔，这个词只指一件东西：一笔，一个。

abstract.en: Add the n and a vowel can follow safely; the little consonant is a bridge between two sounds.
abstract.cn: 加上 n，后面就能安全地接元音；这个小辅音是两个音之间的桥。

examples.en: I need a break before we keep going.
examples.cn: 我们接着走之前，我需要歇一会儿。

examples.en: She works as a teacher in a small town.
examples.cn: 她在一个小镇上当老师。

examples.en: We meet once a week to catch up.
examples.cn: 我们每周见一次，聊聊近况。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「呃」——开口先呃一声，再伸出一根手指：一个，就是它。

root: 源自古英语数词 ān「一」。在辅音音素前，非重读形式脱落词尾 -n 成为 a；在元音音素前保留 -n 成为 an。它与 one、an、any 同源，来自原始日耳曼语重构形式 *ainaz，更早一般认为可追溯到原始印欧语 *oi-no-。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses apply one and the same move: a single item is pointed at, and what changes is how much the speaker says about it, from a stranger in the yard to a rate per week.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在做同一个动作：点出单独一个；变化的只是说话人把这个「一」用在哪里，从院子里的陌生人，到每周一次的频率。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one finger points at a single item in a long row, and the others stay in the background.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根手指点向一长排东西里的某一个，其余的留在背景里。

branches.en: THE UNKNOWN ONE: a thing or a person is singled out but not identified, so the listener learns only that it exists.
branches.cn: 未知线：点出了某个东西或某个人，却说不清是哪一个，听者只知道它存在。

branches.en: THE NUMBER: the old numeral one still shows before units and inside quantity phrases.
branches.cn: 数目线：古老的数词「一」仍在单位前和数量短语里显形。

branches.en: THE RATE: one item is counted against each unit of time or distance, which reads as per.
branches.cn: 比率线：拿一个去对每一个时间或距离单位，读起来就是「每」。

branches.en: THE CLASS: one example is made to stand for a whole type, as in a kind of.
branches.cn: 类别线：让一个例子代表整个类型，如 a kind of。

branches.en: THE FRAME: jobs and set phrases use the bare article as a slot, and negation uses it as the smallest possible amount.
branches.cn: 框架线：职业与固定短语把冠词当作一个必填的位置，否定句则把它当作最小的一份。

intro.en: This entry is a whole grammatical word rather than a stem, so the items below are the small forms it lives among: its own two shapes, its definite partner, and the look-alike prefixes and endings.
intro.cn: 这个词本身就是一个完整的语法词，而不是词根，所以下面列的是它身边的那些小单位：它的两种写法、它的定冠词伙伴，以及形近的前缀与词尾。

latinIntro.en: The indefinite article is Germanic in origin and has no Latin ancestor, so no Latin entries are listed here.
latinIntro.cn: 这个不定冠词源自日耳曼语，没有拉丁语来源，所以这里不列拉丁语条目。

items.example: She wants a cup of tea.
items.exampleCN: 她想要一杯茶。

items.meaning: a, used before a vowel sound
items.meaningCN: 元音音素前使用的变体
items.example: He ate an apple on the way.
items.exampleCN: 他在路上吃了一个苹果。

items.meaning: the known or already mentioned one
items.meaningCN: 定冠词：已知或已提到的那个
items.example: The cup on the desk is mine.
items.exampleCN: 桌上那只杯子是我的。

items.example: One of the windows is open.
items.exampleCN: 其中一扇窗是开着的。

items.meaning: one or some, no matter which
items.exampleCN: 你有什么问题吗？
atypical 意为「非典型的」。

items.meaning: on, in, in a state of
items.meaningCN: 古英语前缀：在……之上；处于……状态
items.example: Asleep means in a state of sleep.
items.exampleCN: asleep 意为「处于睡眠状态」。

items.meaning: plural ending of Latin and Greek nouns
items.meaningCN: 拉丁语与希腊语名词的复数词尾
items.example: The plural of datum is data.
items.exampleCN: datum 的复数形式是 data。

items.meaning: noun-forming ending from Latin and Greek
items.meaningCN: 源自拉丁语与希腊语的名词词尾
items.example: Idea reached English from Greek through Latin.
items.exampleCN: idea 经拉丁语从希腊语进入英语。

definition_zh: 放弃；抛弃；遗弃；丢弃；离弃；放任、纵情
definition_en: to leave a person, place or thing behind for good, or to stop doing something before it is finished
core_image: 摊开的手掌：原本握着的东西被松开，留在身后
scene: 洪水退去，救援队发现那辆旧卡车陷在泥里，怎么也拖不动。They had to abandon the truck in the mud and walk to the village.
sceneCN: 这里 abandon 是「丢下、弃置」（第 1 个义项：把带不走的东西留在原地）；句意为他们只好把那辆卡车丢在泥里，步行去村里。

pos.zh: 及物动词：放弃；抛弃；遗弃；丢弃；放任、纵情
名词（多用于短语 with abandon）：放纵；尽情

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「放弃；遗弃；弃置」
由本词加 -ed 构成的形容词，义为「被遗弃的；荒废的；放纵的」
由本词与 ware 复合而成，指作者已停止维护、无人负责的软件

senses.title: To leave a place or thing behind
senses.definition: to leave a place, vehicle or object behind because you can no longer keep it or take it with you
senses.definitionCN: 因无法继续保有或带走，而把地方、车辆或物件留在原地
senses.example: They had to abandon the truck in the mud.
senses.exampleCN: 他们只好把那辆卡车丢在泥里。
senses.why: Old French a bandon meant 'into someone's power': to abandon is first to hand a thing over and let go of it.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 a bandon 意为「交到别人的支配之下」：abandon 最初就是把东西交出去、松开手，于是有了「丢下不管」。

senses.title: To desert a person in your care
senses.definition: to leave a person or animal that depends on you, especially when you have a duty to stay
senses.definitionCN: 离开依赖自己的人或动物，尤指在本该留下尽责的时候
senses.example: The family abandoned the puppy when they moved away.
senses.exampleCN: 那家人搬走时把小狗遗弃了。
senses.why: The same letting-go turns cruel when the thing released is a living creature that cannot follow you.
senses.whyCN: 当被放开的是一个跟不上你的活物时，同一种「松手」就变成了残忍的遗弃。

senses.title: To stop doing something unfinished
senses.definition: to give up an activity, plan or piece of work before it is complete
senses.definitionCN: 在一项活动、计划或工作完成之前就停止不做
senses.example: The company abandoned the new railway line after two years.
senses.exampleCN: 两年后，公司放弃了那条新铁路线。
senses.why: A project is held in the hand like an object; abandoning it means opening the hand before the work is done.
senses.whyCN: 项目就像握在手里的物件；abandon 就是活还没干完就先松了手，所以有「中途放弃」。

senses.title: To give up a claim or belief
senses.definition: to relinquish a right, claim, demand or belief and stop asserting it
senses.definitionCN: 交出手中的权利、要求、主张或信念，不再坚持
senses.example: She abandoned her claim to the family land.
senses.exampleCN: 她放弃了对家族土地的主张。
senses.why: A claim is something you hold against others; letting go of it is the same release, now in law and argument.
senses.whyCN: 主张是你用来对抗别人的凭据；松开它仍是同一个「放手」动作，只是发生在法律与争论里。

senses.title: To withdraw from a match or race
senses.definition: to withdraw from a game, race or contest before it finishes, often because of weather or injury
senses.definitionCN: 因天气、伤病等原因，在比赛结束前退出竞赛
senses.example: The referee abandoned the match after the storm began.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨开始后，裁判中止了比赛。
senses.why: When the contest can no longer be carried on, the officials let the whole thing go, which is abandoning it.
senses.whyCN: 比赛已经无法继续进行时，裁判把整场比赛放开不管，这就是 abandon 用于「中止、退出」的来路。

senses.title: To give yourself over to a feeling
senses.definition: in abandon oneself to, to stop resisting an emotion or pleasure and let it take over
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 abandon oneself to，指不再抗拒某种情绪或享乐，任其支配自己
senses.example: For one evening they abandoned themselves to the music.
senses.exampleCN: 那一晚他们纵情于音乐之中。
senses.why: Here the thing released is the self: you hand your own control over to the feeling, so the old 'give over' sense turns inward.
senses.whyCN: 这里被放开的是「自己」：你把自控权交给某种感受，于是「交出」的旧义转向了内部，成了沉溺。

senses.title: With abandon: without restraint
senses.definition: in the phrase with abandon, in a free and uninhibited way, with no attempt to hold back
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 with abandon，指自由自在、毫不克制地做某事
senses.example: The children ran through the sprinklers with abandon.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们毫无顾忌地在喷水器间奔跑。
senses.why: The noun keeps the state produced by letting go: once restraint is released, what is left is abandon itself.
senses.whyCN: 名词保留了「松手」之后的状态：约束一放开，剩下的就是 abandon 本身，即尽情与无所顾忌。

senses.title: Abandon ship: to leave a sinking vessel
senses.definition: in the order abandon ship, to leave a vessel that is sinking or in danger, and by extension to quit a failing enterprise
senses.definitionCN: 用于口令 abandon ship，指离开正在下沉或遇险的船，引申为退出失败的事业
senses.example: The captain gave the order to abandon ship at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 船长在黎明时下令弃船。
senses.why: The most concrete case of leaving something behind is stepping off a ship that can no longer carry you.
senses.whyCN: 「丢下东西」最具体的情形，就是从一艘已经载不动你的船上走下来，这就是弃船。

intro.en: Abandon reached English from Old French, and behind the French word lies a Germanic word for a proclamation or command.
intro.cn: abandon 经古法语进入英语，古法语这个词的背后是一个表示「公告、命令」的日耳曼词。

items.en: The reconstructed Frankish form *bann meant 'a proclamation, a command'; its deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 重构的法兰克语形式 *bann 意为「公告、命令」，更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Medieval Latin bannum recorded the same word as 'proclamation, ban, jurisdiction', and it also produced the verb bannire.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 bannum 记录的是同一个词，义为「公告、禁令、管辖」，并生出动词 bannire。

items.en: Old French bandon meant 'power, control'; the phrase a bandon meant 'at someone's disposal, in someone's power'.
items.cn: 古法语 bandon 意为「权力、支配」；短语 a bandon 意为「听凭某人处置、在某人掌握之中」。

items.en: From mettre a bandon, 'to put at someone's disposal', came abandonner, 'to give over, surrender, desert'.
items.cn: 由 mettre a bandon「置于他人支配之下」产生了 abandonner，意为「交出、让与、抛弃」。

items.en: English took the verb in the late fourteenth century; the noun sense of free, unrestrained behaviour is much later.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪后期借入这个动词；名词「放纵、尽情」的用法要晚得多。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the derived forms and the old Germanic relatives; the near-meaning group holds verbs of leaving, quitting and giving up.
note.cn: 形近组收本词的派生形式与古老的日耳曼同源词；近义组收表示离开、停止与放弃的动词。

entries.definition: the act of leaving something or someone behind, or the state of being left.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「放弃、遗弃、弃置」，指丢下某人某物的行为或状态。

entries.definition: left empty or uncared for, or given over to vice.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「被遗弃的、荒废的」，也可指「自甘堕落的」。

entries.definition: An official prohibition, from the same Germanic word for a proclamation.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「禁令、禁止」，与 bandon 同出「公告」这一日耳曼词。

entries.definition: The public announcement of an intended marriage, read in church.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「结婚公告」，教堂里公开宣读，与 abandon 同源。

entries.definition: Software that its owner no longer sells or maintains but that is still passed around.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指作者已停止销售与维护、却仍在流传的软件。

entries.definition: To leave a person or place, especially in a way that breaks a duty.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「遗弃、弃守」，强调背弃责任，语气比 abandon 更重。

entries.definition: To give up or leave someone or something entirely; old and literary in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「抛弃、舍弃」，语气古雅，多用于书面与文学。

entries.definition: To give up a right, position or control, usually willingly and formally.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「放弃（权利、职位、控制）」，多指自愿而正式地交出。

entries.definition: To stop doing something or leave a job; plainer and less dramatic than abandon.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「停止、辞去」，口语色彩强，不似 abandon 那样带决绝意味。

entries.definition: To stop trying or stop doing something; the everyday equivalent of abandon.
entries.definitionCN: 短语动词，义为「放弃、不再尝试」，是 abandon 最日常的说法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old French phrase, the Germanic relatives and the fixed phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的古法语短语、日耳曼同源词，以及这个词实际出现的固定搭配。

normal.en: Bandon meant control: a bandon was 'at someone's disposal', and abandonner was to hand it over.
normal.cn: bandon 意为「支配」：a bandon 就是「听凭处置」，abandonner 就是把它交出去。

normal.en: The same Germanic word gives ban and banns, both about public announcement.
normal.cn: 同一个日耳曼词还给出 ban 与 banns，两者都与公开宣告有关。

normal.en: Abandon ship is the order to step off a vessel that can no longer carry you.
normal.cn: abandon ship 是让人离开一艘已经载不动自己的船的口令。

normal.en: Abandon oneself to music is to hand control over to the music.
normal.cn: abandon oneself to music 就是把控制权交给音乐。

normal.en: With abandon keeps the noun: restraint is gone, and what remains is the letting go.
normal.cn: with abandon 保留了名词用法：约束消失，剩下的正是那份「放开」。

abstract.en: Picture open hands: nothing is taken away, everything is simply no longer held.
abstract.cn: 想象摊开的手掌：东西没有被拿走，只是不再被握住。

abstract.en: The road continues after you stop walking; abandoning is your stopping, not the road ending.
abstract.cn: 你停下脚步之后路还在延伸；放弃是你停步，不是路到了尽头。

abstract.en: The same release can be cruelty, surrender or freedom, depending on what is left behind.
abstract.cn: 同一次松手可以是残忍、是屈服，也可以是自由，取决于被留下的是什么。

examples.en: They had to abandon the truck in the mud.
examples.cn: 他们只好把那辆卡车丢在泥里。

examples.en: She abandoned her plan to study abroad.
examples.cn: 她放弃了出国留学的计划。

examples.en: The children ran through the sprinklers with abandon.
examples.cn: 孩子们毫无顾忌地在喷水器间奔跑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿班等」——班车左等右等不来，索性把行李一丢走人：放弃、抛弃。

root: 古法语 a bandon（听凭处置）衍生出 abandonner（交出、抛弃），再进入英语；bandon 源自法兰克语 *bann「公告、命令」，与英语 ban、banns 同源。把 abandon 拆成 a + ban + don（给予）是后人附会，并非真实词源。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense of abandon is one action of letting go; what changes is the object released: a thing, a person, a task, a claim, a match, the self, or a ship.
sensesIntro.cn: abandon 的每个义项都是同一次「松手」，变的只是被放开的对象：物件、人、任务、权利、比赛、自己，或一艘船。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pair of open hands, and what was held is left behind.
core.cn: 核心意象：摊开的双手，原本握着的东西被留在身后。

branches.en: THINGS AND SHIPS: what cannot be carried is left where it stands.
branches.cn: 物件与船线：带不走的东西就留在原地。

branches.en: PEOPLE: the same release becomes cruel when the one left behind depends on you.
branches.cn: 人物线：当被留下的人依赖你时，同一次松手就成了残忍。

branches.en: TASKS: the hand opens before the work or the contest is finished.
branches.cn: 任务线：活或比赛还没结束，手就先松开了。

branches.en: CLAIMS: a right or belief is handed over and no longer asserted.
branches.cn: 权利线：权利或信念被交出去，不再主张。

branches.en: THE SELF: control is given to a feeling, and the leftover state is called abandon.
branches.cn: 自我线：把控制权交给某种感受，剩下的状态就叫 abandon。

intro.en: Abandon is an Old French verb built from a preposition and a noun, and English adds its ordinary suffixes to make the family.
intro.cn: abandon 是由介词与名词构成的古法语动词，英语再加上普通后缀扩展出这一词族。

latinIntro.en: The base noun is Germanic in origin but was recorded in Medieval Latin as bannum, so the Latin entries below are medieval and not classical.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词根名词源自日耳曼语，但以 bannum 的形式见于中世纪拉丁语，所以下面列的是中世纪拉丁语而非古典拉丁语。

items.example: a bandon meant at someone's disposal.
items.exampleCN: a bandon 意为听凭某人处置。

items.example: Bandon gave the verb its idea of handing over.
items.exampleCN: bandon 赋予这个动词「交出」的含义。
它构成 abandonner。
它构成 abandonment。
它构成 abandoned。
它构成 abandoning。

items.example: A ban is a public order not to do something.
items.exampleCN: ban 就是公开禁止做某事的命令。

items.example: The banns were read on three Sundays.
items.exampleCN: 结婚公告在三个星期日宣读。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「放弃；遗弃；弃置」
由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「被遗弃的；荒废的；放纵的」
由本词与 ware 复合而成，指无人维护却仍在流传的软件

definition_zh: 能力；才能；本领；行为能力
definition_en: the power or skill needed to do something, or a particular talent that a person has
core_image: 一只手稳稳握住重物，把它举了起来
scene: 面试官问她会不会用那套旧软件，她当场演示了一遍。She proved her ability to handle the job within ten minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 ability 是「做某事的能力」（第 1 个义项：完成某事的实际本领）；句意为她十分钟内就证明了自己胜任这份工作的能力。

pos.zh: 名词：能力；才能；本领；行为能力

collocations.phrase: to the best of one's ability

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 habilis 经古法语进入英语，义为「能够的；有能力的」
由 able 加 -ly 构成，义为「能干地；出色地」
由前缀 en- 加 able 构成，义为「使能够；使成为可能」
由前缀 dis- 加 able 构成，义为「使失去能力；使残废」

senses.title: The power to do something
senses.definition: the physical or mental power needed to carry out a particular action or task
senses.definitionCN: 完成某一动作或任务所需的体力或脑力
senses.example: She proved her ability to handle the job within ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 她十分钟内就证明了自己胜任这份工作的能力。
senses.why: Latin habere is 'to hold': ability is the grip that lets a person hold a task and carry it through.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 habere 意为「握住」：ability 就是让人握住一件任务并把它做完的那股握力。

senses.title: A particular talent or skill
senses.definition: a specific skill or talent, especially one that can be named and developed, often used in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 一项具体、可命名也可培养的技能或天赋，常用复数 abilities
senses.example: The course develops the student's musical abilities.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课程培养学生的音乐才能。
senses.why: The single grip can be counted one by one: each thing a person can hold well becomes a separate ability.
senses.whyCN: 这股握力可以被一项项数出来：每一样握得好的东西，就成了一种单独的 ability。

senses.title: Mental capacity to understand
senses.definition: the mental power to understand, reason or learn, especially when compared with others
senses.definitionCN: 理解、推理或学习的心智力量，尤用于与他人比较时
senses.example: The test measures the ability to reason with numbers.
senses.exampleCN: 这项测试测量用数字推理的能力。
senses.why: If ability is a grip, the mind's grip is what holds an idea long enough to work with it.
senses.whyCN: 如果 ability 是一种握力，那么心智的握力就是能把一个想法握住、久到可以摆弄它的力量。

senses.title: Physical capacity
senses.definition: the bodily power to move, endure or perform, as in the ability to walk or to lift
senses.definitionCN: 身体移动、承受或完成动作的力量，如行走或举起的能力
senses.example: The injury affected his ability to walk without pain.
senses.exampleCN: 这处伤影响了他无痛行走的能力。
senses.why: The most literal grip is the body's own: muscles closing on a weight and holding it up.
senses.whyCN: 最字面的握力来自身体本身：肌肉扣住重物并把它举住。

senses.title: Legal capacity to act
senses.definition: in law, the recognized capacity of a person or body to perform a valid act, such as making a contract
senses.definitionCN: 法律上指个人或机构作出有效行为（如订立合同）的资格
senses.example: The court questioned his legal ability to sign the agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 法院质疑他签署该协议的法律行为能力。
senses.why: Law borrows the grip and asks a narrower question: is this person allowed to hold this power at all?
senses.whyCN: 法律借用了这股握力，却问得更窄：这个人究竟有没有资格握住这项权力？

senses.title: To the best of one's ability
senses.definition: in the phrase to the best of one's ability, as well as one is able, with full effort and no holding back
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语「to the best of one's ability」，指尽最大努力、毫不保留地去做
senses.example: He answered every question to the best of his ability.
senses.exampleCN: 他尽自己所能回答了每一个问题。
senses.why: The phrase sets the limit of the grip: you use it up to its edge, and no further.
senses.whyCN: 这个说法给握力标出了边界：你把它用到最边上，再往外就没有了。

senses.title: Ability to pay in law and finance
senses.definition: in law and economics, the financial capacity of a person or company to meet a cost, debt or tax
senses.definitionCN: 法律与经济用语，指个人或公司承担费用、债务或税款的经济能力
senses.example: The fine was set according to the company's ability to pay.
senses.exampleCN: 罚款是按这家公司的支付能力确定的。
senses.why: Money is also something held in the hand; the phrase asks whether the hand is large enough for the bill.
senses.whyCN: 钱同样是握在手里的东西；这个说法问的是那只手够不够大，能不能接住这笔账。

senses.title: Mixed ability in teaching
senses.titleCN: 学生能力参差（教学术语）
senses.definition: in education, the phrase mixed ability describes a class in which students differ widely in skill level
senses.definitionCN: 教育术语，短语 mixed ability 指班内学生水平差距很大的编班方式
senses.example: She teaches a mixed ability class of thirty children.
senses.exampleCN: 她教一个三十名儿童、水平参差的班级。
senses.why: Once ability can be counted, it can also be spread unevenly, and schools need a word for the mixture.
senses.whyCN: 既然能力可以被数出来，它也就分布得不均匀，学校于是需要一个词来描述这种混合。

intro.en: Ability comes from a Latin verb meaning to hold, through the adjective habilis and its noun habilitas.
intro.cn: ability 出自一个意为「握住」的拉丁动词，中间经过形容词 habilis 与名词 habilitas。

items.en: Habere meant 'to hold, have, keep'; it is generally traced to a reconstructed Indo-European root for taking or holding.
items.cn: habere 意为「握住、拥有、保持」；一般认为它可追溯到重构的原始印欧语词根，表示「拿、握」。

items.en: The adjective habilis meant 'easy to hold, handy, fit, capable'.
items.cn: 形容词 habilis 意为「好握的、顺手的、合适的、能干的」。

items.en: The noun habilitas, 'fitness, capacity, ability', was formed from habilis with the noun suffix -itas.
items.cn: 名词 habilitas 由 habilis 加名词后缀 -itas 构成，义为「合适、能力、才干」。

items.en: Old French took habilis as able, 'fit, capable'; the noun recorded for English is usually given as ablete.
items.cn: 古法语把 habilis 借作 able，义为「合适的、能干的」；英语名词所据的古法语形式一般写作 ablete。

items.en: English has the noun from the late fourteenth century, alongside the adjective able.
items.cn: 英语自十四世纪后期起有这个名词，同时也有形容词 able。

note.en: The look-alike group is the able family from the same Latin root; the near-meaning group gathers words for capacity, skill and talent.
note.cn: 形近组是同一拉丁词根下的 able 词族；近义组收表示能力、技能与天赋的词。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning capable of doing something.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「能够的、有能力的」，与 ability 同根。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning in a capable or skilled way.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「能干地、出色地」。

entries.definition: To make someone or something able to do something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使能够、使成为可能」，由 en- 加 able 构成。

entries.definition: To take away the power to act, or to turn a function off.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使失去能力、使失效」，由 dis- 加 able 构成。

entries.definition: The power or potential to do something, often of a system, team or person over time.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「能力、潜力」，常指系统、团队或个人长期具备的条件。

entries.definition: The maximum amount something can hold, or a person's power to do or understand.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「容量；能力」，强调可容纳或可承受的上限。

entries.definition: A learned ability to do something well, usually through practice.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「技能、技巧」，强调经练习获得的熟练本领。

entries.definition: A natural ability, especially an artistic or special one, rather than a learned skill.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「天赋、才干」，多指天生而非练成的本领。

entries.definition: The ability to do a job well enough to a required standard.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「胜任能力」，指达到工作要求的标准。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root habere, the able family and the phrases the noun actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用真实的拉丁词根 habere、able 词族，以及这个名词实际出现的固定说法。

normal.en: Habere means to hold: ability is how well you can hold a task.
normal.cn: habere 意为「握住」：ability 就是你握住一件任务的本事。

normal.en: Able is the adjective, ably the adverb, and ability the noun.
normal.cn: able 是形容词，ably 是副词，ability 是名词。

normal.en: Abilities in the plural names one skill after another.
normal.cn: 复数的 abilities 指的是一项又一项具体的本领。

normal.en: To the best of one's ability means using the grip right up to its edge.
normal.cn: 「to the best of one's ability」意为把这份握力用到最边上。

normal.en: Ability to pay asks whether the hand is big enough for the bill.
normal.cn: ability to pay 问的是那只手够不够大，接不接得住这笔账。

abstract.en: What can be held can be done; the grip comes before the result.
abstract.cn: 握得住，才做得到；握力先于结果。

abstract.en: Ability is invisible until something is actually lifted.
abstract.cn: 能力看不见，直到有东西真的被举起来。

abstract.en: A talent unused is a hand that slowly loses its strength.
abstract.cn: 不用的才能，就像一只手慢慢失去力气。

examples.en: She proved her ability to handle the job within ten minutes.
examples.cn: 她十分钟内就证明了自己胜任这份工作的能力。

examples.en: He has the ability to make people laugh.
examples.cn: 他有逗人发笑的本事。

examples.en: Students of mixed ability work in the same class.
examples.cn: 水平参差的学生在同一个班里学习。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额比勒提」——手比一比，勒紧一提，重物起来了：能力、才能。

root: 拉丁语 habilitas「能力」来自 habilis「能干的、顺手的」，habilis 又来自 habere「握住、拥有」；一般认为更早可追溯到重构的原始印欧语词根，表示「拿、握」。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense of ability is a grip: on a task, on a skill, on an idea, on a weight, on a legal power, on a bill, or on the limit of one's own strength.
sensesIntro.cn: ability 的每个义项都是一次「握住」：握住任务、握住一项技能、握住一个想法、握住重物、握住法律上的权力、握住一笔账，或握住自己力气的那条边界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand closes firmly on a heavy thing and lifts it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手稳稳握住重物，把它举起来。

branches.en: THE GENERAL GRIP: the power to do a particular thing.
branches.cn: 一般能力线：做成某件事的那股力量。

branches.en: COUNTED SKILLS: each thing held well becomes a separate ability.
branches.cn: 可数才能线：每一样握得好的东西，都成为一项单独的才能。

branches.en: MIND AND BODY: the same grip works on ideas and on weights.
branches.cn: 心智与身体线：同一股握力既作用于想法，也作用于重物。

branches.en: LAW: the grip is recognised or refused by the court.
branches.cn: 法律线：这股握力由法庭来承认或否认。

branches.en: FIXED PHRASES: the grip is measured at its edge, in money, or across a class.
branches.cn: 固定说法线：握力被量到边界，或量成钱，或量成一个班里的差异。

intro.en: Ability is a Latin adjective turned into a noun, and English builds the same family again with able, ably, enable and disable.
intro.cn: ability 是由拉丁形容词变来的名词，英语又用 able、ably、enable、disable 把同一词族重建了一遍。

latinIntro.en: Habere, habilis and habilitas are all recorded Latin; the Indo-European layer behind them is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: habere、habilis 与 habilitas 都是有记录的拉丁语，它们背后的印欧语层面属于重构。

items.example: Habere is the holding verb behind the family.
items.exampleCN: habere 是这个词族背后的「握住」动词。
它构成 habilis。

items.example: Habilis is the adjective of fitness.
items.exampleCN: habilis 是表示「合适、能干」的形容词。
它构成 habilitas。

items.example: Habilitas is the direct Latin source of the noun.

senses.title: Skilled and competent
senses.definition: of a person, having good skills or judgement and doing a task well
senses.definitionCN: 指人技能或判断力好，能把事情做好
senses.example: She is an able teacher who can reach even the quietest students.
senses.exampleCN: 她是一位能干的教师，连最沉默的学生也能带动。
senses.why: The Latin source habilis meant easy to handle and apt; a person described this way is one who can be relied on to handle things.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 habilis 本义是「易于掌控的、合适的」；用来说人，就是遇事拿得住、靠得住的能者。

senses.title: Be able to: manage on an occasion
senses.definition: in the phrase be able to, to have the power or chance to do something on a particular occasion
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 be able to，指在某一具体场合有力量或机会做到某事
senses.example: We were able to catch the last train home.
senses.exampleCN: 我们赶上了回家的末班车。
senses.why: The adjective joins the verb be to name the power a person actually has at a given moment, which is why it replaces can in future and perfect forms.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词与 be 连用，指某人在某一刻实际握有的能力；正因如此，将来时与完成时里常用 be able to 代替 can。

senses.title: Having the money or means
senses.definition: having enough money, time or other resources to do something
senses.definitionCN: 有足够的钱、时间或其他资源去做某事
senses.example: After the rent went up, they were no longer able to afford a car.
senses.exampleCN: 房租上涨后，他们再也负担不起一辆车。
senses.why: Power to act is not only strength of body or mind; money and time are also things one can hold and use, so able extends to resources.
senses.whyCN: 行动的力量不只来自体力或脑力；钱和时间同样是能握在手里动用的东西，于是 able 也扩展到「有财力、有办法」。

senses.title: Legally competent
senses.definition: in law, having the mental or legal capacity to do something such as stand trial or sign a contract
senses.definitionCN: 在法律上具备做某事的心智或法定能力，如受审或签约
senses.example: The judge ruled that the defendant was able to stand trial.
senses.exampleCN: 法官裁定被告有能力接受审判。
senses.why: Law asks whether a person can be held responsible; the same word for practical power becomes a test of legal capacity.
senses.whyCN: 法律要问的是一个人能否承担责任；同一个表示实际能力的词，就变成了对法定行为能力的判定。

senses.title: Physically fit and sound
senses.definition: healthy and physically strong, especially in the fixed phrase able-bodied
senses.definitionCN: 健康且体格强壮，尤用于固定说法 able-bodied
senses.example: The crew carried the injured passengers while the able-bodied rowed.
senses.exampleCN: 船员抬着受伤的乘客，体格健全的人则划桨。
senses.why: A body that can answer the demands put on it is literally able; the compound able-bodied keeps this physical sense alive.
senses.whyCN: 能回应要求的身体就是字面意义上的 able；复合词 able-bodied 让这个身体义一直活着。

senses.title: Able seaman: a qualified sailor
senses.definition: in the phrase able seaman, a sailor certified as fully trained and fit for duty
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 able seaman，指经认证训练完备、能胜任船上工作的水手
senses.example: He spent three years as an able seaman before he was made a mate.
senses.exampleCN: 他当了三年的合格水手才被提升为大副。
senses.why: Naval rank borrowed the everyday sense of competent: a sailor rated able was one judged fit to handle the ship.
senses.whyCN: 海军军衔借用了日常语里「合格、能干」的意思：被评为 able 的水手，就是被认定能胜任船上工作的人。

senses.title: The suffix -able: that can be
senses.definition: as a suffix, forming adjectives that mean that can be done or is worth doing, as in readable or washable
senses.definitionCN: 作后缀，构成表示「可以被……的」或「值得……的」形容词，如 readable、washable
senses.example: The old label was barely readable after years in the sun.
senses.exampleCN: 那块旧标签在阳光下晒了多年，几乎看不清了。
senses.why: The Latin ending -abilis grew out of habilis, so suffix and adjective share one root: what can be handled can also be done.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语词尾 -abilis 正是从 habilis 长出来的，所以后缀与形容词同出一根：能被掌控的东西，也就能被做成。

senses.title: More than able to: fully capable
senses.definition: in the phrase more than able to, having far more skill or strength than a task requires
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 more than able to，指技能或力量远超任务所需
senses.example: With ten years on the ward, she is more than able to handle a night shift alone.
senses.exampleCN: 在病房干了十年，她完全能独自应付一个夜班。
senses.why: If able means having enough power, more than able says the power exceeds the need, and the comparison measures ability like a quantity.
senses.whyCN: 如果 able 是有足够的力量，more than able 就是说力量超出了所需；比较结构把能力当成一种可以称量的东西。

intro.en: Able is a Latin adjective that reached English through Old French and then turned into one of the most productive suffixes in the language.
intro.cn: able 是一个经由古法语进入英语的拉丁形容词，后来还变成英语里最能产的构词成分之一。

items.en: habere meant to hold, have or keep. It is the source of habit, exhibit and inhibit as well as of the adjective below.
items.cn: habere 意为「握住、拥有、保有」，它生出 habit、exhibit、inhibit，也生出下面的形容词。

items.en: habilis, formed from habere, meant that can be held, easy to handle, apt, fit. The recorded form is certain; the step from easy to handle to skilful is a matter of interpretation.
items.cn: habilis 由 habere 构成，意为「可以被握住的、易于掌控的、合适的」。词形有文献可证；从「好掌控」到「能干」的引申过程属于解释。

items.en: Old French (h)able is recorded from the twelfth century with the sense capable, fit. Whether English took the word straight from Latin or through French is debated, though the French route is usually assumed.
items.cn: 古法语 (h)able 自十二世纪起有记录，意为「有能力的、合适的」。英语是直接取自拉丁语还是经由法语，学界有争论，一般假定走法语一路。

items.en: English has able from the fourteenth century. The ending -able was soon detached from such words and used to build new adjectives on English verbs.
items.cn: 英语自十四世纪起有 able。词尾 -able 很快从这类词上脱落下来，用来给英语动词造新形容词。

items.en: Nautical and legal uses such as able seaman and able to stand trial grew beside the everyday sense, and be able to became the standard substitute for can.
items.cn: able seaman、able to stand trial 这类航海与法律用法在日常义旁生长，be able to 则成了 can 的标准替代表达。

note.en: The first group is the family built on Latin habere; the second group holds words for skill and capability.
note.cn: 第一组是建立在拉丁语 habere 之上的同族词；第二组收录表示技能与能力的近义词。

entries.definition: The noun for the power or skill to do something, from Latin habilitas.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「能力、本领」，来自拉丁语 habilitas。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to make someone or something able to do something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使能够、使成为可能」，由 en- 加本词构成。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to take away the power to act, often through injury or by design.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使失去能力、使残废」，常指因伤或设计而失去功能。

entries.definition: The negative adjective: not having the power or chance to do something.
entries.definitionCN: 否定形容词，义为「不能的、不会的」，指没有能力或机会做某事。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning in a skilful, competent way.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「能干地、出色地」。

entries.definition: Able to do something, often with the sense of having the necessary qualities; slightly more formal.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有能力的、能胜任的」，强调具备必要素质，语气略正式。

entries.definition: Having enough skill for a task, but not necessarily outstanding.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有能力胜任的、合格的」，只强调够用，不一定出众。

entries.definition: Trained and experienced in a particular job or activity.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「熟练的、有技能的」，强调受过训练并有经验。

entries.definition: Having passed the training or gained the official right to do a job.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有资格的、合格的」，强调通过培训或取得正式资格。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁词根，以及这个词实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: habere is to hold: able is first what can be held in the hand, and then what a person can handle.
normal.cn: habere 是「握住」：able 先是能握在手里的东西，然后是人能拿得住的事。

normal.en: The same root gives ability, enable and disable, so the whole family circles the idea of power to act.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 ability、enable、disable，整个词族都围绕「行动之力」。

normal.en: Be able to is the form English uses for can in the future and the perfect: will be able to, has been able to.
normal.cn: be able to 是英语在将来时和完成时里替代 can 的形式：will be able to、has been able to。

normal.en: Able seaman is a real naval rating, not a compliment; the word once meant fit for duty.
normal.cn: able seaman 是真实的海军等级，不是一句夸奖；这个词曾经就指「胜任职务」。

normal.en: Any verb plus -able makes that can be done: readable, washable, breakable.
normal.cn: 任何动词加 -able 就表示「可以被……的」：readable、washable、breakable。

abstract.en: A steady hand lifts a weight others cannot move: that is the plain picture behind able.
abstract.cn: 一只稳稳的手举起别人搬不动的重物：这就是 able 背后的朴素画面。

abstract.en: The hand can also be a wallet or a licence: able stretches from muscle to money to legal right.
abstract.cn: 这只手也可以是钱包或执照：able 从肌肉一路延伸到金钱与法定权利。

abstract.en: Add un- and the same hand drops: unable is simply the picture reversed.
abstract.cn: 加上 un-，同一只手就垂了下来：unable 只是把画面倒过来。

examples.en: She is an able teacher who can reach even the quietest students.
examples.cn: 她是一位能干的教师，连最沉默的学生也能带动。

examples.en: We were able to catch the last train home.
examples.cn: 我们赶上了回家的末班车。

examples.en: The ramp lets able-bodied and disabled passengers board at the same door.
examples.cn: 这道坡道让健全乘客和残障乘客从同一扇门上车。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「A 伯」——巷口的阿伯什么都会修，真是个能干的人。

root: 拉丁语 habere（握住、拥有）→ habilis（易于掌控的、合适的）→ 古法语 (h)able（有能力的）→ 英语 able；同根词还有 ability、enable、disable，后缀 -able 亦源于拉丁语 -abilis。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all circle the image of a hand with power and reach: skill in a person, power on an occasion, money behind the hand, legal capacity, physical fitness, a naval rating, the suffix, and the idiom that measures ability as a quantity.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都围绕「手上有力量、够得着」这一意象：人的才干、某一场合做得到、背后的财力、法律资格、身体健全、海员等级、后缀构词，以及把能力当作数量来称的固定说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a steady hand that can hold and lift what is in front of it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只稳稳的手，握得住、举得起眼前的东西。

branches.en: THE PERSON: skill and judgement make someone able in a role.
branches.cn: 人物线：技能与判断力让某人在岗位上显得能干。

branches.en: THE OCCASION: the power to act now, with time, money or chance behind it.
branches.cn: 场合线：此刻能行动的力量，背后是时间、金钱或机会。

branches.en: THE BODY AND THE LAW: capacity measured by health or by legal fitness.
branches.cn: 身体与法律线：能力以健康或法定资格来衡量。

branches.en: THE SHIP: a naval rating certifies that a sailor is fit for duty.
branches.cn: 船上线：海军等级证明一名水手能胜任职务。

branches.en: THE MORPHEME AND THE IDIOM: -able makes new adjectives, while more than able measures ability as a quantity.
branches.cn: 构词与习语线：-able 造出新形容词，more than able 把能力当作数量来衡量。

intro.en: Able is a Latin adjective whose ending broke free and became an English suffix; the items below trace that double life.
intro.cn: able 是一个拉丁形容词，它的词尾后来独立出来变成英语后缀；下面的条目追踪这种双重身份。

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 habere、habilis 与 habilitas 均有文献记录，本表所列都不是重构形式。

items.example: Habere is the base of able, habit and exhibit.
items.exampleCN: habere 是 able、habit、exhibit 的共同基础。

items.example: Readable means that can be read.
items.exampleCN: readable 意为「可以被读的」。

items.meaning: in a way that can be
items.example: Suitably is formed with this ending.
items.exampleCN: suitably 就是用这个词尾构成的。

items.meaning: the power or skill to do something
items.example: Ability keeps the Latin noun ending.
items.exampleCN: ability 保留了拉丁名词的词尾。

items.example: A scholarship enabled her to study.

items.meaning: to take away the power to act
items.example: The injury disabled his left arm.

definition_en: on the subject of something, approximately, or in and around a place
core_image: 绕着一样东西转一圈，前后左右都碰到它
scene: 妈妈在厨房里收拾，孩子围着餐桌转来转去，问晚饭吃什么。The children were running about the kitchen while she cooked.
sceneCN: 这里 about 表示「到处、四处」（第 3 个义项：在或到各处）；句意为她做饭时，孩子们在厨房里跑来跑去。

senses.title: On the subject of
senses.definition: on the subject of something, or connected with it
senses.definitionCN: 以某事为话题，或与某事有关
senses.example: She told me about her new job at the bakery.
senses.exampleCN: 她跟我讲了她在那家面包店的新工作。
senses.why: About first meant around; talking around a subject came to mean talking on that subject, since the talk circles it.
senses.whyCN: about 最初表示「在……周围」；围绕一个话题说，就慢慢变成了「关于」这个话题，因为话始终绕着它转。

senses.title: Approximately
senses.definition: used before a number or amount to mean approximately, a little more or less
senses.definitionCN: 用在数字或数量前，表示大约、略多或略少
senses.example: The trip takes about two hours by bus.
senses.exampleCN: 坐公交去大约要两个小时。
senses.why: If a figure is surrounded rather than hit exactly, the word for around naturally marks an estimate.
senses.whyCN: 如果一个数字是被「围着」而不是被精确命中的，那么表示「在周围」的词自然就成了估算的标记。

senses.title: Here and there
senses.definition: in or to many places, moving from one spot to another
senses.definitionCN: 在许多地方，或从一个地点移动到另一个地点
senses.example: The children were running about the kitchen while she cooked.
senses.exampleCN: 她做饭时，孩子们在厨房里跑来跑去。
senses.why: The oldest sense is spatial: about is the space on every side of a point, so movement about is movement in all directions.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是空间的：about 是一个点四周的所有空间，所以动着 about 就是朝各个方向移动。

senses.title: Nearby or on one's person
senses.definition: in the surrounding area, or carried on someone's person
senses.definitionCN: 在周围一带，或带在身上
senses.example: Is there a chemist about? I need something for this cough.
senses.exampleCN: 这附近有药店吗？我需要买点治咳嗽的药。
senses.why: What is about is within reach on every side; from in the area it is a short step to carried on you.
senses.whyCN: 在 about 范围内的东西，四面八方都伸手可及；从「在这一带」到「带在身上」只差一小步。

senses.title: Be about to: on the point of
senses.definition: in be about to, on the point of doing something within a very short time
senses.definitionCN: 用于 be about to，指在极短时间内就要做某事
senses.example: The train is about to leave, so run.
senses.exampleCN: 火车马上要开了，快跑。
senses.why: Something about to happen is already circling the moment of happening: it is near, not yet arrived.
senses.whyCN: 即将发生的事已经绕到了发生的那一刻旁边：它很近，但还没到。

senses.title: Out and about: active outside
senses.definition: in out and about, away from home and moving around, especially after an illness
senses.definitionCN: 用于 out and about，指离开家在外面走动，尤指病后
senses.example: Grandad is out and about again after his knee operation.
senses.exampleCN: 爷爷膝盖手术后又能出门走动了。
senses.why: The same space around the house becomes a measure of recovery: to be out and about is to move through the world again.
senses.whyCN: 房子四周的同一片空间成了康复的尺度：out and about 就是重新在世界上走动起来。

senses.title: How about: a suggestion
senses.definition: in how about or what about, used to suggest something or ask for a decision
senses.definitionCN: 用于 how about 或 what about，提出建议或询问对方的决定
senses.example: How about a walk before dinner?
senses.exampleCN: 晚饭前散散步怎么样？
senses.why: The suggestion is offered as one item placed in the circle of options; the question invites the other person to look around it.
senses.whyCN: 建议被当作放进选项圈子里的一件事；这个问句是请对方绕着它看一看。

senses.title: Bring about: to cause
senses.definition: in bring about, to cause something to happen
senses.definitionCN: 用于 bring about，指使某事发生
senses.example: The new bridge brought about a quiet change in the old town.
senses.exampleCN: 新桥给这座老城带来了悄然的变化。
senses.why: To bring something about is to carry it through the space until it exists on every side, that is, until it is real.
senses.whyCN: bring about 就是把一件事一路带到它四面都成立的地步，也就是带到它真正发生。

intro.en: About is a native English compound of two Old English pieces meaning on and outside, and its history runs from space to subject matter.
intro.cn: about 是英语固有词，由两个古英语成分构成，分别表示「在……上」与「外面」；它的历史从空间一路走到话题。

items.en: būtan meant outside, without, except. It is a compound of be- and ūtan from outside, and it also gives modern but.
items.cn: būtan 意为「在外面、没有、除……之外」。它由 be- 与 ūtan（从外面）构成，也给出今天的 but。

items.en: The form abūtan combined a- on with būtan, giving on the outside of, around. Variants such as onbūtan and ymbbūtan competed in the same period.
items.cn: abūtan 把 a-（在……上）与 būtan 合起来，意为「在……外面、围绕」。同一时期还有 onbūtan、ymbbūtan 等变体并存。

items.en: By the Middle English period the word is usually written aboute, and the sense has widened from around a place to in various directions.
items.cn: 到中古英语时期，这个词通常写作 aboute，词义也从「围绕某处」扩展到「朝各个方向」。

items.en: The concerning sense develops from talking around a matter; the approximately sense likewise grows out of around a figure. Exact first dates for each sense are uncertain.
items.cn: 「关于」义从「围绕一件事来说」发展而来；「大约」义同样从「绕着一个数字」长出来。各义项的确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Fixed phrases such as be about to, out and about and about-face belong to later usage, and about became the ordinary British word for approximately.
items.cn: be about to、out and about、about-face 等固定说法属于较晚的用法；about 则成为英式英语里表示「大约」的常用词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers compounds and near neighbours in spelling; the near-meaning group gathers words for subject matter and estimation.
note.cn: 形近组收本词的复合词与拼写相近的词；近义组收表示话题与估算的词。

entries.definition: A complete turn of the body, or a complete reversal of policy.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「转身」或「立场与政策的彻底转变」，由本词加 face 构成。

entries.definition: The British term for the same turn or reversal.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，英式说法，义同「转身、大转向」。

entries.definition: Indirect, or a circular road junction; built from round plus about.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或名词，义为「绕远的、迂回的」或「环形路口」，由 round 加 about 构成。

entries.definition: Near this place; about plus the old adverbial ending -s.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「在这一带」，由 about 加古副词词尾 -s 构成。

entries.definition: A short period of illness or activity; it only looks similar and comes from a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「一阵（疾病或活动）」；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: On the subject of; formal in tone and common in notices.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「关于」，语气正式，常见于通知与公文。

entries.definition: Close to a number but not exact; more formal than about.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「大约、近似地」，比 about 正式。

entries.definition: On every side of, or in various directions; the closest spatial twin.
entries.definitionCN: 介词或副词，义为「围绕、到处」，是空间义上最接近的同义词。

entries.definition: With reference to; used in letters and official writing.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「关于、就……而言」，多用于书信与正式文字。

entries.definition: Approximately, in everyday speech.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「粗略地、大约」，常见于口语。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the Old English pieces of the word and the phrases it forms today.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子用这个词的古英语成分，以及它今天构成的固定说法。

normal.en: a- means on and būtan means outside: about is on the outside of a thing.
normal.cn: a- 表示「在……上」，būtan 表示「外面」：about 就是「在一件东西的外面」。

normal.en: The same būtan gives but, which still keeps the sense of outside.
normal.cn: 同一个 būtan 还给出 but，后者仍保留「在外」的意味。

normal.en: Be about to puts you on the edge of the moment, close but not there yet.
normal.cn: be about to 把你放在那一刻的边缘：很近，但还没到。

normal.en: Out and about is the everyday phrase for being up and moving again.
normal.cn: out and about 是「又能起身走动」的日常说法。

normal.en: About-face is a turn of the whole body, and then a turn of policy.
normal.cn: about-face 先是整个身体转过来，然后是政策转过来。

abstract.en: Draw a circle round a stone: the line is about the stone, and everything the line touches is about it.
abstract.cn: 绕着石头画一个圈：这条线就在石头周围，线碰到的一切都与它有关。

abstract.en: Stand inside that circle and walk: you are moving about.
abstract.cn: 站进那个圈里走动：你就是在 about 地移动。

abstract.en: Say a few words that circle a subject: the words are about it, though they never touch it.
abstract.cn: 说几句绕着某个话题转的话：这些话就是「关于」它，尽管从未碰到它。

examples.en: She told me about her new job at the bakery.
examples.cn: 她跟我讲了她在那家面包店的新工作。

examples.en: The trip takes about two hours by bus.
examples.cn: 坐公交去大约要两个小时。

examples.en: The children were running about the kitchen while she cooked.
examples.cn: 她做饭时，孩子们在厨房里跑来跑去。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿包特」——把话绕着事情包一圈，说的就是「关于」；数字被包住，就成了「大约」。

root: 古英语 abūtan「在……外面、围绕」，由 a-（在……上）加 būtan（外面、除外）构成；būtan 又给出 but。核心义从「围绕」扩展到「到处」「大约」「关于」，并进入 be about to、out and about 等固定说法。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses keep the shape of a circle: speech circles a subject, a number sits inside an estimate, movement fills the space around, and a phrase puts an action just outside the present.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都保留「圆圈」的形状：话语绕着一个话题，数字被围在估算里，移动填满四周空间，而某个短语把动作放在当下之外。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line drawn around an object, touching it on every side.
core.cn: 核心意象：绕着一样东西画出的线，四面都碰到它。

branches.en: THE SUBJECT: talk circles a matter, and a question circles an option.
branches.cn: 话题线：话语绕着事情转，问句绕着选项转。

branches.en: THE ESTIMATE: a figure is surrounded rather than hit exactly.
branches.cn: 估算线：数字被围住，而不是被精确命中。

branches.en: THE SPACE: movement fills the area, and what is in the area is within reach.
branches.cn: 空间线：移动填满这一带，而在这一带的东西就伸手可及。

branches.en: THE EDGE OF ACTION: about to sits just before the event, and out and about is movement back into the world.
branches.cn: 行动边缘线：about to 正处在事件之前，out and about 则是重新回到世界里走动。

branches.en: THE RESULT: to bring about is to carry something all the way round until it exists.
branches.cn: 结果线：bring about 就是把一件事一路绕到它真正存在。

intro.en: About is not a Latin word at all; it is an Old English compound whose pieces still survive in other English words.
intro.cn: about 完全不是拉丁词，而是古英语复合词；它的各个成分仍活在其他英语词里。

latinIntro.en: About is a native Germanic word with no Latin borrowing behind it, so the Latin entry list is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: about 是日耳曼语固有词，背后没有拉丁语借入成分，因此拉丁同源词一栏留空。

definition_zh: 在……上方；高于；超过；上述的
definition_en: in or to a higher place than something, or greater in amount, rank or importance
core_image: 抬头看见屋檐上方的一线天空
scene: 冬天的早晨，山谷里全是雾，山顶的寺庙露在雾线之上。The temple stands above the clouds in the early morning.
sceneCN: 这里 above 表示「在……上方、高于」（第 1 个义项：位置在……上方）；句意为清晨那座寺庙立在云层之上。

pos.zh: 在……上方；超过；高于
在上面；在上方
上述的；上文的

derivatives.zh: above 加 mentioned 构成，义为「上述的、前面提到的」
above 加 board 构成，义为「光明正大的、公开的」
above 加 ground 构成，义为「地面以上的、在地面上的」

senses.title: In a higher position
senses.definition: in or to a higher place than something, without touching it
senses.definitionCN: 在比某物更高的位置，且不与之接触
senses.example: The temple stands above the clouds in the early morning.
senses.exampleCN: 清晨，那座寺庙立在云层之上。
senses.why: Old English abufan meant on the upper side of; the word simply names the side of a thing that faces up.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 abufan 的意思是「在……朝上的那一面」；这个词只是指出一件东西朝上的那一侧。

senses.title: Higher up, overhead
senses.definition: as an adverb, at a higher level, in the sky or overhead
senses.definitionCN: 作副词，指在更高处、天空中或头顶上方
senses.example: A lamp hung above, throwing a small circle of light.
senses.exampleCN: 一盏灯挂在上方，投下一小圈光。
senses.why: The same upper side is viewed without an object: there is nothing named below, only the space overhead.
senses.whyCN: 同一个朝上的一面，在不提对象时被单独看待：下面没点名任何东西，只有头顶的那片空间。

senses.title: More than a number or level
senses.definition: greater than a particular number, amount, level or standard
senses.definitionCN: 大于某个数字、数量、水平或标准
senses.example: Temperatures stayed above freezing all night.
senses.exampleCN: 整夜气温都在冰点以上。
senses.why: Height is the easiest scale for quantity: more is literally higher on a vertical line, so above takes the place of more than.
senses.whyCN: 高度是最直观的数量刻度：更多就是在线条上更靠上，于是 above 顶替了「多于」。

senses.title: Above all: most importantly
senses.definition: in the phrase above all, more than anything else and before everything else
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 above all，表示最重要的、先于一切
senses.example: Above all, keep the children away from the water.
senses.exampleCN: 最要紧的是，别让孩子靠近水边。
senses.why: What stands above the rest in space stands first in importance; height becomes rank.
senses.whyCN: 在空间上高过其余的东西，在重要程度上也排在最前；高度就这样变成了等级。

senses.title: Above suspicion: beyond doubt
senses.definition: in the phrase above suspicion or above criticism, too honest or good to be doubted or blamed
senses.definitionCN: 用于 above suspicion 或 above criticism，指品行好到不容怀疑或指责
senses.example: Her record was above suspicion from the first day.
senses.exampleCN: 她的记录从第一天起就无可怀疑。
senses.why: If a thing is above reach, the hand of doubt cannot get at it; moral height means being out of range.
senses.whyCN: 如果一样东西高到伸手够不着，怀疑的手就抓不到它；道德上的高度就是超出触及范围。

senses.title: Above doing something: too proud
senses.definition: in the phrase above doing something, considering oneself too important or honest to do it
senses.definitionCN: 用于 above doing something，指自认身份或品行高而不屑去做
senses.example: He is not above taking credit for other people's work.
senses.exampleCN: 他并不屑于把别人的成果算作自己的功劳。
senses.why: A person placed high looks down on a small act; being above an action means refusing to stoop to it.
senses.whyCN: 被放在高处的人俯视一件小事；above an action 就是不肯为它弯腰。

senses.title: Mentioned earlier
senses.definition: as an adjective or adverb, mentioned earlier in a piece of writing
senses.definitionCN: 作形容词或副词，指在文章前面已经提到过
senses.example: The above figures cover the last two quarters only.
senses.exampleCN: 上述数字只涵盖最近两个季度。
senses.why: A page has height too: what is above in the text has already been read, so spatial height becomes earlier position.
senses.whyCN: 纸面也有高度：文本中「在上方」的内容已经读过了，空间高度于是变成时间上的靠前。

senses.title: From heaven or a higher power
senses.definition: in religious or literary use, from heaven or from a power regarded as higher than human
senses.definitionCN: 在宗教或文学用法中，指来自上天或高于人的力量
senses.example: They waited for a sign from above.
senses.exampleCN: 他们等待来自上天的征兆。
senses.why: The sky is the highest place people can point to, so whatever is above is naturally placed with the gods.
senses.whyCN: 天空是人能指向的最高处，因此凡在「上面」的，自然就被归到神那里。

intro.en: Above is an Old English compound of on and an older word for over, and its height became rank, quantity and text order.
intro.cn: above 是一个古英语复合词，由「在……上」与更古老的「在上方」一词构成；它的高度后来变成等级、数量与文本顺序。

items.en: The element behind Old English ufan is generally reconstructed as a Germanic form related to up and over. The exact shape is a reconstruction, not a recorded word.
items.cn: 古英语 ufan 背后的成分，一般认为可重构为与 up、over 有关的日耳曼语形式；确切形态属于重构，并非有记录的词。

items.en: ufan meant from above, overhead, and is related to ūp up and ofer over.
items.cn: ufan 意为「从上面、在头顶」，与 ūp（up）和 ofer（over）同族。

items.en: a- on plus bufan above gave abufan, on the upper side of. The b- of bufan is the same be- seen in before and behind.
items.cn: a-（在……上）加 bufan（在上面）构成 abufan，意为「在……朝上的那一面」。bufan 的 b- 与 before、behind 里的 be- 同源。

items.en: Written forms such as above and aboven appear in Middle English as the word settles into its modern shape.
items.cn: 中古英语中出现 above、aboven 等写法，这个词逐渐定型为今天的样子。

items.en: The spatial sense extends to rank and quantity, and to the page: the above means what has already been written.
items.cn: 空间义扩展到等级与数量，也扩展到纸面：the above 指已经写在前面的话。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers compounds and one spelling neighbour; the near-meaning group gathers words for height, excess and limits.
note.cn: 形近组收本词的复合词与一个拼写相近的词；近义组收表示高度、超出与界限的词。

entries.definition: Named earlier in the same text.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「上述的、前面提到的」，由本词加 mentioned 构成。

entries.definition: Open and honest, literally above the table.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「光明正大的、公开的」，字面是「在桌面之上」。

entries.definition: On or above the surface of the ground.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或副词，义为「地面以上的、在地面上」。

entries.definition: A home or residence, from the verb abide; it only looks similar and comes from a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「住所、家」，来自动词 abide；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Higher than or across; often interchangeable with above, but can also mean covering.
entries.definitionCN: 介词或副词，义为「在……上方、越过」，常可与 above 互换，但也含「覆盖」之意。

entries.definition: Directly above your head; more specific than above.
entries.definitionCN: 副词或形容词，义为「在头顶上方」，比 above 更具体。

entries.definition: On the far side of, or more than; used for limits rather than height.
entries.definitionCN: 介词或副词，义为「在……那一边、超出」，用于界限而非高度。

entries.definition: Greater than; a formal word for the quantity sense of above.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「超过的、大于的」，是 above 数量义的正式说法。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the Old English pieces of the word and the phrases it forms today.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子用这个词的古英语成分，以及它今天构成的固定说法。

normal.en: a- is on and bufan is above: above is on the upper side of.
normal.cn: a- 是「在……上」，bufan 是「在上面」：above 就是「在……朝上的那一面」。

normal.en: The family includes up and over, so height is built into the word.
normal.cn: 这个词族还包括 up 与 over，高度是它的内置含义。

normal.en: Above all puts one thing at the top of the list of importance.
normal.cn: above all 把一件事放到重要性的最顶端。

normal.en: Above suspicion means too high to be reached by doubt.
normal.cn: above suspicion 意为高到怀疑够不着。

normal.en: The above in a letter means the lines you have already read.
normal.cn: 信里的 the above 指你已经读过的那几行。

abstract.en: Look up at a roof edge against the sky: the space beyond it is above.
abstract.cn: 抬头看屋檐与天空的交界：屋檐那一侧的空间就是 above。

abstract.en: A vertical line turns into a ladder: height becomes rank, then amount, then order on a page.
abstract.cn: 一条竖线变成一把梯子：高度成了等级，再成了数量，最后成了纸面上的先后。

abstract.en: Whatever is above is out of reach, which is why it can also mean beyond blame or doubt.
abstract.cn: 在上方的东西都够不着，所以它也能表示「超出责备或怀疑」。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿包夫」——包袱举在头顶上面，就是「在上方」。

root: 古英语 abufan「在……上面」，由 a-（在……上）加 bufan（在上面）构成；bufan 与 ūp（up）、ofer（over）同属一个日耳曼词族。核心义从「位置更高」扩展到「数量更多」「等级更高」以及「文中靠前」。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense of above starts from a vertical line: a higher place becomes a greater amount, then a higher rank, then an earlier position on the page, and finally the sky where higher powers are placed.
sensesIntro.cn: above 的每个义项都从一条竖线出发：更高的位置变成更大的数量，再变成更高的等级，再变成纸面上更靠前的位置，最后变成安置神灵的天空。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line of sky visible over the edge of a roof.
core.cn: 核心意象：屋檐边缘之上露出的那一线天空。

branches.en: THE SPACE: something sits higher, with or without a named object below.
branches.cn: 空间线：某物处在更高处，下方点不点名对象都可以。

branches.en: THE SCALE: height turns into quantity, so above means more than a figure.
branches.cn: 刻度线：高度变成数量，于是 above 表示多于某个数字。

branches.en: THE RANK: what is higher is more important, harder to doubt and harder to stoop to.
branches.cn: 等级线：更高的东西更重要，更难被怀疑，也更难让它弯腰。

branches.en: THE PAGE: what is above in a text has already been read.
branches.cn: 纸面线：文本中位于上方的部分已经读过了。

branches.en: THE SKY: the highest visible place is where higher powers are put.
branches.cn: 天空线：可见的最高处，就是人们安置更高力量的地方。

definition_zh: 在国外；到国外；广泛地；流传在外
definition_en: in or to a foreign country, or spread over a wide area and known to many people
core_image: 一只行李箱立在自家门口，人已经站在另一片国土上
scene: 她收拾好行李，把钥匙交给邻居，说要去念两年书。My cousin has been living abroad since she finished college.

senses.title: Living in a foreign country
senses.definition: staying or living in a country that is not your own
senses.definitionCN: 留在或居住在自己国家以外的国家
senses.example: She has lived abroad for six years and rarely comes home.
senses.exampleCN: 她在国外住了六年，很少回家。
senses.why: Abroad began as 'spread wide'; from the wide world outside the home it settled on lands beyond one's own border.
senses.whyCN: abroad 原义是「铺得很开」；从自家门外那片广阔天地出发，词义最终落在国境之外的国土上，这就是「在国外」的来源。

senses.title: Going or travelling to a foreign country
senses.definition: travelling or moving to a country other than one's own
senses.definitionCN: 前往或搬到本国以外的国家
senses.example: He is going abroad next month to study design.
senses.exampleCN: 他下个月要出国学设计。
senses.why: The same wide space can be seen as a place or as a direction; with verbs of movement, abroad marks the destination.
senses.whyCN: 同一片广阔空间既可以看作地点，也可以看作方向；与表示移动的动词连用时，abroad 就指向目的地「国外」。

senses.title: From a foreign country
senses.definition: in the phrase from abroad, originating in or arriving from another country
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 from abroad，指来自另一个国家或从另一国到达
senses.example: Most of the students here are from abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的学生大多来自国外。
senses.why: If abroad is the wide space outside, then from abroad names the direction that space sends people and things.
senses.whyCN: 如果 abroad 指国门之外那片广阔空间，那么 from abroad 就标出这片空间送来人与物的方向，这是同一空间概念的起点用法。

senses.title: A rumour or feeling in circulation
senses.titleCN: 流传在外（的传闻或情绪）
senses.definition: in the phrase there is something abroad, existing and being talked about among people
senses.definitionCN: 用于「某事物 abroad」的结构，指某种说法或情绪存在于人群中并被谈论
senses.example: There is a rumour abroad that the factory will close.
senses.exampleCN: 外面流传着工厂将要关闭的传闻。
senses.why: Something spread wide is no longer in one place; a rumour abroad has escaped and is now moving among people.
senses.whyCN: 被铺得很开的东西不再待在一个地方；a rumour abroad 表示传闻已经跑出去，在人群中间流动，这是「广泛」义的自然延伸。

senses.title: Spread over a wide area
senses.definition: in the phrase spread abroad, scattered or made known over a large area
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 spread abroad，指散布或传播到很大范围
senses.example: The seeds were spread abroad by the autumn wind.
senses.exampleCN: 种子被秋风吹散到各处。
senses.why: This is the oldest picture in the word: broad means wide, and a- makes it adverbial, so things are sent out over width.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最古老的画面：broad 是「宽」，a- 使它成为副词，于是东西被向外铺开、撒到四面八方。

senses.title: Out of doors, not at home
senses.definition: in older or literary use, out in the open or away from one's house
senses.definitionCN: 较旧或文学性的用法，指在户外，或不在家中
senses.example: The children were abroad in the fields before sunrise.
senses.exampleCN: 天还没亮，孩子们就已经在田野里了。
senses.why: Before it meant foreign lands, abroad meant out in the wide open; the modern foreign sense grew out of this older use.
senses.whyCN: 在表示「外国」之前，abroad 先表示「到了外面开阔处」；今天的「国外」义正是从这种「出门在外」的旧义长出来的。

senses.title: Home and abroad as a set phrase
senses.definition: in the phrase at home and abroad, covering both one's own country and foreign countries
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 at home and abroad，指既包括本国也包括外国
senses.example: The band is now famous at home and abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 这支乐队如今在国内外都很有名。
senses.why: The word can stand opposite home, so the two together draw the full map: inside the border and outside it.
senses.whyCN: abroad 可以与 home 相对而站，两者合起来正好画出完整的地图：国境之内与国境之外。

senses.title: All abroad: completely mistaken
senses.definition: in the old British phrase all abroad, completely wrong or confused about something
senses.definitionCN: 用于英式旧短语 all abroad，指对某事完全弄错或不知所措
senses.example: You are all abroad if you think the train leaves at six.
senses.exampleCN: 你要是以为火车六点开，那就完全弄错了。
senses.why: To be abroad is to be away from the right place; being all abroad is being far from the truth as well.
senses.whyCN: abroad 本就是「离开了应在的地方」；all abroad 则把这个偏离推到极致，连真相都离得很远。

intro.en: Abroad is the adverb from broad: a prefix meaning on was added to the old adjective for wide.
intro.cn: abroad 是 broad 的副词形式：一个表示「在」的前缀加在古老的「宽」这个形容词上。

items.en: Brād meant wide or broad, and it is the adjective behind both broad and abroad.
items.cn: 古英语 brād 意为「宽的、广阔的」，是 broad 与 abroad 共同的形容词基础。

items.en: The prefix a-, weakened from on, turned adjectives and nouns into adverbs such as abed, afoot and abroad.
items.cn: 前缀 a- 由 on 弱化而来，把形容词或名词变成副词，如 abed、afoot、abroad。

items.en: Abroad is recorded in the fourteenth century meaning widely apart or out of doors; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: abroad 在十四世纪有记录，义为「散开地、在户外」；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: By the sixteenth century the sense of being in or going to foreign countries is established; the older outdoor sense then became literary.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，「在外国、到外国」的义项已经确立；较早的「户外」义此后转为文学用法。

items.en: Modern English keeps the foreign sense as the everyday one and preserves the wide-spread sense in phrases such as spread abroad.
items.cn: 现代英语以「国外」为日常义，并在 spread abroad 一类短语中保留「广泛传播」的旧义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the broad root and one word that is often confused with it; the near-meaning group gathers words about foreign places or being away.
note.cn: 形近组收 broad 词根以及一个常被混淆的词；近义组收表示外国或离开原处的词。

entries.definition: Wide; the adjective from which abroad was built with the prefix a-.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「宽的、广阔的」，abroad 正是由它加前缀 a- 构成。

entries.definition: The noun for width or extent, from the same broad root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「宽度、广度」，与 broad 同根。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to make or become wider.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「加宽、扩大」，由 broad 加 -en 构成。

entries.definition: On or onto a ship, train or plane; it was formed from a- plus board, so it only looks like abroad and has a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 副词或介词，义为「在船（车、飞机）上」，由 a- 加 board 构成，只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: In or to a country across the sea; common in trade, study and postings.
entries.definitionCN: 副词或形容词，义为「在海外、去海外」，多用于贸易、留学或派驻。

entries.definition: Belonging to a country other than one's own; an adjective rather than an adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「外国的」，是形容词而非副词。

entries.definition: At a distance from home or from a place; it does not say that the place is foreign.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「离开、在外」，只表示不在原处，不说明是否在国外。

entries.definition: Located or happening in the sea away from the coast, or set up in another country for tax reasons.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或副词，义为「近海的、境外的」，常指海上或为避税设在国外。

normalIntro.en: The hooks connect abroad to broad, to the a- prefix, and to the phrases it actually forms.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想把 abroad 与 broad、前缀 a-，以及它真实构成的短语连起来。

normal.en: a- means on and broad means wide: abroad is out in the wide world.
normal.cn: a- 表示「在」，broad 表示「宽」：abroad 就是置身于广阔的天地之中。

normal.en: The same broad root gives breadth and broaden, all about width.
normal.cn: 同一个 broad 词根还给出 breadth 与 broaden，都围绕「宽度」。

normal.en: Go abroad is to step outside your own border; live abroad is to stay there.
normal.cn: go abroad 是走出国境，live abroad 是留在那里生活。

normal.en: From abroad: the direction is inward, from the wide world to here.
normal.cn: from abroad：方向是向内的，从那片广阔世界来到这里。

normal.en: Spread abroad keeps the old sense of being scattered over a wide area.
normal.cn: spread abroad 保留了「散布到很广范围」的旧义。

abstract.en: Picture a map unrolled on a table: everything beyond your own line is abroad.
abstract.cn: 想象一张在桌上摊开的地图：自己那条边界之外的部分就是 abroad。

abstract.en: The word is about width before it is about nations, so anything spread wide is abroad.
abstract.cn: 这个词先关乎「宽」，然后才关乎「国」，所以凡是被铺开的东西都在 abroad。

abstract.en: Home and abroad are the two halves of one map, so the word always answers inside or outside.
abstract.cn: home 与 abroad 是一张地图的两半，这个词始终在回答「在里面还是在外面」。

examples.en: She has lived abroad for six years and rarely comes home.
examples.cn: 她在国外住了六年，很少回家。

examples.en: He is going abroad next month to study design.
examples.cn: 他下个月要出国学设计。

examples.en: There is a rumour abroad that the factory will close.
examples.cn: 外面流传着工厂将要关闭的传闻。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「啊，布罗德」——踏出国门，外面是一片宽阔天地：出国、在国外。

root: 古英语 brād「宽的」加副词性前缀 a-（由 on 弱化，表示「在」）构成，字面义为「在广阔处」，先指「在户外、散开地」，十六世纪起指「在国外」。

sensesIntro.en: Abroad starts from the image of a wide open space; that space can be a foreign country, a direction, a rumour spreading, the outdoors, or a mind far from the truth.
sensesIntro.cn: abroad 从「一片开阔空间」起意；这片空间可以是外国、一个方向、四处流传的传闻、户外的天地，也可以是一颗远离真相的心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wide open land beyond the border, with a suitcase standing at the gate.
core.cn: 核心意象：国境之外一片开阔的土地，门口立着一只行李箱。

branches.en: THE JOURNEY: living in another country and moving to it.
branches.cn: 行程线：在另一国生活，以及前往另一国。

branches.en: THE DIRECTION: from abroad points inward, from the wide world to here.
branches.cn: 方向线：from abroad 指向内侧，从那片广阔世界来到这里。

branches.en: THE SPREAD: things scattered or made known over a wide area.
branches.cn: 铺开线：事物被散布或传播到很广的范围。

branches.en: THE CIRCULATION: a rumour moving among people, and the pairing with home.
branches.cn: 流转线：传闻在人群中流动，以及与 home 成对使用。

branches.en: THE OLD SENSE: out in the open, and the phrase all abroad for being far from the truth.
branches.cn: 旧义线：身处户外，以及 all abroad 表示远离真相。

intro.en: Abroad is a prefix plus an adjective, and the same prefix builds a large family of English location words.
intro.cn: abroad 是一个前缀加一个形容词，同一个前缀还构成了一大族英语方位词。

latinIntro.en: Broad is a Germanic word with no reliable Latin cognate, so the Latin list is empty by design.
latinIntro.cn: broad 是日耳曼语词，没有可靠的拉丁同族词，所以拉丁语条目有意留空。

items.exampleCN: 一条宽阔的河穿过小镇。

items.example: They travelled abroad for a year.

旅行开阔心胸。

definition_en: the state of not being present, or the lack of something that ought to be there
core_image: 一把空着的椅子，桌上还留着你的杯子
scene: 教室里那把椅子空了一整个星期，老师点名时停了一下。His long absence from class worried his classmates.
sceneCN: 这里 absence 指长时间没来上课（第 2 个义项：缺勤、缺课）；句意为他的长期缺课让同学们担心。

pos.zh: 缺席；不在；缺乏；缺失

collocations.phrase: absence makes the heart grow fonder

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 absens 进入英语，义为「缺席的；不在的；缺乏的」
由 absent 加 -ly 构成，义为「心不在焉地」
由 absent 加 -ee 构成，义为「缺席者」，如 absentee landlord 指在外地主
