senses.title: The state of not being present
senses.definition: the fact of a person or thing not being in the expected place
senses.definitionCN: 人或事物不在应有的位置这一事实
senses.example: Nobody noticed his absence until the meeting ended.
senses.exampleCN: 直到会议结束，才有人注意到他没来。
senses.why: Latin abesse is ab- 'away' plus esse 'to be', so absence is quite literally being away.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 abesse 是 ab-「离开」加 esse「存在」，absence 字面就是「存在到别处去了」，所以先有「不在场」。

senses.title: An occasion of missing school or work
senses.definition: a countable instance of not attending school, work or a regular duty
senses.definitionCN: 可数的一次未到校、未上班或未履行固定职责
senses.example: The teacher marked three absences in his record.
senses.exampleCN: 老师在他的记录上记了三次缺勤。
senses.why: Each time a person fails to be present, the state turns into an event that can be counted.
senses.whyCN: 每当一个人没能出现在该在的地方，那种「不在」就变成一件可数的事，于是有了「一次缺勤」。

senses.title: The lack of something that should be there
senses.definition: the state of not having something, especially a quality, fact or condition that is needed
senses.definitionCN: 指缺少某物，尤指缺少所需的性质、事实或条件
senses.example: The absence of any witnesses made the case hard to prove.
senses.exampleCN: 没有任何证人，使这个案子难以证明。
senses.why: If being can be away from a place, it can also be away from a thing: what should be there simply is not.
senses.whyCN: 如果「存在」可以离开某个地点，也可以离开某样东西：本该在那里的东西就是不在，于是义为「缺乏」。

senses.title: In the absence of: without something
senses.definition: in the phrase in the absence of, used to mean without something or because something is not available
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 in the absence of，表示没有某物或因为某物不可得
senses.example: In the absence of a doctor, the nurse made the decision alone.
senses.exampleCN: 在没有医生的情况下，护士独自做了决定。
senses.why: The phrase turns the missing thing into a condition: the empty place becomes the setting for what happens.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把缺失的东西变成一种条件：空出来的位置成了事情发生的背景。

senses.title: Leave of absence: official time away
senses.definition: in the phrase leave of absence, formal permission to be away from work or duty for a period
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 leave of absence，指获准在一段时间内离开工作或职责
senses.example: She took a year's leave of absence to care for her father.
senses.exampleCN: 她请了一年假去照顾父亲。
senses.why: Here the absence is granted rather than regretted: the same empty place is now filled by permission.
senses.whyCN: 这里的「不在」是被批准的，而不是令人遗憾的：同一个空位，如今由许可来填补。

senses.title: Absence of mind: being distracted
senses.definition: in the phrase absence of mind, the state of not paying attention because the mind is elsewhere
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 absence of mind，指心思在别处而没有留意眼前
senses.example: He signed the wrong form through a moment of absence of mind.
senses.exampleCN: 他一时心不在焉，签错了表格。
senses.why: The mind can be absent from the body just as a person is absent from a room; the same away moves inward.
senses.whyCN: 人可以从房间里「不在」，心思也可以从身体这里「不在」；同一个「离开」转向了内部，于是有了心不在焉。

senses.title: Absence makes the heart grow fonder
senses.definition: in the proverb absence makes the heart grow fonder, being apart is said to increase affection
senses.definitionCN: 用于谚语「absence makes the heart grow fonder」，指分离反而让人更添思念
senses.example: After a month apart she missed him badly; absence makes the heart grow fonder.
senses.exampleCN: 分开一个月后她非常想念他；真是离别使人情更深。
senses.why: The empty place is felt as a shape, and that shape keeps the absent person present in the mind.
senses.whyCN: 空出来的位置会被感受成一个形状，而这个形状让不在场的人一直留在心里，于是缺席反而加深了感情。

senses.title: Conspicuous by its absence
senses.definition: in the phrase conspicuous by its absence, noticeably missing from a place where it was expected
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 conspicuous by its absence，指在本该出现之处明显缺席，反而引人注意
senses.example: The star player was conspicuous by his absence from the team photo.
senses.exampleCN: 球队合影里少了那位明星球员，反而格外显眼。
senses.why: A gap in a pattern draws the eye more than a filled slot; the missing thing becomes the most visible thing.
senses.whyCN: 图案里的空缺比填满的格子更抓眼；缺失的东西反而成了最显眼的东西。

intro.en: Absence comes from the Latin verb for being, with the prefix that means away.
intro.cn: absence 来自拉丁语中表示「存在」的动词，加上表示「离开」的前缀。

items.en: Esse is the Latin verb to be; abesse, to be away, is built from ab- plus esse.
items.cn: esse 是拉丁语动词「存在、是」；abesse「不在」由 ab- 加 esse 构成。

items.en: Absens, the present participle of abesse, meant being away, and it is the source of English absent.
items.cn: absens 是 abesse 的现在分词，意为「不在的」，也是英语 absent 的来源。

items.en: Absentia is recorded in classical Latin for the state of being away, including absence from a place or from a duty.
items.cn: absentia 在古典拉丁语中已有记录，表示离开、不在的状态，包括不在某地或未尽职责。

items.en: Old French absence carried the noun into English in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 absence 把这个名词带入英语，时在十四世纪。

items.en: English extended the word from people to things, so that a missing fact or quality could also be called an absence.
items.cn: 英语把它从人扩展到事物，缺失的事实或性质也可以称为 absence。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the absent family and one deceptive spelling; the near-meaning group holds words for lack and for not attending.
note.cn: 形近组收 absent 词族以及一个容易看错的拼写；近义组收表示缺乏与未出席的词。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning not present; it comes from the same Latin absens.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「缺席的、不在的」，与 absence 同出拉丁语 absens。

entries.definition: A person who is absent, especially from work or school.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「缺席者」，尤指缺勤者或缺课学生。

entries.definition: In a distracted way, as if the mind is somewhere else.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「心不在焉地」。

entries.definition: A bitter green liqueur; the spelling is close, but the word comes from a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「苦艾酒」，只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: The state of not having enough of something; it usually implies need, not mere emptiness.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「缺乏、不足」，通常含「不够用」的意味，而不只是空着。

entries.definition: A situation in which there is not enough of something that people need.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「短缺」，指所需之物数量不足。

entries.definition: An empty space left by something missing; more literary and more physical.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「空缺、虚空」，更具文学与空间感。

entries.definition: The formal word for failing to be present at a required event.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「未出席」，是较正式的用语。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the real Latin pieces ab- and esse, and the phrases absence keeps appearing in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想使用真实的拉丁语成分 ab- 与 esse，以及 absence 实际出现的短语。

normal.en: ab- means away and esse means to be: absence is being away.
normal.cn: ab- 表示「离开」，esse 表示「存在」：absence 就是「存在在别处」。

normal.en: The same esse gives present and essence, all about being.
normal.cn: 同一个 esse 还给出 present 与 essence，都与「存在」有关。

normal.en: Absent is the adjective, absence the noun, absently the adverb.
normal.cn: absent 是形容词，absence 是名词，absently 是副词。

normal.en: Leave of absence is absence with permission attached.
normal.cn: leave of absence 是附带了许可的「不在」。

normal.en: In the absence of means the missing thing has become a condition.
normal.cn: in the absence of 表示缺失之物已经变成了一种条件。

abstract.en: Picture an empty chair at a dinner table: the chair says more than any speech.
abstract.cn: 想象餐桌旁一把空椅子：这把椅子比任何话都说得更多。

abstract.en: Emptiness is never neutral; the missing thing keeps a shape in the room.
abstract.cn: 空缺从不中性；缺失之物会在房间里留下一个形状。

abstract.en: The mind can be absent from the body, which is why the word also names distraction.
abstract.cn: 心思可以从身体里缺席，所以这个词也用来指心不在焉。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses start from one empty place: a person missing, an event counted, a thing lacking, a phrase built on that lack, or a gap that becomes meaningful.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从同一个空位出发：缺了一个人、数出一次缺席、少了一样东西、由缺失构成的短语，或一个有意义的空缺。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty chair with a cup still standing on the table.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把空椅子，桌上的杯子还在。

branches.en: THE PERSON: not being there, and each countable failure to attend.
branches.cn: 人物线：不在这里，以及每一次可以计数的未到场。

branches.en: THE THING: a missing fact or quality, and the condition built from that lack.
branches.cn: 事物线：缺失的事实或性质，以及由这种缺乏构成的条件。

branches.en: THE PERMISSION: leave of absence is the empty place officially approved.
branches.cn: 许可线：leave of absence 是被正式批准的空位。

branches.en: THE MIND: absence of mind turns the gap inward.
branches.cn: 心智线：absence of mind 把这种空缺转向内部。

branches.en: THE PARADOX: the gap deepens feeling, or becomes the most visible thing in the frame.
branches.cn: 悖论线：空缺加深了感情，或者成了画面里最显眼的东西。

definition_zh: 绝对的；完全的；专制的；确实的
definition_en: complete and total, free from any limit or condition, or true without depending on anything else
core_image: 一把没有刻度的尺子，量什么都不用参照别的东西
scene: 屋里静得连钟摆声都听得见，谁也不敢先开口。The room fell into absolute silence when she began to speak.
sceneCN: 这里 absolute 表示「完全的、彻底的」（第 1 个义项：完全的）；句意为她开口时，房间里变得一片寂静。

pos.zh: 绝对的；完全的；专制的；确实的
绝对（哲学概念）

derivatives.zh: 由 absolute 加 -ly 构成，义为「完全地；绝对地；当然」
由 absolute 加 -ness 构成，义为「绝对性；完全」

senses.title: Complete and total
senses.definition: complete in every respect, with nothing missing or partial
senses.definitionCN: 各方面都完整，没有缺失或部分之处
senses.example: The room fell into absolute silence.
senses.exampleCN: 房间里变得一片寂静。
senses.why: Latin absolutus meant loosened or set free; something set free from every condition is complete in itself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 absolutus 意为「被松开、被释放」；从一切条件中解放出来的东西，自身就是完整的，所以指「完全」。

senses.title: Holding power without limit
senses.definition: of a ruler or government, having complete control and no legal check
senses.definitionCN: 指统治者或政府拥有完全控制权，不受法律制约
senses.example: The country was ruled by an absolute monarch for two centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家由一位专制的君主统治了两百年。
senses.why: A power freed from all restraints is the political version of being loosened from conditions.
senses.whyCN: 摆脱一切约束的权力，正是「从条件中松开」这一意象在政治上的版本。

senses.title: True regardless of context
senses.definition: of a value, standard or truth, valid on its own and not dependent on comparison
senses.definitionCN: 指价值、标准或真理本身成立，不依赖与其他事物比较
senses.example: Philosophers still argue whether any absolute moral standard exists.
senses.exampleCN: 哲学家们仍在争论是否存在任何绝对的道德标准。
senses.why: If a thing is loosed from relations, it no longer needs a second thing to be measured against.
senses.whyCN: 如果一事物从事物关系中松脱出来，它就不再需要另一个事物作为参照，这就是「绝对」的抽象义。

senses.title: Absolute zero: the lowest temperature
senses.definition: in physics, the lowest temperature possible, at which particles have minimum energy
senses.definitionCN: 物理学中指可能达到的最低温度，此时粒子能量最小
senses.example: Nothing can be cooled below absolute zero.
senses.exampleCN: 任何东西都无法冷却到绝对零度以下。
senses.why: This zero is absolute because it is fixed by nature, not by a scale that someone chose.
senses.whyCN: 这个零之所以是「绝对的」，是因为它由自然确定，而不是由人选择的温标确定，仍是不依赖参照的意思。

senses.title: Absolute value in mathematics
senses.definition: in mathematics, the distance of a number from zero, written without a sign
senses.definitionCN: 数学中指一个数到零的距离，不计正负号
senses.example: The absolute value of minus five is five.
senses.exampleCN: 负五的绝对值是五。
senses.why: Mathematics strips away direction and keeps only size, leaving a quantity that depends on nothing but distance.
senses.whyCN: 数学把方向剥掉，只留下大小，得到的是一个只由距离决定、不依赖正负的量。

senses.title: The absolute construction in grammar
senses.definition: in grammar, a phrase that stands apart from the main clause because it has its own subject, as in the weather being fine, we went out
senses.definitionCN: 语法中指带有自己主语、与主句相对独立的短语，如「the weather being fine, we went out」
senses.example: The absolute construction gives the phrase its own subject.
senses.exampleCN: 独立结构让这个短语拥有自己的主语。
senses.why: The phrase is absolved from the main clause: loosened from it, it stands on its own.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语从主句中被「松开」了：与主句脱离之后，它独自站立，所以称为独立结构。

senses.title: Absolute majority in voting
senses.definition: in voting, more than half of all possible votes, not merely more than any rival
senses.definitionCN: 在投票中指超过全部可能票数的一半，而不只是多于其他任何一方
senses.example: The bill passed with an absolute majority of the assembly.
senses.exampleCN: 该法案以议会绝对多数获得通过。
senses.why: The threshold is fixed by the whole, not by the size of the opposition, so it is absolute rather than relative.
senses.whyCN: 这个门槛由全体决定，而不是由对手的多少决定，因此是「绝对的」而非「相对的」。

senses.title: The Absolute as a philosophical noun
senses.definition: in philosophy, the ultimate reality that depends on nothing else and contains everything
senses.definitionCN: 哲学中指不依赖他物、包含一切的终极实在
senses.example: Hegel tried to describe the Absolute as a whole that includes its own opposites.
senses.exampleCN: 黑格尔试图把「绝对」描述为一个包含自身对立面的整体。
senses.why: The adjective turns into a noun: whatever is free of all conditions becomes something one can name.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转成了名词：凡摆脱一切条件者，就成为一个可以被命名的东西，这就是哲学里的「绝对」。

intro.en: Absolute is a Latin participle built from a prefix of separation and a verb meaning to loosen.
intro.cn: absolute 是一个拉丁语分词，由表示分离的前缀与表示「松开」的动词构成。

items.en: Solvere meant to loosen, untie or dissolve; it is also the source of solve, solution and dissolve.
items.cn: solvere 意为「松开、解开、溶解」，也是 solve、solution、dissolve 的来源。

items.en: Ab- away plus solvere gave absolvere, to loosen from, set free or finish.
items.cn: ab-「离开」加 solvere 构成 absolvere，意为「松开、释放、完成」。

items.en: The past participle absolutus meant loosened, unrestricted or complete; grammar and law already used it in the classical period.
items.cn: 过去分词 absolutus 意为「被松开的、不受限制的、完整的」；古典时期语法与法律已在使用。

items.en: Old French absolut and the Latin form behind it brought the word into English in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 absolut 及其背后的拉丁语形式在十四世纪把这个词带入英语。

items.en: Science and grammar each fixed a phrase, absolute zero and the absolute construction, while everyday speech kept the sense of complete.
items.cn: 科学与语法各自固定了一个短语，即绝对零度与独立结构；日常语言则保留「完全」的意思。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the family built on the Latin participle; the near-meaning group holds words for wholeness and for freedom from conditions.
note.cn: 形近组收由这个拉丁分词构成的一族词；近义组收表示「完整」与「不受条件限制」的词。

entries.definition: Entire in amount or degree, often used for emphasis.

entries.definition: Given or done without any conditions attached; closest to the political sense.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无条件的」，与「不受条件限制」这一层义项最接近。

entries.definition: Complete, used mostly of bad or extreme things.

normalIntro.en: The hooks rest on the real Latin pieces ab- and solvere and on the fixed phrases the word now forms.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想依靠真实的拉丁语成分 ab- 与 solvere，以及这个词如今构成的固定短语。

normal.en: ab- means away and solvere means to loosen: absolute is loosened from limits.
normal.cn: ab- 表示「离开」，solvere 表示「松开」：absolute 就是从限制中松开。

normal.en: The same root gives absolve and dissolve, all about loosening.
normal.cn: 同一词根还给出 absolve 与 dissolve，都与「松开」有关。

normal.en: Absolute zero is the zero nature sets, not the zero of a chosen scale.
normal.cn: 绝对零度是自然设定的零，而不是所选温标上的零。

normal.en: An absolute monarch answers to no law above himself.
normal.cn: 专制的君主不受任何更高法律的约束。

normal.en: The absolute construction carries its own subject and stands apart from the main clause.
normal.cn: 独立结构自带主语，独立于主句之外。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler with no marks: it measures nothing against another rod, so it is absolute.
abstract.cn: 想象一把没有刻度的尺子：它不靠另一根尺来量，所以是绝对的。

abstract.en: To be absolute is to have nothing outside oneself to lean on.
abstract.cn: 成为绝对，就是身外没有任何可以倚靠的东西。

abstract.en: The word began as set loose; freedom from conditions is what all eight senses share.
abstract.cn: 这个词起于「被松开」；八个义项共享的正是「不受条件约束」。

examples.en: The room fell into absolute silence when she began to speak.

examples.en: She has absolute confidence in her own judgement.

sensesIntro.en: Every sense of absolute removes a limit: a complete thing, an unchecked ruler, a truth without comparison, a zero fixed by nature, a measured distance, a detached phrase, a fixed threshold, or a reality depending on nothing.
sensesIntro.cn: absolute 的每个义项都在去掉一层限制：完整的事物、不受制约的统治者、无需比较的真理、由自然确定的零、被量出的距离、脱离主句的短语、固定的门槛，以及不依赖他物的实在。

definition_zh: 完全地；绝对地；确实；当然（表示完全同意）
definition_en: completely and without any limit, or used to agree strongly or to emphasize that something is true
core_image: 一个被拧到尽头的旋钮，没有中间档
scene: 朋友问她愿不愿意来帮忙搬家，她连一秒都没犹豫就点头。When I asked if she would help, she said absolutely.
sceneCN: 这里 absolutely 是口语中表示完全同意（第 5 个义项：完全赞同）；句意为我问她愿不愿意帮忙，她说当然。

pos.zh: 完全地；绝对地；确实；当然

derivatives.zh: 本词的形容词形式，义为「绝对的；完全的；专制的」
由 absolute 加 -ness 构成，义为「绝对性；完全」
由 absolute 加 -ism 构成，义为「专制主义；绝对主义」

senses.title: To an extreme degree
senses.definition: used before an adjective to emphasize that a quality is present to an extreme degree
senses.definitionCN: 用于形容词前，强调某种性质达到极高程度
senses.example: The soup was absolutely delicious.
senses.exampleCN: 这汤好喝极了。
senses.why: Something absolute is complete; placed before an adjective, that completeness becomes the very top of a scale.
senses.whyCN: 绝对的东西是完整的；把它放到形容词前面，那种完整就变成了一把尺子的顶端，所以是「极其」。

senses.title: Completely, with nothing left out
senses.definition: entirely, so that no part is excluded or only partly affected
senses.definitionCN: 整体地，没有任何部分被排除或只受到部分影响
senses.example: The old bridge was absolutely destroyed by the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老桥被洪水彻底冲毁了。
senses.why: The sense of being loosened from limits reappears here as nothing held back: the whole of the thing is affected.
senses.whyCN: 「从限制中松开」的意思在这里表现为「没有任何保留」：整个事物都受到了影响。

senses.title: With complete certainty
senses.definition: used with words such as certain or sure to mean that there is no doubt at all
senses.definitionCN: 与 certain、sure 等词连用，表示毫无疑义
senses.example: I am absolutely certain that I locked the door.
senses.exampleCN: 我十分确定自己锁了门。
senses.why: A judgement free from conditions admits no exception, so certainty hardens into absolute certainty.
senses.whyCN: 一个不受条件约束的判断不容许例外，于是「确定」被加固成「确定无疑」。

senses.title: Emphasizing that something is true
senses.definition: used to stress that what is being said is true, as in absolutely right
senses.definitionCN: 用于强调所说的话是真的，如 absolutely right
senses.example: You are absolutely right about the timetable.
senses.exampleCN: 关于时间表，你完全说得对。
senses.why: The adverb closes the door on any partly: a thing that is absolute cannot be only half true.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词堵住了「部分成立」的余地：绝对的东西不可能只对一半。

senses.title: Complete agreement in conversation
senses.definition: used alone as a reply to mean yes, very strongly, or I agree completely
senses.definitionCN: 单独用作答语，表示非常肯定地说「是」或「我完全同意」
senses.example: Would you like to come along? Absolutely!
senses.exampleCN: 你想一起来吗？当然！
senses.why: Agreeing completely is the conversational shape of an absolute judgement: no reservation is left.
senses.whyCN: 完全同意是「绝对判断」在对话里的形态：没有留下任何保留。

senses.title: Absolutely not: a flat refusal
senses.definition: in the phrase absolutely not, a firm and complete refusal
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 absolutely not，表示坚决而彻底的拒绝
senses.example: Can I borrow the car tonight? Absolutely not.
senses.exampleCN: 今晚我能借用汽车吗？绝对不行。
senses.why: If yes can be absolute, so can no; the same emphasis serves refusal as well as agreement.
senses.whyCN: 既然「是」可以是绝对的，「不」也可以是；同一种强调既用于赞同，也用于拒绝。

senses.title: In an unlimited or despotic way
senses.definition: in a way that has no legal or practical limit, as of a ruler who governs absolutely
senses.definitionCN: 指不受法律或实际限制地，如君主专制地统治
senses.example: The dynasty ruled absolutely for almost three hundred years.
senses.exampleCN: 这个王朝专制统治了近三百年。
senses.why: The oldest Latin sense survives here without metaphor: power that has been loosened from every check.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的拉丁义项在这里不加比喻地保留下来：权力已经从一切制约中松开。

senses.title: Unconditionally, in legal use
senses.definition: in law, granted or held with no condition attached and no limit in time
senses.definitionCN: 在法律中，指授予或持有时不附带条件、也不受时间限制
senses.example: The land was granted to the family absolutely.
senses.exampleCN: 这块土地被无条件地授予了这个家族。
senses.why: Law keeps the technical core of the word: a title held absolutely is one freed from conditions and reversals.
senses.whyCN: 法律保留了这个词的技术核心：绝对保有的所有权，就是从条件与追夺中解放出来的所有权。

intro.en: Absolutely is the adjective absolute with the ordinary English adverb ending, and its history is the history of that Latin participle.
intro.cn: absolutely 是形容词 absolute 加上英语常见副词词尾，它的历史就是那个拉丁分词的历史。

items.en: Solvere meant to loosen or untie; English solve and solution descend from it.
items.cn: solvere 意为「松开、解开」，英语 solve 与 solution 都源自它。

items.en: Absolvere, from ab- plus solvere, gave the participle absolutus, meaning loosened, complete or unrestricted.
items.cn: ab- 加 solvere 构成 absolvere，其过去分词 absolutus 意为「被松开的、完整的、不受限制的」。

items.en: Old French absolut passed the adjective into English, where it kept the sense of complete and unconditional.
items.cn: 古法语 absolut 把这个形容词带入英语，保留了「完整、无条件」的意思。

items.en: The adverb was formed by adding -ly to absolute; both words are recorded in English in the late Middle Ages.
items.cn: 副词由 absolute 加 -ly 构成；两个词在中世纪晚期都已见于英语。

items.en: Use as a one-word agreement is a modern conversational development; the older senses concern degree, certainty, power and law.
items.cn: 单独用作答语表示同意是较晚出现的口语发展；较早的义项涉及程度、确定性、权力与法律。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the absolute family; the near-meaning group holds adverbs of completeness and of certainty.
note.cn: 形近组收 absolute 这一族词；近义组收表示「完全」与「确定」的副词。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning complete or unconditional, from which the adverb is formed.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「完全的、无条件的」，副词正是由它构成。

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of being complete or unlimited.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「绝对性、完全」。

entries.definition: The political system in which one ruler holds unlimited power.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「专制主义、绝对主义」。

entries.definition: To declare someone free of blame, from the same Latin absolvere.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「赦免、宣告无罪」，与 absolute 同出拉丁语 absolvere。

entries.definition: In every part; it stresses wholeness rather than emphasis or agreement.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「完全地」，强调完整，而不含强调或赞同的语气。

entries.definition: Entirely; close in meaning but more informal in speech.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「完全地」，意思接近，但口语色彩更强。

entries.definition: Completely, usually with a strong or negative word.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「彻底地」，通常与强烈或负面的词连用。

entries.definition: Wholly; it often appears with words of agreement or difference.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「完全地」，常用于表示同意或差异的语境。

entries.definition: Used to agree or to say something is sure, without the force of absolutely.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「当然、肯定」，语气不如 absolutely 强。

normalIntro.en: The hooks work from the adjective absolute, its Latin core, and the fixed pairs the adverb appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想从形容词 absolute、它的拉丁语核心，以及这个副词实际出现的固定搭配出发。

normal.en: Add -ly to absolute: the completeness becomes a way of acting.
normal.cn: 在 absolute 后加 -ly：那种「完整」变成了一种做事方式。

normal.en: ab- away plus solvere loosen: absolutely means with no limit left.
normal.cn: ab- 表「离开」，solvere 表「松开」：absolutely 就是没有留下任何限制。

normal.en: Absolutely right and absolutely certain are fixed, natural pairs.
normal.cn: absolutely right 与 absolutely certain 是固定而自然的搭配。

normal.en: One word as a reply, absolutely, means yes with no reservation.
normal.cn: 单独一个 absolutely 作回答，表示毫无保留的「是」。

normal.en: Absolutely not is the same force turned into refusal.
normal.cn: absolutely not 是把同样的力度转向拒绝。

abstract.en: Picture a dial with only one setting, all the way, and that is what absolutely adds to a word.
abstract.cn: 想象一个只有一个档位的旋钮，转到底，这正是 absolutely 给一个词加上的东西。

abstract.en: It does not soften and it does not hedge; it closes the space where partly could live.
abstract.cn: 它不软化、也不含糊；它把「部分」可能藏身的空间关上了。

abstract.en: The same word can say yes entirely or no entirely, because completeness has no direction.
abstract.cn: 同一个词可以说「完全是」，也可以说「完全不」，因为完整本身没有方向。

examples.en: The soup was absolutely delicious.
examples.cn: 这汤好喝极了。

examples.en: I am absolutely certain that I locked the door.
examples.cn: 我十分确定自己锁了门。

examples.en: Would you like to come along? Absolutely!
examples.cn: 你想一起来吗？当然！

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿布索卢特利」——旋钮一拧到底，不留余地：完全、绝对。

root: absolute 加副词后缀 -ly 构成；absolute 来自拉丁语 absolutus（absolvere 的过去分词），ab-「离开」+ solvere「松开」，字面义为「被松开、不受限制」，副词义即「完全地、无条件地」。

sensesIntro.en: Absolutely always means all the way: all the way up a scale, all of a thing, all of one's certainty, all of one's agreement or refusal, all of a ruler's power, or all of a legal title.
sensesIntro.cn: absolutely 始终表示「到底」：把一个尺度推到顶、把一件事做全、把确定性用满、把赞同或拒绝说到底、把权力用到没有边界、把产权给到无条件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dial pushed all the way to the end, with no setting in between.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个被拧到底的旋钮，中间没有别的档位。

branches.en: DEGREE: the top of a scale and the whole of a thing.
branches.cn: 程度线：尺子的顶端与事物的整体。

branches.en: TRUTH: certainty and emphasis that leave no room for partly.
branches.cn: 真实线：确定性，以及不给「部分」留余地的强调。

branches.en: CONVERSATION: full agreement and flat refusal.
branches.cn: 对话线：完全赞同与断然拒绝。

branches.en: POWER: ruling without any check.
branches.cn: 权力线：不受任何制约的统治。

branches.en: LAW: holding title with no condition attached.
branches.cn: 法律线：不附带任何条件的所有权。

intro.en: Absolutely is a Latin-rooted adjective plus the everyday adverb ending, so its parts are shared with hundreds of English words.
intro.cn: absolutely 是一个拉丁词根的形容词加上常见副词词尾，它各部分与成百上千个英语词共享。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verbs and participle behind the word are all recorded, so only the deeper root is a reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词背后的拉丁动词与分词都有文献记录，只有更早的词根属于重构。

items.exampleCN: 它在许多动词中标记分离。

items.example: Solvere is the core of the family.
items.exampleCN: solvere 是这一词族的核心。
它也产生了英语 absolve。

items.example: The participle became absolute in English.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词在英语里变成 absolute。

items.exampleCN: 这位科学家要求绝对准确。

items.example: The two versions are absolutely different.
items.exampleCN: 这两个版本完全不同。

latinEntries.meaning: to loosen from, set free, finish

latinEntries.meaningCN: 被松开的；不受限制的；完整的

derivatives.zh: 绝对的；完全的
绝对性；完全
专制主义；绝对主义

definition_zh: 吸收（液体、气体、光热声）；吸收（知识、信息）；慢慢消化（消息）；消纳（成本、冲击）；缓冲（震动）；合并、吞并；使全神贯注
definition_en: to take something inward and keep it inside, whether a liquid, energy, knowledge, a cost or a person's whole attention
core_image: 一块干海绵按进水里，水从细孔钻进去，海绵一点点变沉
scene: 厨房台面上打翻了一杯牛奶，抹布往上一按，白色很快就淡了。The sponge absorbed the spilled milk in a few seconds.
sceneCN: 这里的 absorbed 是「吸收液体」（第 1 个义项：把液体吸入材料内部）；句意为海绵几秒钟就把洒出来的牛奶吸干了。画面里有台面、抹布和那摊牛奶。

pos.zh: 吸收（液体、气体、光热、声音）；吸收（知识）；消纳（成本）；合并；使专注

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「吸收、专注」
由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「能吸收的」
由 absorbent 加名词后缀构成，义为「吸收能力」
由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「引人入胜的」

senses.title: To soak up a liquid or gas
senses.definition: to take a liquid, gas or other substance in through the surface and hold it inside
senses.definitionCN: 通过表面把液体、气体等物质吸进去并留在内部
senses.example: The sponge absorbed the spilled milk in a few seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 海绵几秒钟就把洒出来的牛奶吸干了。
senses.why: Latin sorbere meant to suck in, and the core image is a dry material pulling water into its holes.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 sorbere 意为「吸入」，核心意象是干燥的材料把水吸进自己的细孔里，所以最具体的义项就是吸水。

senses.title: To take in heat, light or sound
senses.definition: to take in energy such as heat, light or sound rather than reflecting it or letting it pass through
senses.definitionCN: 吸收热、光、声等能量，而不是把它反射出去或让它透过去
senses.example: Dark fabric absorbs more heat than a white shirt does.
senses.exampleCN: 深色布料比白衬衫吸收更多热量。
senses.why: The same inward pull is applied to energy: what hits the surface does not bounce back but stays inside it.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「往里吸」的动作被用到能量上：碰到表面的东西没有弹回去，而是留在了里面。

senses.title: To take in knowledge and ideas
senses.definition: to learn and remember information, skills or ideas so that they become part of what one knows
senses.definitionCN: 学习和记住信息、技能或观念，使它们成为自己知识的一部分
senses.example: Young children absorb new sounds and words very quickly.
senses.exampleCN: 幼儿吸收新的语音和词汇非常快。
senses.why: The mind is pictured as the sponge: knowledge goes in like water, stays inside, and is slowly used.
senses.whyCN: 心智被想象成海绵：知识像水一样进去、留在里面，再慢慢被取用，因此「吸收知识」沿用同一个动作。

senses.title: To digest surprising news
senses.definition: to take in a piece of news or an experience and gradually understand what it means
senses.definitionCN: 接受一条消息或一段经历，并逐渐明白它意味着什么
senses.example: She sat by the window, quietly absorbing what the doctor had said.
senses.exampleCN: 她坐在窗边，默默消化医生刚才说的话。
senses.why: Information is first swallowed whole and only later understood, the same delay between taking water in and the material turning wet.
senses.whyCN: 信息先被整个吞下，之后才被理解；这和水被吸进去、材料随后才变湿是同一个有先后次序的过程。

senses.title: To carry a cost or loss
senses.definition: to bear an extra cost, loss or burden without collapsing and without passing it on to others
senses.definitionCN: 承担额外的成本、损失或负担，既不会垮掉，也不把它转给别人
senses.example: Large chains can absorb rising rent better than small shops.
senses.exampleCN: 大型连锁店比小店更能消纳上涨的租金。
senses.why: A cost is poured in like water; if the container is large enough it holds the whole amount, so absorb means to take the burden into oneself.
senses.whyCN: 成本像水一样被倒进来；容器够大就能全部装下，于是 absorb 从「装得下」变成「把负担收进自己这里」。

senses.title: To soften the force of a blow
senses.definition: to reduce the force of a shock, blow or sudden change so that its effect is less severe
senses.definitionCN: 减弱撞击、打击或突变的力量，使其影响不那么严重
senses.example: The thick carpet absorbed the shock of the fall.
senses.exampleCN: 厚厚的地毯缓冲了摔倒时的冲击。
senses.why: The energy of a blow is pulled into the material instead of reaching the body, which is the core image acting on force rather than on water.
senses.whyCN: 撞击的能量被材料吸走，传不到人身上；这是核心意象作用在「力」而不是「水」上的结果。

senses.title: To take over a smaller organization
senses.definition: to make a smaller company, group or area become part of a larger one
senses.definitionCN: 使较小的公司、团体或地区成为更大整体的一部分
senses.example: The small studio was absorbed into a giant media group.
senses.exampleCN: 这家小工作室被一家大型传媒集团吞并了。
senses.why: A small body is drawn inside a bigger one and loses its own outline, just as the water loses its shape inside the sponge.
senses.whyCN: 小机构被吸进更大的整体里，失去了自己的轮廓，就像水在海绵里失去形状一样。

senses.title: To hold someone's attention completely
senses.definition: to occupy someone's attention so fully that little else is noticed
senses.definitionCN: 完全占据某人的注意力，使他几乎注意不到别的事
senses.example: He was so absorbed in the game that he missed his stop.
senses.exampleCN: 他太专注于比赛，错过了下车的站。
senses.why: Attention is the last thing that gets sucked in: it is pulled entirely into one object, leaving no room outside.
senses.whyCN: 注意力是最后被吸走的东西：它被整个吸进一件事里，外面再也留不下位置，于是有了「全神贯注」。

intro.en: Absorb comes straight from Latin, and the whole family keeps the image of something being sucked inward.
intro.cn: absorb 直接来自拉丁语，整个词族都保留「被往里吸」的意象。

items.en: Sorbere meant 'to suck in, swallow'. Its deeper Indo-European origin is uncertain and usually described as reconstructed.
items.cn: sorbere 意为「吸入、吞咽」；它更早的印欧语来源不确定，通常只能写作重构形式。

items.en: The prefix ab- 'away, off' plus sorbere formed absorbere, 'to swallow up, suck in'. The force of the prefix is explained in more than one way.
items.cn: 前缀 ab-「离开」与 sorbere 合成 absorbere，意为「吞没、吸入」；关于这个前缀的具体作用，各家解释并不完全一致。

items.en: The action noun absorptio 'a swallowing up' is recorded, and it is the source of the English noun absorption.
items.cn: 动作名词 absorptio「吞没」有文献记录，它是英语名词 absorption 的来源。

items.en: The verb reached English through Middle French absorber or directly from the Latin form; the two routes are hard to separate.
items.cn: 这个动词经中古法语 absorber 进入英语，也可能直接来自拉丁语形式；两条路径不易截然分开。

items.en: The verb is recorded in the fifteenth century with the literal sense of taking in liquid; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 动词在十五世纪有记录，最初是「吸入液体」的字面义；确切首见年代不确定。

note.en: The look-alike group is built on the Latin root sorb-; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of taking something in, each with a different limit.
note.cn: 形近组建立在拉丁词根 sorb- 上；近义组收「把东西收进来」的动词，各自的适用范围不同。

entries.definition: The noun for the process of taking something in, or for complete attention to one thing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「吸收、专注」，指吸入的过程或对一件事的完全投入。

entries.definition: An adjective for a material that can take in liquid easily.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「能吸收的」，指容易吸入液体的材料。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning so interesting that it takes up all your attention.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「引人入胜的」，指有趣到占满注意力的。

entries.definition: A frozen dessert of fruit and sugar; it has nothing to do with sucking in.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「雪葩、水果冰沙」；只是拼写相近，词源不同，与「吸入」无关。

entries.definition: To make something completely wet by leaving it in liquid for a while.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「浸泡、使湿透」，强调把东西放在液体里一段时间，比 absorb 更偏「变湿」。

entries.definition: To take in and fully integrate information, ideas or people into a larger whole.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「同化、消化吸收」，语气正式，强调吸收之后融入整体。

entries.definition: To break down food, or to think about information until you understand it.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「消化」，既指消化食物，也指把信息想明白，与「消化消息」一义最近。

entries.definition: To attract and hold someone's attention strongly, often by charm.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「迷住、使着迷」，只对应「全神贯注」一义，靠魅力而非好奇心。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded Latin verb and the phrases the word really appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用有文献记录的拉丁动词，以及这个词真实出现的搭配。

normal.en: sorbere is to suck in: absorb is the same pull, seen from the material's side.
normal.cn: sorbere 意为「吸入」：absorb 就是同一个「吸」的动作，从材料这一侧看过去。

normal.en: ab- plus sorbere gives the Latin verb absorbere, to swallow up.
normal.cn: ab- 加 sorbere 构成拉丁动词 absorbere，意为「吞没」。

normal.en: A sponge and a paper towel are absorbent; a raincoat is not.
normal.cn: 海绵和纸巾是 absorbent（会吸水的），雨衣则不是。

normal.en: Learn the pair absorb and absorption together: the verb and its noun.
normal.cn: 把 absorb 和 absorption 成对记：一个动词，一个名词。

normal.en: be absorbed in a book is literally being pulled inside the book.
normal.cn: be absorbed in a book 字面上就是被拉进书里去了。

abstract.en: Think of a dry cloth dropped in a puddle: the water disappears into it and the cloth grows heavy.
abstract.cn: 想象一块干布掉进水洼：水消失了，布变沉了，这就是 absorb 的画面。

abstract.en: Whatever is absorbed is not gone; it is inside, waiting to be used.
abstract.cn: 被吸收的东西并没有消失，它只是进到里面去了，等着被使用。

abstract.en: A big firm absorbs a cost the way a big container absorbs water: the level rises, but nothing spills.
abstract.cn: 大公司消纳成本，就像大容器装水：水位升高，但不会溢出来。

examples.en: This towel absorbs water much faster than the old one.
examples.cn: 这条毛巾比旧的那条吸水快得多。

examples.en: She was so absorbed in her book that she did not hear the doorbell.
examples.cn: 她看书看得太入神，没听见门铃。

examples.en: The small firm was absorbed into a much larger group last year.
examples.cn: 这家小公司去年被一个规模大得多的集团吞并了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「啊不吸」——嘴上说不吸，海绵一按下去，水全进去了：吸收。

root: 拉丁语 absorbere「吞没、吸入」，由 ab-「离开、向外」与 sorbere「吸、吞」构成；sorbere 更早的印欧语来源不确定，一般只写作重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses picture one inward pull: liquid, energy, knowledge, news, cost, shock, a smaller company or a person's attention is taken inside something larger.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在画同一个「往里吸」的动作：液体、能量、知识、消息、成本、冲击、较小的机构或某人的注意力，被收进一个更大的东西里面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dry sponge is pressed onto a spill and the water disappears inside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：干海绵按在洒出的水上，水消失在海绵内部。

branches.en: THE MATERIAL: a liquid or gas enters a solid and stays there.
branches.cn: 材料线：液体或气体进入固体并留在里面。

branches.en: THE ENERGY: heat, light and sound are taken in instead of reflected.
branches.cn: 能量线：热、光、声被收进去，而不是反射出去。

branches.en: THE MIND: knowledge is stored, and surprising news is swallowed before it is understood.
branches.cn: 心智线：知识被储存，意外的消息先被吞下、再被理解。

branches.en: THE BURDEN: a cost is carried inside and a blow has its force taken away.
branches.cn: 负担线：成本被装进内部，撞击的力量被卸掉。

branches.en: THE WHOLE: a smaller body is drawn into a larger one, and attention is drawn into one object.
branches.cn: 整体线：小机构被吸进更大的整体，注意力被吸进单一对象。

intro.en: Absorb is a Latin verb used whole in English, with ordinary suffixes building the rest of the family.
intro.cn: absorb 是整体借入英语的拉丁动词，其余词族由普通后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Sorbere, absorbere and absorptio are all recorded Latin forms, so only the older Indo-European layer is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: sorbere、absorbere 与 absorptio 都是有文献记录的拉丁语形式，只有更早的印欧语层属于重构。

items.example: The prefix marks something moving away from its place.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标示某物离开原处。

items.example: The verb supplies the inward pull of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供这个词「往里吸」的动作。

items.example: The Latin verb is the direct source of absorb.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词是 absorb 的直接来源。
这个名词是英语 absorption 的基础。
它构成 absorption。
它构成 absorbent。
它构成 absorbency。
它构成 absorbing。

items.example: The same root appears in sorption.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根也出现在 sorption 中。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「吸收、专注」
由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「能吸收的」
由 absorbent 加名词后缀构成，义为「吸收能力」
由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「引人入胜的」

definition_zh: 滥用（权力、制度、药物）；虐待；辱骂；侵害行为；糟蹋、过度使用；辜负（信任）
definition_en: to use something or someone in a wrong, harmful or excessive way, or such wrong use itself
core_image: 一把本该切菜的刀被拿去砍门，刃口卷了，手也划破了
scene: 车间里那台机器早就该保养了，主管却一直让人超负荷地开。The manager was accused of abusing his power.
sceneCN: 这里的 abusing 是「滥用职权」（第 1 个义项：把权力用在不当的地方）；句意为主管被指滥用权力。画面里有老旧的机器和满脸不服的工人。

pos.zh: 名词：滥用；虐待；辱骂；侵害行为
动词：滥用；虐待；辱骂；糟蹋

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「辱骂的；虐待的；滥用的」
由本词加施动后缀构成，义为「施虐者；滥用者」
由 abusive 加副词后缀构成，义为「辱骂地；虐待地」
由 abusive 加名词后缀构成，义为「辱骂性；虐待性」

senses.title: Misuse of power or authority
senses.definition: the use of power or official authority for the wrong purpose or beyond its proper limits
senses.definitionCN: 把权力或职务上的权限用于错误目的，或超出应有的限度
senses.example: The manager was accused of abusing his power.
senses.exampleCN: 这名主管被指滥用权力。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to use something away from its proper use; power is the first thing people are tempted to use this way.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词本义是「把东西用到偏离正当用途的地方」；权力正是人们最容易这样使用的东西，所以它成了第一个义项。

senses.title: Harmful use of drugs or alcohol
senses.definition: the use of drugs, alcohol or other substances in a way that harms the user
senses.definitionCN: 以伤害使用者的方式服用药物、酒精等物质
senses.example: Drug abuse among teenagers has fallen in recent years.
senses.exampleCN: 近年来青少年药物滥用有所减少。
senses.why: A substance is meant to heal or give pleasure in measure; using it outside that measure turns a tool into harm, the same wrong use as before.
senses.whyCN: 药物本来是用来治病或适量取乐的；一旦超出这个度量，工具就变成伤害，这仍是同一个「用错了」的动作。

senses.title: Cruel treatment of a person or animal
senses.definition: cruel or violent treatment of a person or animal, especially one who cannot defend himself or herself
senses.definitionCN: 残忍或暴力地对待人或动物，尤指无法自我保护的弱者
senses.example: The charity runs a hotline for reports of child abuse.
senses.exampleCN: 这家慈善机构设有举报虐待儿童的热线。
senses.why: When the thing being used is a living person, wrong use stops being a metaphor: the person is treated as an object, and that is abuse.
senses.whyCN: 当被「使用」的对象是活人时，「用错」不再是比喻：人被当成物件来对待，这就是虐待。

senses.title: Insulting words aimed at someone
senses.definition: spoken words that insult, threaten or humiliate someone repeatedly
senses.definitionCN: 反复用来侮辱、威胁或羞辱某人的话语
senses.example: Shouting is one thing, but verbal abuse is not part of the job.
senses.exampleCN: 大声说话是一回事，但言语辱骂不属于工作内容。
senses.why: Speech is also a tool; turned against a person it wounds rather than works, so the same word covers hurtful language.
senses.whyCN: 语言也是一种工具；当它被掉转过来对着人，就不再做事而只造成伤害，于是同一个词也指伤人的话。

senses.title: Exploiting a system or rule
senses.definition: the dishonest use of a system, procedure or rule to gain an advantage it was not meant to give
senses.definitionCN: 不正当地利用制度、程序或规则，取得它本不该给的便利
senses.example: The report found widespread abuse of the visa system.
senses.exampleCN: 报告发现签证制度被广泛钻空子。
senses.why: Systems are tools too; using their gaps instead of their purpose is misuse at the scale of an institution.
senses.whyCN: 制度同样是工具；利用它的缝隙而不是它的用途，就是「用错」在机构层面的表现。

senses.title: To damage something by rough use
senses.definition: to damage equipment, a body or a place by using it too roughly or too often
senses.definitionCN: 因使用过于粗暴或频繁而损坏设备、身体或场所
senses.example: He abused the old truck until the engine finally gave out.
senses.exampleCN: 他把那辆旧卡车往死里用，最后发动机彻底坏了。
senses.why: Here the damage is visible: a tool used past its limits wears out, and the word names the wearing rather than the intention.
senses.whyCN: 这里的损坏看得见：工具被用到超出限度就会磨损，这个词于是指磨损本身，而不只是意图。

senses.title: A wrongful act, in the plural
senses.definition: in the plural, cruel or unjust acts, especially those that violate people's rights
senses.definitionCN: 用复数形式，指残忍或不公正的行为，尤指侵犯人权的行为
senses.example: The commission documented human rights abuses in the region.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会记录了该地区的侵犯人权行为。
senses.why: Each single misuse is an event; counted together they become a record of wrongs, which is why the plural names a pattern of harm.
senses.whyCN: 每一次滥用都是一件事；把它们合起来数，就成了一份罪错清单，所以复数形式指的是成串的侵害。

senses.title: To betray the trust placed in you
senses.definition: to take advantage of someone's trust, kindness or hospitality for one's own benefit
senses.definitionCN: 利用别人的信任、善意或款待来为自己谋利
senses.example: She felt he had abused her trust in the worst possible way.
senses.exampleCN: 她觉得他以最糟糕的方式辜负了她的信任。
senses.why: Trust is the most invisible thing one person lends another; using it as a means to an end is misuse in its most personal form.
senses.whyCN: 信任是一个人借给另一个人最无形的东西；把它当成手段来用，就是「用错」最私人化的一种形态。

intro.en: Abuse goes back to a Latin verb that simply means to use something wrongly, and every sense keeps that shape.
intro.cn: abuse 可追到拉丁语中一个意为「用错」的动词，所有义项都保持着这个形状。

items.en: Uti meant 'to use, make use of'. It is well recorded, and it is also the source of the English word use through Latin usus.
items.cn: uti 意为「使用、利用」，有明确记录；它经由拉丁语 usus 也是英语 use 的来源。

items.en: Ab- 'away from' plus uti formed abuti, 'to misuse, use up'. The prefix marks use that has turned away from the proper purpose.
items.cn: ab-「离开」与 uti 构成 abuti，意为「误用、用尽」；这个前缀标示用法偏离了正当目的。

items.en: The past participle abusus served both as a noun 'misuse' and as the participle behind the adjective abusivus.
items.cn: 过去分词 abusus 既作名词表示「误用」，也是形容词 abusivus 的分词基础。

items.en: Old French abuser carried both the sense of misusing a thing and of deceiving a person, and English took the word in that double shape.
items.cn: 古法语 abuser 同时带有「误用某物」和「欺骗某人」两种意思，英语正是以这双重的面貌借入的。

items.en: The noun is recorded in the fourteenth century and the verb in the following one; the exact first dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 名词在十四世纪有记录，动词晚一个世纪出现；确切首见年代不确定。

note.en: The look-alike group is the Latin uti family; the near-meaning group names wrong use, cruel treatment and insult with different degrees of force.
note.cn: 形近组是拉丁语 uti 词族；近义组列出「用错」「苛待」与「侮辱」，力度各不相同。

entries.definition: An adjective describing words or treatment that are cruel, insulting or harmful.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「辱骂的、虐待的、滥用的」，描述伤人的言语或对待。

entries.definition: A person who treats someone cruelly or uses something wrongly.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「施虐者、滥用者」，指苛待他人或不当使用某物的人。

entries.definition: The adverb, meaning in a cruel or insulting manner.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「辱骂地、虐待地」，由 abusive 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: To free someone from a mistaken belief; the prefix dis- reverses the idea of using wrongly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使醒悟、纠正……的错误想法」，与 abuse 同根，前缀 dis- 表示「解除」。

entries.definition: The wrong or careless use of something, especially an object or a system.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「误用、滥用」，多指对物品或制度的错误使用，不含虐待义。

entries.definition: To treat a person or animal badly, especially over a period of time.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「苛待、虐待」，专指对人的恶劣对待，与「滥用权力」无关。

entries.definition: To use someone or something unfairly for your own gain.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「剥削、利用」，强调为自己获利而不公平地使用他人。

entries.definition: To say something rude that offends someone; a single act, unlike repeated verbal abuse.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或名词，义为「侮辱」，通常指一次性的冒犯，不像 verbal abuse 那样反复发生。

normalIntro.en: These hooks are built on the real Latin pair ab- and uti, and on the fixed phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子建立在真实的拉丁语组合 ab- 与 uti 上，并使用这个词的固定搭配。

normal.en: uti is to use, and ab- turns use away from its purpose: abuse is use in the wrong direction.
normal.cn: uti 是「使用」，ab- 把使用从正当目的上转开：abuse 就是「用错了方向」。

normal.en: abuse of power is the phrase used in news reports about officials.
normal.cn: abuse of power 是新闻报道官员问题时常用的说法。

normal.en: drug abuse names the harmful use of a substance, not the substance itself.
normal.cn: drug abuse 指的是对物质的有害使用，而不是物质本身。

normal.en: child abuse and elder abuse both protect people who cannot defend themselves.
normal.cn: child abuse 与 elder abuse 都指向无法自我保护的弱者。

normal.en: Keep the pair abuse and abusive together: the act and the adjective that describes it.
normal.cn: 把 abuse 和 abusive 成对记：一个是行为，一个是形容这种行为的形容词。

abstract.en: Picture a kitchen knife used to pry open a door: the blade is ruined and the hand is cut.
abstract.cn: 想象一把菜刀被拿去撬门：刀刃毁了，手也划破了。

abstract.en: The word always asks what a thing is for, and then shows it being used against that purpose.
abstract.cn: 这个词始终先问「这东西是干什么用的」，再展示它被用到了相反的方向。

abstract.en: Abuse leaves two marks: the tool is worn out and the person on the other side is hurt.
abstract.cn: 滥用会留下两道痕迹：工具被磨损，另一边的人受了伤。

examples.en: The report describes several abuses of power inside the department.
examples.cn: 报告描述了该部门内部的多起滥用权力行为。

examples.en: She never abused her position to get special treatment.
examples.cn: 她从未滥用职位来获取特殊待遇。

examples.en: Neighbours reported the noise, but what worried them more was the verbal abuse.
examples.cn: 邻居们报告了噪音，但更让他们担心的是那些辱骂。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额必优使」——把好东西用歪了，就是不当地使：滥用。

root: 拉丁语 abuti「误用、用尽」，由 ab-「离开」与 uti「使用」构成；其过去分词 abusus 兼作名词「误用」，英语经古法语 abuser 借入。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense of abuse is a tool turned against its purpose: power, a substance, a person, speech, a system, a machine, a right or a trust.
sensesIntro.cn: abuse 的每个义项都是「工具被掉转过来反对它本来的用途」：权力、物质、人、言语、制度、机器、权利或信任。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tool meant for one job is used for another and is damaged in the process.
core.cn: 核心意象：本该干一件事的工具被拿去干别的，并在这个过程中被损坏。

branches.en: THE PUBLIC SPHERE: power and rules are steered toward private gain.
branches.cn: 公共领域线：权力与规则被引向私利。

branches.en: THE BODY: a healing substance is taken past its measure and turns harmful.
branches.cn: 身体线：治病的物质被用到超过度量，反过来造成伤害。

branches.en: THE PERSON: a human being is treated as an object, or another person's trust is spent.
branches.cn: 人身线：人被当成物件对待，或别人的信任被花掉。

branches.en: THE RECORD: insults and wrongs pile up into a pattern that can be counted.
branches.cn: 记录线：辱骂与侵害累积成一种可以计数的模式。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: rough use wears a machine down until it fails.
branches.cn: 器物线：粗暴使用把机器磨损到报废。

intro.en: Abuse is a Latin verb compound, and its English family is formed with common adjective and noun suffixes.
intro.cn: abuse 是拉丁语动词复合体，其英语词族由常见的形容词与名词后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Uti, abuti and abusus are recorded Latin forms; they also stand behind the everyday English word use.
latinIntro.cn: uti、abuti 与 abusus 都是有记录的拉丁语形式，它们也是日常英语 use 的后盾。

items.example: The prefix marks a turning away from the proper purpose.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标示偏离正当目的。

items.example: The verb is the using root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是这一词族中表示「使用」的词根。

items.example: The Latin verb is the direct source of abuse.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词是 abuse 的直接来源。

items.example: The participle also feeds the adjective abusive.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词也滋养了形容词 abusive。
它构成 abusive。
它构成 abusively。
它构成 abuser。
它构成 abusiveness。

items.example: It forms disabuse, to free from a false belief.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 disabuse，意为使摆脱错误想法。

由本词加施动后缀构成，义为「施虐者；滥用者」

definition_zh: 学术的；学业的；纯理论的；学院派的；普通学科的；以学术见长的；大学教师、学者
definition_en: relating to study, research and teaching at a university, or existing only in theory rather than in practice
core_image: 深夜图书馆的一张桌子，一摞书、一支笔和一盏不肯关的台灯
scene: 开学第一周，宿舍楼下的公告栏贴满了课程和考试安排。The academic year begins in early September.
sceneCN: 这里的 academic 是「学业的、学校的」（第 2 个义项：与学校学习安排有关）；句意为学年在九月初开始。画面里有公告栏、课程表和刚返校的学生。

pos.zh: 形容词：学术的；学业的；纯理论的；学院派的
名词：大学教师；学者

collocations.zh: 纯理论的；与实际无关的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加副词后缀构成，义为「学业上；学术上」
同源名词，义为「学院；研究院；专科学校」
由本词加表示人的后缀构成，义为「院士；学会会员」
同源名词，义为「学术界；学术圈」

senses.title: Relating to scholarly research
senses.definition: connected with serious study and research, especially at a university
senses.definitionCN: 与严肃的学习和研究有关，尤指大学里的研究
senses.example: Her academic research focuses on how children learn to read.
senses.exampleCN: 她的学术研究关注儿童如何学会阅读。
senses.why: The word starts from the name of the grove where Plato taught, so its first job is to mark whatever belongs to that world of study.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是柏拉图授课那片园子的名字，所以它最本职的工作就是标示「属于那个研究世界」的东西。

senses.title: Relating to school study and results
senses.titleCN: 学业的：与在校学习有关
senses.definition: connected with study, lessons and results at a school or college rather than with sport or social life
senses.definitionCN: 与学校或学院的课程、学习和成绩有关，而非体育或社交生活
senses.example: The academic year begins in early September.
senses.exampleCN: 学年在九月初开始。
senses.why: Once the word belongs to the school, it naturally covers the calendar and the marks of school life, not only research in a library.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词属于学校，它自然就覆盖了学校生活里的日历与分数，而不只是图书馆里的研究。

senses.title: Only true in theory, not in practice
senses.definition: of a question or argument, having no practical effect because the real decision has already been made
senses.definitionCN: 指问题或争论没有实际影响，因为真正的决定早已作出
senses.example: Whether the rule is fair is academic now that the contract is signed.
senses.exampleCN: 合同都签了，这条规则公不公平已经只是理论问题。
senses.why: What lives only in books has no weight in the street; a question with no practical consequence is confined to the study.
senses.whyCN: 只活在书里的东西在街上没有分量；一个不产生实际后果的问题，就被关进了书房。

senses.title: Dry and bookish in style
senses.titleCN: 学院派的：拘泥书本、脱离实际
senses.definition: of writing, art or thinking, correct but dry, showing more study than life
senses.definitionCN: 指写作、艺术或思想正确却干枯，书卷气多于生活感
senses.example: The film was praised abroad but called academic at home.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片在国外受好评，在本国却被说成学院派。
senses.why: The same belonging to the study becomes a criticism when the study is cut off from the street: too much book, too little life.
senses.whyCN: 同样一种「属于书房」的属性，一旦书房与街道隔绝，就变成批评：书太多，生活太少。

senses.title: A university teacher or researcher
senses.definition: a person who teaches or does research at a university, used as a countable noun
senses.definitionCN: 在大学任教或做研究的人，作可数名词使用
senses.example: She is a young academic with two books to her name.
senses.exampleCN: 她是一位年轻学者，已经出过两本书。
senses.why: From the adjective describing the world of study, English made a noun for a person who lives in that world.
senses.whyCN: 从描述「研究世界」的形容词出发，英语造出一个名词，专指生活在这个世界里的人。

senses.title: Of caps, gowns and ceremonies
senses.definition: relating to the traditional dress and ceremonies of universities, such as gowns and caps
senses.definitionCN: 与大学的传统服饰和仪式有关，如学位袍和学位帽
senses.example: The graduates posed for photos in full academic dress.
senses.exampleCN: 毕业生们穿着全套学位服拍照。
senses.why: The oldest sense of belonging to a place of learning survives most visibly in its costume, where the tradition is worn on the body.
senses.whyCN: 「属于学府」这一最古老的含义，最显眼地保存在服装上：传统被穿在了身上。

senses.title: Of subjects taught for their own sake
senses.definition: of school subjects such as history or physics, studied for knowledge rather than for a trade
senses.definitionCN: 指历史、物理这类以求知为目的、而非为职业训练设置的学科
senses.example: The school offers a strong academic curriculum alongside its sports program.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校除了体育项目，还提供扎实的学科课程。
senses.why: If a subject belongs to the world of study rather than to a workshop, it is called academic, and the word then labels a whole curriculum.
senses.whyCN: 一门科目如果属于研究的世界而不属于车间，就被称为 academic；这个词于是用来标示整类课程。

senses.title: Devoted to learning, of a person or family
senses.titleCN: 以读书治学见长的（人、家庭）
senses.definition: of a person, family or institution, valuing books, study and scholarship above practical or sporting success
senses.definitionCN: 指人、家庭或机构重视读书治学，胜过实际事务或体育成绩
senses.example: She grew up in an academic family where dinner talk was about books.
senses.exampleCN: 她在一个书香家庭长大，饭桌上的话题总是书。
senses.why: When a whole household is oriented toward study, the adjective stops describing a topic and starts describing a way of life.
senses.whyCN: 当一个家庭整体朝向读书治学，这个形容词就不再描述某个话题，而开始描述一种生活方式。

intro.en: Academic goes back to the name of the grove outside Athens where Plato taught, and from there to every school.
intro.cn: academic 可追到雅典城外柏拉图授课的那片园子的名字，再从那里走向一切学校。

items.en: Akademeia was the name of a grove and gymnasium near Athens, associated with the hero Akademos. The origin of the name itself is uncertain.
items.cn: Akademeia 是雅典附近一片园林与体育场的名字，与英雄 Akademos 有关；这个名称本身的来源不确定。

items.en: Akademikos meant 'of the Academy', the school Plato founded there; it described members and teachings of that circle.
items.cn: Akademikos 意为「学园的」，即柏拉图在此创办的学派；它形容该学派的成员与学说。

items.en: Latin academia named both the place and the philosophical school, and kept the word alive through learned writing.
items.cn: 拉丁语 academia 既指那个地方，也指那个哲学学派，并通过学术写作把词保存了下来。

items.en: English borrowed academy in the sixteenth century, and academic followed as the adjective for things belonging to it.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 academy，随后 academic 作为「属于它的」形容词出现。

items.en: In the twentieth century the adjective also became a noun for a university teacher, and gained its mildly critical sense of 'out of touch'.
items.cn: 二十世纪，这个形容词又变成指大学教师的名词，并获得「脱离实际」这一略带批评的义项。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Greek name behind the word; the near-meaning group holds words about study, theory and teaching.
note.cn: 形近组共享这个词背后的希腊名称；近义组收与学习、理论、教学有关的词。

entries.definition: A school or society for a special field, such as an art or military academy.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「学院、研究院、专科学校」，如艺术学院或军校。

entries.definition: The world of universities and research, taken as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「学术界、学术圈」，指大学与研究构成的整体世界。

entries.definition: A member of a learned academy or society.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「院士、学会会员」，指学术团体或学会的成员。

entries.definition: The adverb, meaning in terms of study or school results.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「学业上、学术上」，用于说明在学习或成绩方面。

entries.definition: Showing careful study and deep knowledge; describes a person or a piece of work.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有学者风范的、学术性的」，多形容人或著作严谨有学问。

entries.definition: Relating to teaching and learning, often with the aim of helping people learn.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「教育的、有教育意义的」，范围比 academic 更宽。

entries.definition: Based on ideas rather than practice; closest to the 'purely academic' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「理论的」，与 academic 的「纯理论」一义最接近，但完全不涉及学校。

entries.definition: Relating to schools or to the medieval method of academic debate; formal in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「学校的、经院式的」，语气正式，常用于中世纪学术辩论的语境。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Greek place name behind the word and the collocations it really appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用这个词背后的希腊地名，以及它真实出现的搭配。

normal.en: Akademeia was the grove where Plato taught: academic means belonging to that world of study.
normal.cn: Akademeia 是柏拉图授课的那片园子：academic 就是「属于那个研究世界」。

normal.en: academy is the place, academic is the adjective, academia is the whole world of it.
normal.cn: academy 是那个场所，academic 是形容词，academia 是整个学术圈。

normal.en: academic year is the school calendar, a fixed phrase worth learning whole.
normal.cn: academic year 指学年，是值得整体记住的固定说法。

normal.en: academic performance is the standard phrase for marks and results at school.
normal.cn: academic performance 是表示在校成绩的标准说法。

normal.en: purely academic means it only matters in theory, as in a purely academic question.
normal.cn: purely academic 表示只在理论上重要，例如纯理论的问题。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp still on in an empty library: someone is awake because a question is not finished.
abstract.cn: 想象空图书馆里还亮着一盏灯：有人醒着，因为一个问题还没想完。

abstract.en: The same word praises and mocks: it praises depth of study and mocks distance from life.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既能赞美也能嘲讽：赞美钻研的深度，也嘲讽与生活的距离。

abstract.en: A grove became a school, a school became a university, and a university became a way of life.
abstract.cn: 一片园子变成一所学校，一所学校变成一所大学，一所大学又变成一种生活方式。

examples.en: He left his job to pursue an academic career in biology.
examples.cn: 他辞掉工作，去追求生物学方面的学术生涯。

examples.en: Her academic performance improved a lot after she changed schools.
examples.cn: 转学之后，她的学业成绩提高了很多。

examples.en: Whether the delay was legal is now an academic question.
examples.cn: 这次延期是否合法，如今已只是个理论问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿卡德米」——阿卡德米的书房里堆满书，讲的是学术与学业。

root: 希腊语 Akadēmeia「雅典城外的学园」，相传与英雄 Akademos 有关，名称本身的来源不确定；柏拉图在此办学，遂有 Akadēmikos「学园的」，经拉丁语 academia 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Academic begins with one place of study and spreads outward: to research, to school results, to pure theory, to a dry style, to the people, the gowns, the subjects and the families of that world.
sensesIntro.cn: academic 从一处读书的地方开始向外扩散：学术研究、学校成绩、纯理论、干枯风格，以及那个世界里的人、礼服、学科与家庭。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp burning late over a desk of books inside a place of study.
core.cn: 核心意象：学府里一张书桌，灯亮到很晚。

branches.en: THE RESEARCH: whatever belongs to serious study and publication.
branches.cn: 研究线：属于严肃学习与发表的东西。

branches.en: THE SCHOOL: the calendar, the marks and the subjects taught there.
branches.cn: 学校线：学年安排、成绩以及在校所教的科目。

branches.en: THE STUDY CUT OFF: what has no practical effect, or has too much book and too little life.
branches.cn: 书房隔绝线：不产生实际后果的东西，或书太多、生活太少的东西。

branches.en: THE PEOPLE AND DRESS: the teachers, and the gowns that make the tradition visible.
branches.cn: 人与服饰线：大学教师，以及让传统看得见的学位服。

branches.en: THE HOUSEHOLD: a whole family oriented toward books and learning.
branches.cn: 家庭线：整个家庭以读书治学为中心。

intro.en: Academic is a Greek place name turned adjective, and its family keeps the shape of the original school.
intro.cn: academic 是由希腊地名转成的形容词，其词族保留着那所学园最初的形状。

latinIntro.en: The Latin form academia carried the Greek word into European learning; the Greek name itself is the oldest recorded layer.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语形式 academia 把这个希腊词带进欧洲的学术传统；希腊语名称本身是最早有记录的层次。

items.exampleCN: 这个名字属于一个地点，而不是一个意为「学习」的词根。

items.example: The adjective first described Plato's followers.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词最初描述柏拉图的追随者。

items.example: Latin kept the word alive in learned writing.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语在学术写作中把这个词保存下来。

items.example: The academy opened in the sixteenth century.
items.exampleCN: 这所学院在十六世纪开办。

items.example: The stem carries the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干承载着整个词族。

definition_zh: 接受（赠予、邀请）；接受（现实）；承认（事实、责任）；同意（提议、条件）；录取、接纳；接受某种付款方式；将就、忍受；不排斥（移植组织）
definition_en: to take something offered to you, or to agree to something and let it stay in your life
core_image: 两只手伸出去，把别人递来的东西稳稳接住，再收进怀里
scene: 年夜饭的桌边，长辈把一个红包递过来，年轻人双手接住。She accepted the red envelope with both hands.
sceneCN: 这里的 accepted 是「接受赠予」（第 1 个义项：愿意收下别人递来的东西）；句意为她用双手接下了那个红包。画面里有饭桌、红包和笑着的长辈。

pos.zh: 动词：接受；承认；同意；接纳；忍受

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「接受、认可」
由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「可接受的、尚可的」
由过去分词转成的形容词，义为「公认的、被普遍接受的」
由本词加施动后缀构成，义为「接受者」，多用于专业语境

senses.title: To take what is offered
senses.definition: to take willingly something that someone offers you, such as a gift, an invitation or help
senses.definitionCN: 愿意收下别人给予的东西，如礼物、邀请或帮助
senses.example: She accepted the red envelope with both hands.
senses.exampleCN: 她用双手接下了那个红包。
senses.why: Latin capere is to take, and the whole word begins with an outstretched pair of hands closing on what is passed over.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 capere 是「拿、取」，这个词的开端就是一双伸出的手把递过来的东西握住，所以最本义的动作就是「接」。

senses.title: To come to terms with a loss
senses.definition: to gradually stop fighting a loss or change that cannot be undone and let it be true
senses.definitionCN: 逐渐停止抗拒无法挽回的失去或变化，并承认它已经发生
senses.example: It took him months to accept the loss of his old shop.
senses.exampleCN: 他花了好几个月才接受老店没了这件事。
senses.why: What is handed to you may be painful; accepting is still holding out the hands, only now without wanting to.
senses.whyCN: 递到手上的东西也可能是痛苦的；接受仍然是把手伸出去，只是这一次并不情愿。

senses.title: To admit that something is true
senses.definition: to admit that a fact is true or that you are responsible for something
senses.definitionCN: 承认某个事实为真，或承认某事是自己的责任
senses.example: He accepted that the mistake was his.
senses.exampleCN: 他承认那个错误是他的。
senses.why: An unwelcome fact is also something offered; taking it in rather than pushing it away is the same gesture in thought.
senses.whyCN: 不受欢迎的事实也是一种「递来的东西」；不把它推开而是收进来，就是同一个动作发生在思考里。

senses.title: To agree to an offer or terms
senses.definition: to say yes to an offer, plan or set of conditions and be bound by it
senses.definitionCN: 对提议、计划或条件表示同意，并受其约束
senses.example: They accepted the offer without asking for more money.
senses.exampleCN: 他们接受了这个报价，没有再要更多的钱。
senses.why: A proposal is held out like an object; saying yes is taking it and putting it into effect.
senses.whyCN: 提议就像一件被递出来的东西；说「好」就是把它接过来并让它生效。

senses.title: To admit someone into a group
senses.definition: to allow someone to join a school, team or organization after deciding they are suitable
senses.definitionCN: 认定某人合适后，允许他进入学校、团队或组织
senses.example: She was accepted at three universities.
senses.exampleCN: 她被三所大学录取了。
senses.why: Here the group does the taking: it opens its hands and draws the person inside its own boundary.
senses.whyCN: 这一次是群体在做「接」的动作：它张开手，把人拉进自己的边界之内。

senses.title: To take a form of payment
senses.definition: of a shop or service, to take a particular kind of money or card as payment
senses.definitionCN: 指商家或服务方收取某种货币或银行卡作为付款
senses.example: Do you accept credit cards here?
senses.exampleCN: 这里收信用卡吗？
senses.why: Payment is something handed across a counter; a shop that takes it has literally accepted the object in front of it.
senses.whyCN: 付款是递过柜台的东西；愿意收下它的店，字面上就是接住了眼前这件东西。

senses.title: To put up with something unwelcome
senses.definition: to tolerate an unpleasant situation or condition because it cannot easily be changed
senses.definitionCN: 因为不易改变，而容忍不愉快的处境或条件
senses.example: He accepted the low pay because he needed the job.
senses.exampleCN: 他接受了这份低薪，因为他需要这份工作。
senses.why: Taking something you did not choose shades into bearing it; the hands stay open even when they would rather not.
senses.whyCN: 收下并非自己选择的东西，就滑向「承受」；即使心里不愿意，手还是张着。

senses.title: Of the body, to keep transplanted tissue
senses.definition: of a body, to allow a transplanted organ or tissue to remain without rejecting it
senses.definitionCN: 指身体容许移植的器官或组织留存下来而不排斥它
senses.example: The body accepted the new kidney within a few weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 身体在几周内就接受了新肾脏。
senses.why: The medical sense keeps the oldest physical meaning: the body takes the foreign part in and does not push it back out.
senses.whyCN: 医学义保留了最古老的身体含义：身体把外来的部分收进去，而不是把它推出去。

intro.en: Accept is built from a Latin verb meaning to take to oneself, and all its senses keep the gesture of receiving.
intro.cn: accept 由拉丁语中意为「拿到自己这里」的动词构成，所有义项都保留着「接住」的动作。

items.en: Capere meant 'to take, seize, grasp'. It is well recorded and also lies behind capture, captive and receive.
items.cn: capere 意为「拿、抓、握」，有明确记录，也是 capture、captive 与 receive 的词根。

items.en: Ad- 'to, toward' plus capere formed accipere, 'to receive, take to oneself'. The prefix marks the movement of the thing toward the receiver.
items.cn: ad-「向、朝」与 capere 构成 accipere，意为「接收、拿到自己这里」；前缀标示东西朝接收者移动。

items.en: Old French accepter carried the word into English with the senses of receiving, agreeing and tolerating already present.
items.cn: 古法语 accepter 把这个词带进英语，当时「接收、同意、容忍」几个意思已同时存在。

items.en: The verb is recorded in English from the fourteenth century onward; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个动词从十四世纪起在英语中有记录；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Later usage added admission to schools, taking of card payments and the medical sense of a body not rejecting a transplant.
items.cn: 后来的用法又加入了学校录取、收取刷卡付款，以及身体不排斥移植组织这一医学义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin verb capere; the near-meaning group holds words of receiving, admitting and tolerating.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁动词 capere；近义组收表示「接收」「承认」与「容忍」的词。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of accepting something or the state of being accepted.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「接受、认可」，指接受的动作或被接纳的状态。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning good enough to be agreed to or allowed.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可接受的、尚可的」，指好到可以同意或允许。

entries.definition: A person or thing that receives something, used mainly in technical contexts.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「接受者」，多用于物理、化学等专业语境。

entries.definition: To leave out; it shares the Latin root capere but with ex- 'out' it means the opposite of taking in.
entries.definitionCN: 介词或动词，义为「除……之外、排除」；与 accept 同出 capere，但前缀 ex- 表示「向外」，意思正好相反。

entries.definition: To get something that is sent or given, with less emphasis on agreeing to it.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「收到、接到」，强调东西到手，不太强调是否愿意。

entries.definition: To agree that something is true, often unwillingly, or to let someone enter.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「承认」或「准许进入」，语气比 accept 更强调不情愿或正式准入。

entries.definition: To state that you know something is true or that you have received something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「承认、确认收到」，语气正式，多指公开表明已知悉。

entries.definition: To allow something you dislike to continue without stopping it.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「容忍、忍受」，只对应「将就」一义，强调不加阻止。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded Latin root capere and the phrases accept actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用有记录的拉丁词根 capere，以及 accept 真实出现的搭配。

normal.en: capere is to take, and ad- points toward you: accept is to take something toward yourself.
normal.cn: capere 是「拿」，ad- 指向你这边：accept 就是把东西拿到自己这里。

normal.en: Keep accept, acceptance and acceptable in one line: verb, noun and adjective.
normal.cn: 把 accept、acceptance、acceptable 串成一条线：动词、名词、形容词。

normal.en: accept an offer is the phrase used when someone says yes to a job or a deal.
normal.cn: accept an offer 是接受工作或交易时的常用说法。

normal.en: accept responsibility means you take the blame instead of pushing it away.
normal.cn: accept responsibility 意为把责任接过来，而不是推开。

normal.en: be accepted at a university is the standard way to say you were admitted.
normal.cn: be accepted at a university 是表示「被大学录取」的标准说法。

abstract.en: Picture both hands open, waiting: the whole word lives in that gesture.
abstract.cn: 想象两只摊开的手在等着：整个词就活在这个动作里。

abstract.en: Some things are handed to you and some are pushed at you; accept covers both, which is why it also means to bear.
abstract.cn: 有些东西是递过来的，有些是硬塞过来的；accept 两者都管，所以它也能表示「承受」。

abstract.en: A body that accepts a new organ and a person who accepts bad news are doing the same thing: not pushing it out.
abstract.cn: 身体接受新器官，和人接受坏消息，做的是同一件事：不把它推出去。

examples.en: He accepted the job offer after a long talk with his family.
examples.cn: 和家人长谈之后，他接受了那份工作。

examples.en: It is hard to accept that the old market is gone for good.
examples.cn: 很难接受那个老市场永远消失了。

examples.en: The little shop does not accept cards, so bring some cash.
examples.cn: 这家小店不收银行卡，带点现金吧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额可塞普特」——别人递来，手一伸就塞进怀里：接受。

root: 拉丁语 accipere「接收、拿到自己这里」，由 ad-「向」与 capere「拿、抓」构成；其反复动词 acceptare 经古法语 accepter 进入英语。capere 也是 capture、receive 的词根。

sensesIntro.en: Accept is always the same gesture of taking something in: a gift, a loss, a fact, a proposal, a new member, a payment, an unwelcome condition or a transplanted organ.
sensesIntro.cn: accept 始终是同一个「把东西收进来」的动作：礼物、失去、事实、提议、新成员、付款、不理想的条件，或移植的器官。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two open hands close around something that is being passed over.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只张开的手合拢，接住递过来的东西。

branches.en: THE HAND: a gift or a payment is taken across the space between two people.
branches.cn: 手边线：礼物或付款越过两个人之间的距离被接住。

branches.en: THE MIND: a loss or a fact is taken in instead of being pushed away.
branches.cn: 心智线：失去或事实被收进来，而不是被推开。

branches.en: THE DEAL: a proposal is taken and made binding.
branches.cn: 交易线：提议被接下并产生约束力。

branches.en: THE GROUP: a school or team opens its boundary and draws a person in.
branches.cn: 群体线：学校或团队打开边界，把人收进来。

branches.en: THE BODY: unwanted conditions are borne, and transplanted tissue is not rejected.
branches.cn: 身体线：不想要的条件被承受下来，移植的组织不被排斥。

intro.en: Accept is a Latin compound verb; its English family grows with common noun and adjective suffixes.
intro.cn: accept 是拉丁语复合动词，其英语词族由常见的名词与形容词后缀扩展而成。

latinIntro.en: Capere, accipere and acceptus are recorded Latin forms, and the same root underlies capture and receive.
latinIntro.cn: capere、accipere 与 acceptus 都是有记录的拉丁语形式，同一词根也支撑着 capture 与 receive。

definition_zh: 可接受的；尚可的；合意的；允许的；可以忍受的；合乎语法的
definition_en: good enough to be agreed to, allowed, or tolerated, even though it may not be excellent
core_image: 一只手把东西递出去，对方点点头把它接住：够格，才被收下
scene: 房东把租金写在一张纸上，双方商量了好一阵。After a long talk, they agreed on a price acceptable to both of them.
sceneCN: 这里 acceptable 指「双方都能接受」（第 2 个义项：能被相关各方同意）；句意为谈了很久之后，他们商定了一个双方都能接受的价格。

pos.zh: 形容词：可接受的；尚可的；合意的；允许的

senses.title: Good enough to pass
senses.definition: of a quality or standard, good enough to be approved although not excellent
senses.definitionCN: 指质量或水准虽不优秀，但已达到可以通过的程度
senses.example: The food was plain but acceptable.
senses.exampleCN: 饭菜简单，但还过得去。
senses.why: The Latin root means to receive; what can be received is, at the very least, good enough to take in.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「接收」；能被收下的东西，最低限度就是达到了可以接受的程度。

senses.title: Agreeable to the people involved
senses.definition: of an offer, price, or plan, able to be agreed to by everyone concerned
senses.definitionCN: 指提议、价格或方案能被相关各方同意
senses.example: They finally found terms acceptable to both sides.
senses.exampleCN: 他们终于找到了双方都能接受的条件。
senses.why: Being received turns into being agreed to: the thing is not merely tolerated, it is taken by both hands.
senses.whyCN: 「被收下」进一步变成「被同意」：这样东西不只是被容忍，而是被双方一起接了过去。

senses.title: Proper in social behaviour
senses.definition: of behaviour, dress, or language, considered proper by most people in a society
senses.definitionCN: 指行为、衣着或语言被社会上多数人视为得体
senses.example: Short skirts were not considered acceptable at the office then.
senses.exampleCN: 那时在办公室里，短裙被认为不合规矩。
senses.why: Society is the receiver here: an act is acceptable when the group is willing to take it in without objection.
senses.whyCN: 这里的「接收者」是社会：一个行为若群体愿意毫无异议地接纳，就是合乎规范的。

senses.title: Permitted by a rule
senses.definition: allowed by a law, rule, or person in authority
senses.definitionCN: 指法律、规定或有权威的人所允许
senses.example: Is it acceptable to park here after six?
senses.exampleCN: 六点以后在这里停车可以吗？
senses.why: The receiver becomes an authority that lets the thing pass; what is let through is acceptable.
senses.whyCN: 接收者变成了放行的权威：被放行通过的东西，就是被允许的。

senses.title: Possible to endure
senses.definition: of pain, noise, or a hard condition, bearable rather than pleasant
senses.definitionCN: 指疼痛、噪音或艰难处境尚能承受，谈不上舒服
senses.example: The noise from the road was acceptable once the windows were closed.
senses.exampleCN: 关上窗以后，路上的噪音还算能忍受。
senses.why: Enduring is a slow way of receiving: the body keeps taking the discomfort without pushing it away.
senses.whyCN: 忍受是一种缓慢的接收：身体持续接纳这份不适，而没有把它推开。

senses.title: Welcome and pleasing
senses.definition: of a gift, offering, or act, pleasing and gladly received, in a rather formal use
senses.definitionCN: 指礼物、供奉或行为令人满意、被欣然接受，属较正式的用法
senses.example: The villagers brought offerings acceptable to the river god.
senses.exampleCN: 村民献上了河神愿意接受的供品。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer: acceptable simply meant that a person or a god was glad to receive the thing.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的一层：acceptable 原本只表示某人或神明乐于把它收下。

senses.title: Well formed in grammar
senses.definition: in linguistics, of a sentence or phrase, following the rules of the language so that native speakers accept it
senses.definitionCN: 语言学用语，指句子或短语符合该语言的规则，母语者认为可以成立
senses.example: The sentence is odd in meaning but grammatically acceptable.
senses.exampleCN: 这个句子意思古怪，但语法上是可接受的。
senses.why: Grammar is a set of rules that decide what a language community will receive as a valid sentence.
senses.whyCN: 语法是一套规则，用来决定语言共同体愿意接收什么为合法句子。

senses.title: Valid for an official purpose
senses.definition: of a document, card, or method of payment, recognized as valid by the person or office receiving it
senses.definitionCN: 指证件、卡或支付方式被接收一方认可为有效
senses.example: A passport is the only acceptable proof of identity here.
senses.exampleCN: 在这里，护照是唯一被认可的身份证明。
senses.why: The receiver checks the thing before taking it; only what passes that check is acceptable.
senses.whyCN: 接收方先查验再收下；只有通过这道检查的东西才是可用的。

intro.en: Acceptable is a Latin word built on the verb 'to take', carried into English through Old French.
intro.cn: acceptable 是建立在拉丁语「拿取」动词之上的词，经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Capere meant 'to take, seize, grasp'. The deeper origin of the root is uncertain.
items.cn: capere 意为「拿取、抓住、握住」；这个更早的词根来源不确定。

items.en: Ad- 'to, toward' plus capere formed accipere, 'to receive, take to oneself'.
items.cn: ad-「向、朝」加 capere 构成 accipere，意为「接收、收为己有」。

items.en: The frequentative acceptare meant 'to receive repeatedly, to welcome', adding the idea of a willing reception.
items.cn: 反复动词 acceptare 意为「一再接收、欢迎」，加入了「乐意接纳」的意思。

items.en: Acceptabilis meant 'that may be received or approved', from which the English word descends through Old French.
items.cn: acceptabilis 意为「可以被接收或认可的」，英语词由此经古法语传承而来。

items.en: English borrowed the adjective in the fourteenth century with the senses of pleasing and of worth receiving.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入这个形容词，当时兼有「令人满意」与「值得接受」两义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same taking root; the near-meaning group lists words for what can pass a standard.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「拿取」词根构成的词；近义组列出表示「能达标、能过关」的词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to take something that is offered.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「接受、收下」别人递来的东西。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of receiving or approving something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「接受、认可、接纳」，指接收或批准的行为。

entries.definition: The noun for how far something can be accepted.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「可接受性」，指某事物能被接受的程度。

entries.definition: The negative adjective meaning too bad to be allowed or tolerated.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不能接受的、不可容忍的」，是本词加否定前缀构成的反义形式。

entries.definition: Good enough to meet a requirement, with a slightly more formal and official tone.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「令人满意的、符合要求的」，语气比 acceptable 更正式、更像评语。

entries.definition: Bearable but not pleasant, used mainly of pain, heat, or noise.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可以忍受的」，多用于疼痛、酷热或噪音，不含满意之意。

entries.definition: Enough in amount or good enough in quality, with an emphasis on sufficiency.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「足够的、尚可的」，重点在数量或程度够用，而非被认可。

entries.definition: Allowed by rules or law, used when the question is permission rather than quality.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可允许的」，用于讨论规则是否准许，而非质量好坏。

entries.definition: Just good enough to pass, often with a hint of faint praise.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「勉强过得去的」，常带一点「只好如此」的意味。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin verb of taking and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语「拿取」动词，以及这个词常出现的搭配。

normal.en: accipere is to receive: acceptable means able to be received.
normal.cn: accipere 是「接收」：acceptable 就是「能被接收的」。

normal.en: The same root gives accept, acceptance and acceptability.
normal.cn: 同一词根还给出 accept、acceptance 与 acceptability。

normal.en: A price acceptable to both sides is a price nobody rejects.
normal.cn: 「a price acceptable to both sides」就是没有人拒绝的价格。

normal.en: Socially acceptable describes what a group will take without complaint.
normal.cn: socially acceptable 描述的是一个群体愿意无异议接纳的东西。

normal.en: The negative form is simply un- plus acceptable.
normal.cn: 否定形式就是 un- 加上 acceptable。

abstract.en: Picture a doorman who nods: whatever he lets through is acceptable.
abstract.cn: 想象一个点头的守门人：他放过去的东西，就是可接受的。

abstract.en: Acceptance is a scale with a low bar, not a high prize.
abstract.cn: 「被接受」是一道低门槛，而不是一项高等奖赏。

abstract.en: The word never praises; it only says the thing may be taken.
abstract.cn: 这个词从不称赞，它只说这件东西可以收下。

examples.en: The room was small but perfectly acceptable for one night.
examples.cn: 房间不大，但住一晚完全过得去。

examples.en: We need a solution that is acceptable to both sides.
examples.cn: 我们需要一个双方都能接受的方案。

examples.en: Leaving early is acceptable if you tell the office first.
examples.cn: 只要事先跟办公室说一声，早退是可以的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克塞普特伯」——手伸过去把东西接住，点头收下，就是可接受的。

root: 拉丁语 accipere「接受」由 ad-「向」加 capere「拿取」构成；其反复动词 acceptare 产生晚期拉丁语 acceptabilis「可接受的」，再经古法语 acceptable 进入英语。更早的词根来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Acceptable always describes something held out for approval: a quality, a deal, a behaviour, a rule, a burden, a gift, a sentence, or a document.
sensesIntro.cn: acceptable 始终描述某样被递出来等待认可的东西：质量、交易、行为、规则、负担、礼物、句子或证件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand holds something out, and the other side nods and takes it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把东西递出来，另一方点头接住。

branches.en: QUALITY: what meets the minimum standard is taken in, though nobody praises it.
branches.cn: 质量线：达到最低标准的东西被收下，虽然没人称赞它。

branches.en: CONSENT: a deal both sides take, and a gift a god receives gladly.
branches.cn: 同意线：双方都接下的交易，以及神明欣然收下的供品。

branches.en: RULES: society and authority decide what may be taken in.
branches.cn: 规则线：社会与权威决定什么可以被接纳。

branches.en: ENDURANCE: the body keeps taking what it cannot push away.
branches.cn: 忍受线：身体持续接纳它推不开的东西。

branches.en: VALIDITY: grammar and offices check whether the thing may pass.
branches.cn: 有效线：语法与办事机构查验这样东西能否通过。

scene: 老小区的正门封了，住户每天都要绕到后街。The only access to the garden is through a narrow gate.
sceneCN: 这里 access 指「进入的通道」（第 1 个义项：可以进入某处的路径或门）；句意为通往花园的唯一通道是一扇窄门。
