senses.title: A way in or through
senses.definition: a path, door, road, or other route by which a place can be entered or reached
senses.definitionCN: 指进入或抵达某处的路径、门、道路等
senses.example: The only access to the village is by boat.
senses.exampleCN: 进入这个村子唯一的通道是坐船。
senses.why: Latin accessus was a coming near; a way in is the route that lets that approach happen.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 accessus 意为「走近」；通道就是让这种走近得以发生的路线。

senses.title: The right to use or obtain
senses.definition: the right or opportunity to use, see, or obtain something that is limited or controlled
senses.definitionCN: 指使用、查看或取得受限事物的权利或机会
senses.example: Every student has access to the online library.
senses.exampleCN: 每个学生都能使用在线图书馆。
senses.why: If a route is open to you, you may walk along it; the route quietly turns into a permission.
senses.whyCN: 如果一条路对你敞开，你就可以沿着它走过去；路线于是悄悄变成了许可。

senses.title: The act of getting in
senses.definition: the act of entering a place or of reaching a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 指进入某地或接触到某人、某物的行为
senses.example: Reporters were refused access to the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 记者被拒绝进入会场。
senses.why: The noun shifts from the route to the movement along it: the approach itself.
senses.whyCN: 名词从「路线」转到「沿路线移动」：也就是走近这个动作本身。

senses.title: A connection to a system
senses.definition: the ability of a device or user to connect to the internet, a network, or a service
senses.definitionCN: 指设备或用户连接互联网、网络或服务的能力
senses.example: The hotel offers free internet access in every room.
senses.exampleCN: 这家旅馆每个房间都提供免费网络接入。
senses.why: A network is treated like a building: you need a way in before you can use what is inside.
senses.whyCN: 网络被当作一栋建筑：先有进去的路，才能使用里面的东西。

senses.title: To reach or enter
senses.definition: to reach, enter, or make use of a place, especially one that is restricted
senses.definitionCN: 指进入、抵达或使用某地，尤指受限之处
senses.example: Staff can access the lab with their ID cards.
senses.exampleCN: 工作人员可以用工牌进入实验室。
senses.why: The verb turns the route into motion: walking the way in.
senses.whyCN: 动词把「路线」变成动作：沿着进去的路走。

senses.title: To open stored data
senses.definition: to open, read, or retrieve files or data stored in a computer system
senses.definitionCN: 指打开、读取或调取计算机系统中存储的文件或数据
senses.example: You can access your files from any device.
senses.exampleCN: 你可以从任何设备访问自己的文件。
senses.why: Data is stored behind a system, and reaching it follows the same pattern as reaching a room.
senses.whyCN: 数据存放在系统之后，取到它的方式和走进一个房间是同一种模式。

senses.title: A sudden fit of feeling
senses.definition: a sudden outburst of an emotion, an old and mostly literary use
senses.definitionCN: 指情绪的突然爆发，属古老且多用于文学的用法
senses.example: In an access of rage, he tore the letter in two.
senses.exampleCN: 一阵暴怒之下，他把信撕成两半。
senses.why: Latin accessus also meant an onset, as if a feeling came upon a person and entered him.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 accessus 也有「来袭、发作」之意，仿佛一种情绪扑上来，进入了人。

senses.title: Used before a noun for a route
senses.definition: placed before another noun to name a road, code, or point that gives entry
senses.definitionCN: 放在另一名词之前，表示提供进入的道路、密码或地点
senses.example: Turn left at the access road behind the station.
senses.exampleCN: 在车站后面的辅路向左转。
senses.why: The route sense is compressed into a modifier: a road whose whole job is to give access.
senses.whyCN: 「路线」这一义被压缩成修饰语：一条存在意义就是提供通行的路。

intro.en: Access comes from a Latin verb of going, and the noun still keeps the shape of a doorway.
intro.cn: access 来自一个表示「走」的拉丁语动词，名词至今仍保留「门口」的形状。

items.en: The verb cedere meant 'to go, move, yield'. Its earlier origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 动词 cedere 意为「走、移动、让出」；更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Ad- 'to' plus cedere formed accedere, 'to come near, approach; to be added'.
items.cn: ad-「向」加 cedere 构成 accedere，意为「走近、接近；附加」。

items.en: The noun accessus meant 'a coming near, an entrance', and also 'an increase'.
items.cn: 名词 accessus 意为「接近、入口」，同时也有「增加」之义。

items.en: Old French acces brought the noun into English in the fourteenth century with the senses of approach and entrance.
items.cn: 古法语 acces 在十四世纪把这个名词带入英语，带有「接近」与「入口」两义。

items.en: The verb is much later and is generally dated to the twentieth century; the computing sense grew with the computer.
items.cn: 动词用法晚得多，一般追溯到二十世纪；计算机「存取数据」义随电脑普及而发展。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin root of going and reaching; the near-meaning group names ways of entering or being admitted.
note.cn: 形近组共享表示「走、抵达」的拉丁词根；近义组列出「进入」与「获准进入」的各种说法。

entries.definition: Able to be reached, entered, or used, also used of places designed for disabled people.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可到达的、可使用的」，也指为残障人士设计的无障碍场所。

entries.definition: The noun for how easy something is to reach or use.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「可达性、无障碍程度」，指某处或某物被到达和使用的容易程度。

entries.definition: Too far, too difficult, or too locked to be reached.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「难以到达的、难以理解的」，是 accessible 加否定前缀构成的反义形式。

entries.definition: The act of taking up an office or of joining a group, from the same Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「就职、加入、新增」，来自同一个拉丁语动词。

entries.definition: The door or opening by which you enter, more physical than access.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「入口、门口」，比 access 更强调具体的门或开口。

entries.definition: The act of going in, or the right to go in, often in official contexts.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「进入、入场权」，常用于较正式的语境。

entries.definition: Permission to enter a place or join an institution, often after a check.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「准许进入、录取」，通常需要经过查验或审核。

entries.definition: The act of coming near, or a way of dealing with something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「接近、途径」，也可指处理问题的方法。

entries.definition: To arrive at or stretch out to something, with no idea of permission.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「到达、伸手够到」，不含「获准」的意思。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin verb of going and the everyday phrases built on access.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语「走」动词，以及由 access 构成的日常搭配。

normal.en: cedere is to go: access is the going up to a place.
normal.cn: cedere 是「走」：access 就是朝某处走过去。

normal.en: Accedere adds ad- 'to', so the word always points at a destination.
normal.cn: accedere 加了 ad-「向」，所以这个词总是指向一个目的地。

normal.en: Access to a place is a route; access to a thing is a right.
normal.cn: access to a place 是路线，access to a thing 则是权利。

normal.en: An access code is the modern key to the old door.
normal.cn: access code 就是开那扇老门的新式钥匙。

normal.en: The verb keeps the same shape: access a file, access a building.
normal.cn: 动词形式完全一样：access a file 是访问文件，access a building 是进入大楼。

abstract.en: A door, a key, and a hand on the handle: permission is only a route that stayed open.
abstract.cn: 一扇门、一把钥匙、一只搭在门把上的手：许可不过是一条没有关上的路。

abstract.en: The same word covers a garden gate and a folder on a screen, because both stand between you and what you want.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指花园小门，也指屏幕上的文件夹，因为两者都挡在你和想要的东西之间。

abstract.en: Access is never the thing itself; it is the thin passage that leads to it.
abstract.cn: access 从来不是东西本身，它只是通向那件东西的细窄通道。

examples.en: Students have free access to the online library.
examples.cn: 学生可以免费使用在线图书馆。

examples.en: You can access your files from any device.
examples.cn: 你可以从任何设备访问自己的文件。

examples.en: The rear door gives access to the garden.
examples.cn: 后门通向花园。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「艾克塞斯」——走到门口，门恰好开了：能走进去就是 access。

root: 拉丁语 accessus「接近、入口」来自 accedere「走近」，由 ad-「向」加 cedere「走、让」构成；更早的词源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Access starts as a physical way in and spreads to permission, to networks, to stored data, and even to a feeling that suddenly comes over a person.
sensesIntro.cn: access 从一条实在的进门之路出发，扩展到许可、网络、存储的数据，甚至扩展到突然扑上心头的情绪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a locked side door; a key turns and the way in appears.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇锁着的侧门，钥匙一转，进去的路出现了。

branches.en: THE DOOR: a route into a place, and the act of walking through it.
branches.cn: 门口线：进入某处的路线，以及穿过去的动作。

branches.en: THE RIGHT: an open route becomes a permission, and the permission becomes an act.
branches.cn: 权利线：敞开的路线变成许可，许可又变成一次具体的进入。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM: a network and its stored files are reached the way a room is reached.
branches.cn: 系统线：网络与其中存储的文件，都按走进房间的方式来抵达。

branches.en: THE ONSET: an emotion arrives and enters a person, an old literary branch.
branches.cn: 发作线：情绪来临并进入一个人，这是古老的文学分支。

branches.en: THE MODIFIER: the route sense shrinks into a word placed before a noun.
branches.cn: 定语线：路线义缩小成一个放在名词前的修饰词。

intro.en: Access is a Latin noun of motion, and English builds its family with suffixes rather than new roots.
intro.cn: access 是一个表示运动的拉丁语名词，英语靠后缀而不是新词根扩展它的词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb cedere, its compound accedere and the noun accessus are all recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语动词 cedere、它的复合形式 accedere 与名词 accessus 均有文献记录。

definition_zh: 事故；意外；偶然的事；偶然的境遇；偶性；临时记号
definition_en: an unexpected event, especially one that causes damage or injury, or something that happens by chance
core_image: 一块石头从上方落下，正好砸在中途经过的人身上：事情自己掉了下来
scene: 雨天路滑，骑车的人在拐弯处摔倒在路边。He broke his wrist in a cycling accident last week.
sceneCN: 这里 accident 指「造成伤害的意外事故」（第 1 个义项：偶然发生并带来损害的事件）；句意为上周他在一次骑车事故中摔断了手腕。

pos.zh: 名词：事故；意外；偶然的事；偶性；临时记号

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -al 构成，义为「意外的；偶然的」
由 accidental 加后缀 -ly 构成，义为「偶然地；无意中」
由本词加构词成分 -prone 构成，义为「容易出事故的」
与 accident 同出拉丁语 accidens，指语法中研究词形变化的部分，意义早已分化

senses.title: An unexpected event that causes harm
senses.definition: an event that happens by chance and causes damage, injury, or death
senses.definitionCN: 指偶然发生并造成损坏、伤害或死亡的事件
senses.example: She was hurt in a car accident on the way home.
senses.exampleCN: 她在回家路上的一场车祸中受了伤。
senses.why: Accidere is to fall upon: something falls on a person without warning, and that falling is the accident.
senses.whyCN: accidere 意为「落到身上」：某件事毫无预警地落到一个人头上，这次坠落就是事故。

senses.title: Something that happens by chance
senses.definition: an event that happens without a plan or an obvious cause
senses.definitionCN: 指没有计划、也没有明显原因而发生的事
senses.example: Their meeting at the airport was a pure accident.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在机场相遇纯属偶然。
senses.why: If an event simply falls, no one arranged it; chance is the whole mechanism.
senses.whyCN: 如果一件事就这样落下来，没有人安排它，那么偶然本身就是全部机制。

senses.title: A chance feature of one's circumstances
senses.definition: a fact about a person's birth, background, or situation that results from chance rather than choice
senses.definitionCN: 指出身、背景或处境中由偶然而非选择决定的事实
senses.example: Being born in a wealthy country is an accident of birth.
senses.exampleCN: 出生在一个富裕国家是出身的偶然。
senses.why: The falling event does not only hurt; it also quietly decides where a person lands.
senses.whyCN: 落下来的事件不只带来伤害，它也悄悄决定一个人落在什么位置。

senses.title: A non-essential property in philosophy
senses.definition: in philosophy, a quality or property that a thing may lose without ceasing to be itself
senses.definitionCN: 哲学用语，指事物失去之后仍不改变其本质的属性
senses.example: Colour is an accident of the object, not its essence.
senses.exampleCN: 颜色是物体的偶性，而不是它的本质。
senses.why: Scholastic philosophy used accidens for what befalls a thing from outside, as opposed to what belongs to its substance.
senses.whyCN: 经院哲学用 accidens 指从外部落到事物身上的属性，与属于实体的本质相对。

senses.title: A sign that alters a note in music
senses.definition: a sharp, flat, or natural sign that raises or lowers a note outside its key
senses.definitionCN: 指标在调外升高或降低某音的升号、降号或还原号
senses.example: A small accident before the note tells the player to raise it.
senses.exampleCN: 音符前面的小临时记号提示演奏者把这个音升高。
senses.why: The sign is added from outside the key and falls on one note, so the old philosophical sense of an added property survives.
senses.whyCN: 这个符号从调外加上来，只落在某一个音上，于是哲学中「附加属性」的旧义在此残留。

senses.title: By accident: without intending to
senses.definition: in the fixed phrase by accident, meaning without plan or intention
senses.definitionCN: 用于固定短语 by accident，表示没有计划、并非有意
senses.example: I found the old photo by accident while cleaning the drawer.
senses.exampleCN: 我在清理抽屉时无意中发现了那张旧照片。
senses.why: The falling event turns into an adverbial phrase: it simply dropped in, and nobody aimed it.
senses.whyCN: 「落下的事件」变成状语短语：它只是掉了进来，没有人瞄准它。

senses.title: No accident: not a coincidence
senses.definition: in the phrase no accident, meaning not a chance event but a result that was arranged or expected
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 no accident，表示并非偶然，而是有意安排或必然的结果
senses.example: It is no accident that the two stories sound alike.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个故事听起来相似，绝非偶然。
senses.why: The same image works in reverse: if nothing simply falls, someone must have placed it there.
senses.whyCN: 同一个意象反过来用：如果没有任何东西自己掉下来，那一定是有人把它放在了那里。

senses.title: A child's loss of bladder or bowel control
senses.definition: an informal use for the case when a child urinates or defecates in their clothes by mistake
senses.definitionCN: 非正式用法，指孩子不小心尿在或拉在衣服里
senses.example: The toddler had an accident on the way to the nursery.
senses.exampleCN: 小孩在去幼儿园的路上尿裤子了。
senses.why: It is a small bodily event that arrives unplanned, so the general sense of a chance mishap shrinks to the body.
senses.whyCN: 这是一件没有计划就落到身上的身体小事，于是「偶然的不幸」这一泛义缩小到了身体上。

intro.en: Accident is built on a Latin verb of falling, and every sense still carries the image of something coming down on someone.
intro.cn: accident 建立在拉丁语「落下」动词之上，每个义项都仍带着「有东西落到人身上」的意象。

items.en: *ḱad- is generally reconstructed as 'to fall'. The reconstruction is conventional and its exact shape is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语 *ḱad- 表示「落下」；这是学界通行的重构形式，具体形态不确定。

items.en: Cadere meant 'to fall', and it also lies behind cadence and decay.
items.cn: cadere 意为「落下」，cadence 与 decay 也出自这个词。

items.en: Ad- 'to' plus cadere formed accidere, 'to fall upon, happen to someone'.
items.cn: ad-「向」加 cadere 构成 accidere，意为「落到身上、发生在某人身上」。

items.en: The participle accidens, 'happening', became a philosophical noun for a non-essential property; English borrowed the word through Old French in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 分词 accidens 意为「正在发生的」，后来成为指「非本质属性」的哲学名词；英语在十四世纪经古法语借入此词。

items.en: The everyday sense of a harmful mishap became dominant, while the musical sign and the fixed phrases by accident and no accident grew alongside it.
items.cn: 日常所说的「有害意外」成为主要义项，音乐中的临时记号以及 by accident、no accident 等固定说法也同时发展起来。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms and relatives of the same falling root; the near-meaning group names kinds of mishap and unwanted events.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「落下」词根的形式与亲属词；近义组列出各种意外与不愉快事件。

entries.definition: The adjective for something happening by chance or without intent.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「偶然的、意外的」，指偶然发生或并非有意。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning by chance or without intending to.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「偶然地、无意中」。

entries.definition: An adjective for a person who often has accidents.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「容易出事故的」，形容常常出意外的人。

entries.definition: A grammar term for the part of grammar dealing with word endings and forms.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，语法术语，指研究词形变化的语法部分；与 accident 同出拉丁语 accidens，但意义早已分化。

entries.definition: A small accident with little damage, often slightly formal in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「小意外、小事故」，损害不大，语气略正式。

entries.definition: A violent collision of vehicles or a loud fall, more concrete than accident.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「撞车、撞击」，比 accident 更具体，强调猛烈碰撞。

entries.definition: The act of two objects hitting each other, common in reports and insurance.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「相撞」，多见于报告与保险语境。

entries.definition: An event, often unpleasant, but not necessarily an accident; it uses in- instead of ad- on the same Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「事件、插曲」，常指不愉快的事，但不一定是事故；与 accident 同出拉丁语 cadere，只是前缀换成了 in-。

entries.definition: A person killed or injured in an accident or a war.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「伤亡人员」，指在事故或战争中死伤的人。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin verb of falling and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语「落下」动词，以及这个词常出现的搭配。

normal.en: cadere is to fall: an accident is something that falls on you.
normal.cn: cadere 是「落下」：accident 就是落到你身上的事。

normal.en: ad- plus cadere gives accidere, to happen to someone.
normal.cn: ad- 加 cadere 构成 accidere，意为「发生在某人身上」。

normal.en: The same root appears in cadence and decay.
normal.cn: 同一词根还出现在 cadence 与 decay 中。

normal.en: By accident means that nobody planned it.
normal.cn: by accident 意为没有人计划过它。

normal.en: The musical sign is also an accident, a note falling outside its key.
normal.cn: 音乐里的临时记号也叫 accident，是一个落在调外的音。

abstract.en: A falling stone: nothing pushes it, nothing aims it, yet it lands exactly on someone.
abstract.cn: 一块落下的石头：没人推它，也没人瞄准它，它却正好落在某人身上。

abstract.en: Chance and harm are one picture seen twice: the fall decides both where and how hard.
abstract.cn: 偶然与伤害是同一幅画看两遍：这次坠落同时决定了落在哪里、落得多重。

abstract.en: Philosophy turns the fall into a property: what lands on a thing does not become its essence.
abstract.cn: 哲学把这次坠落变成一种属性：落到事物身上的东西，并不会成为它的本质。

examples.en: She was hurt in a car accident on the way home.
examples.cn: 她在回家路上的一场车祸中受了伤。

examples.en: I found the old photo by accident while cleaning the drawer.
examples.cn: 我在清理抽屉时无意中发现了那张旧照片。

examples.en: It is no accident that the two stories sound alike.
examples.cn: 这两个故事听起来相似，绝非偶然。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克西登特」——石头从上面掉下来，正砸在路人身上：事故、意外。

root: 拉丁语 accidere「落到身上、发生」由 ad-「向」加 cadere「落下」构成；分词 accidens 在经院哲学中指「偶性」，英语经古法语 accident 借入。更早的印欧词根属于通行重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Accident begins as a fall and then spreads: a harmful fall, a chance fall, a fall that shapes a life, a property falling onto a thing, and finally a note falling outside its key.
sensesIntro.cn: accident 从一次「落下」开始，然后向外扩展：有害的坠落、偶然的降临、决定人生位置的落下、落到事物身上的属性，最后是落在调外的音符。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone falls from above and lands on a passer-by.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块石头从高处落下，砸在中途经过的人身上。

branches.en: THE BODY: a harmful fall, from a road crash down to a child's small mishap.
branches.cn: 身体线：有害的坠落，从路上的撞车一直缩小到孩子的小意外。

branches.en: THE CHANCE: an event no one arranged, and a circumstance no one chose.
branches.cn: 偶然线：没人安排的事件，以及没人选择的境遇。

branches.en: THE PROPERTY: philosophy keeps the idea of something added from outside.
branches.cn: 属性线：哲学保留了「从外部添加之物」的观念。

branches.en: THE NOTE: a musical sign that falls outside the key.
branches.cn: 音符线：一个落在调外的音乐符号。

branches.en: THE PHRASES: by accident denies a plan, while no accident asserts one.
branches.cn: 短语线：by accident 否认有安排，no accident 则肯定有安排。

intro.en: Accident is a Latin participle turned noun, and English built its family with ordinary endings.
intro.cn: accident 是由拉丁语分词转成的名词，英语用普通后缀扩展出它的词族。

definition_zh: 住处；住宿；食宿；调节；适应；和解；容纳空间；便利安排
definition_en: a place to stay, or the act of adjusting something to fit a need or of reaching an agreement
core_image: 把略长的桌子斜着塞进小屋：空间与需要彼此让步、刚好合上
scene: 订房网站上，旅客挑了一间离车站不远的房间。We booked accommodation near the station for three nights.
sceneCN: 这里 accommodation 指「住处、住宿」（第 1 个义项：旅行期间住的地方）；句意为我们在车站附近订了三晚住宿。

pos.zh: 名词：住处；住宿；食宿；调节；和解；便利安排

derivatives.zh: 本词去掉名词后缀得到的动词，义为「容纳；为……提供住处；迁就」
由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「乐于助人的；随和的」
由本词加后缀 -ive 构成，义为「调节性的；愿意配合的」

senses.title: A place to stay
senses.definition: a place where someone can stay, especially while travelling or living away from home
senses.definitionCN: 指可以住下的地方，尤指旅行或离家期间
senses.example: The price includes accommodation and breakfast.
senses.exampleCN: 价格包含住宿和早餐。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to fit; a room that fits a traveller is the most concrete result of that fitting.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词意为「使合适」；一间刚好容下旅人的房间，就是这种「合适」最具体的结果。

senses.title: Lodging together with meals
senses.definition: a place to stay together with meals provided, often as part of a job or a course
senses.definitionCN: 指提供膳食的住处，常作为工作或课程的一部分
senses.example: The job comes with free accommodation and meals.
senses.exampleCN: 这份工作提供免费食宿。
senses.why: Fitting a person means fitting the whole person: a bed alone leaves hunger outside the arrangement.
senses.whyCN: 安置一个人就是安置完整的人：只给一张床，饥饿仍被留在安排之外。

senses.title: The act of adjusting to fit
senses.definition: the act of changing something, or of changing oneself, so that it fits a new condition
senses.definitionCN: 指改变某物或改变自身，使之适应新条件的行为
senses.example: Good accommodation to a new school takes time.
senses.exampleCN: 适应一所新学校需要时间。
senses.why: The core meaning is fitting: whenever two things must fit, one of them has to give a little.
senses.whyCN: 核心义就是「相合」：凡两样东西要合在一起，其中一样总要让一点。

senses.title: An agreement reached by adjustment
senses.definition: an arrangement in which two sides each accept less than they wanted, so that they can work together
senses.definitionCN: 指双方各自少要一点、从而能够共事的安排
senses.example: The two sides reached an accommodation after a long night of talks.
senses.exampleCN: 经过一夜长谈，双方达成了和解。
senses.why: Two positions that do not fit are bent until they do, and the result is an accommodation.
senses.whyCN: 两个合不上的立场被弯一弯，直到合上；这个结果就是和解。

senses.title: The eye's focusing adjustment
senses.definition: the change in the shape of the lens of the eye so that near or far objects stay in focus
senses.definitionCN: 指眼睛晶状体改变形状，使近处或远处物体保持清晰
senses.example: Accommodation of the lens lets the eye focus on a near page.
senses.exampleCN: 晶状体的调节让眼睛能看清近处的书页。
senses.why: Physiology uses the same word for the body part that changes its shape to fit the distance of an object.
senses.whyCN: 生理学用同一个词，指身体部位改变形状去迎合物体的远近。

senses.title: Rooms and facilities in the plural
senses.definition: in American English, the rooms, buildings, and services provided for guests or residents
senses.definitionCN: 在美式英语中，指为客人或住户提供的房间、建筑与服务设施
senses.example: The hotel has excellent accommodations for families.
senses.exampleCN: 这家旅馆有很适合家庭的住宿设施。
senses.why: What was one act of fitting becomes a set of concrete units you can count.
senses.whyCN: 原本一次「安置」的行为，变成了一组可以一个个数出来的具体单元。

senses.title: Space to hold people or things
senses.definition: the space or capacity available for people, cars, or objects
senses.definitionCN: 指可供人、车辆或物品使用的空间或容量
senses.example: The hall has accommodation for five hundred guests.
senses.exampleCN: 这个大厅能容纳五百位客人。
senses.why: Fitting is finally about space: a place accommodates what it can physically take in.
senses.whyCN: 「相合」说到底关乎空间：一个地方能装下多少，它就能容纳多少。

senses.title: Changes made for a special need
senses.definition: a change in rules, buildings, or equipment made so that a person with a disability can take part on equal terms
senses.definitionCN: 指为了让残障人士平等参与而修改规则、建筑或设备
senses.example: The school made several accommodations for students who need extra time.
senses.exampleCN: 学校为需要额外时间的学生做了几项便利安排。
senses.why: The fitting is now deliberate: the environment is bent so that a person who did not fit is included.
senses.whyCN: 这时的「相合」是有意为之：环境被弯一弯，让原本合不进来的人也被包含进去。

intro.en: Accommodation is built from the Latin word for measure, and its history runs from fitting to lodging.
intro.cn: accommodation 建立在拉丁语表示「尺度」的词上，它的历史从「使相合」一路走到「住宿」。

items.en: Modus meant 'measure, manner', and it also underlies mode and moderate.
items.cn: modus 意为「尺度、方式」，mode 与 moderate 也出自它。

items.en: Com- 'together' plus modus formed commodus, 'measured together, fitting, convenient'.
items.cn: com-「一起」加 modus 构成 commodus，意为「量得合适、方便合用的」。

items.en: Ad- 'to' plus commodare formed accommodare, 'to make fit, adapt', with a further sense of lending.
items.cn: ad-「向」加 commodare 构成 accommodare，意为「使合适、调节」，另有「借出」之义。

items.en: The noun accommodatio meant 'a fitting, an adjustment'; it passed through French and entered English in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 名词 accommodatio 意为「使相合、调节」；它经法语传入，在十六世纪进入英语。

items.en: The lodging sense develops in the eighteenth century, and the American plural for rooms and services becomes common later.
items.cn: 「住宿」义在十八世纪发展出来，美式英语中表示房间与设施的复数用法则在更晚时流行。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms of the same fitting root; the near-meaning group names places to stay and ways of adjusting.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「使相合」词根的各种形式；近义组列出住处与调节、妥协的说法。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to provide room for, to fit in with, or to do someone a favour.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「容纳、为……提供住处、迁就」，也可指帮某人的忙。

entries.definition: Willing to change plans to help other people.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「乐于助人的、随和的」，指愿意改变计划去配合别人。

entries.definition: A formal adjective for something that adjusts or is willing to adjust.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「调节性的、愿意配合的」，语气较正式。

entries.definition: Unwilling to help or to change arrangements for others.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不配合的、不肯通融的」，是 accommodating 加否定前缀构成的反义形式。

entries.definition: A place to sleep, often rented and usually without meals.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「寄宿处」，常指租来的睡觉之处，通常不含膳食。

entries.definition: Buildings for people to live in, especially as a social or official matter.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「住房、住宅」，多从社会或官方角度谈居住建筑。

entries.definition: Rooms provided for people to live in, used especially of soldiers or staff.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「住处、营房」，多指为军人或员工提供的房间。

entries.definition: An agreement in which each side gives up part of what it wanted.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「妥协」，指双方各自放弃部分要求的协议。

entries.definition: The process of changing to suit new conditions, with no idea of lodging.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「适应、改编」，只强调改变以适合新条件，不含住宿义。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin measure word and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语「尺度」词，以及这个词常出现的搭配。

normal.en: modus is measure: accommodation is what has been measured to fit.
normal.cn: modus 是「尺度」：accommodation 就是量过尺寸、刚好合上的东西。

normal.en: The same root gives commodity and commodious.
normal.cn: 同一词根还给出 commodity 与 commodious。

normal.en: Hotel accommodation is a room measured to fit a guest.
normal.cn: hotel accommodation 就是一间量好尺寸、刚好容下客人的房间。

normal.en: To reach an accommodation is to bend until two sides fit.
normal.cn: to reach an accommodation 就是弯一弯，让两边合上。

normal.en: The American plural accommodations counts the rooms one by one.
normal.cn: 美式复数 accommodations 把房间一间一间数出来。

abstract.en: A table and a small room: neither changes its nature, but one turns and both fit.
abstract.cn: 一张桌子和一间小屋：谁都没有改变本性，只是一转，两边就合上了。

abstract.en: The word covers a bed, a deal, an eye and a wheelchair ramp, because all four are ways of making things fit.
abstract.cn: 这个词涵盖一张床、一项协议、一只眼睛和一条轮椅坡道，因为四者都是让东西合上的办法。

abstract.en: Accommodation always costs a little space or a little pride, and that is why it works.
abstract.cn: 「相合」总要让出一点空间或一点自尊，也正因如此它才成立。

examples.en: The price includes accommodation and breakfast.
examples.cn: 价格包含住宿和早餐。

examples.en: The two sides reached an accommodation after a long night of talks.
examples.cn: 经过一夜长谈，双方达成了和解。

examples.en: Accommodation of the lens lets the eye focus on a near page.
examples.cn: 晶状体的调节让眼睛能看清近处的书页。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿康莫德申」——把桌椅挪一挪，刚好塞进屋里：住宿、调节、和解。

root: 拉丁语 accommodare「使合适」由 ad-「向」加 commodare「使合用」构成，后者来自 commodus「合适的」，而 commodus 是 com- 加 modus「尺度」构成的。

sensesIntro.en: Accommodation starts from the idea of measuring two things so that they fit, then becomes a room, a meal, an agreement, an eye movement, and a change made for someone's needs.
sensesIntro.cn: accommodation 从「量一量、让两样东西合上」出发，随后变成一间房、一顿饭、一份和解、一次眼睛的调节，以及为某人需要所做的改动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a table slightly too long is turned askew and slides into a small room.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张略长的桌子斜过来一放，刚好滑进小屋。

branches.en: THE ROOM: a place measured to hold a traveller, with or without meals.
branches.cn: 房间线：量好尺寸、刚好容下旅人的地方，供餐或不供餐。

branches.en: THE ADJUSTMENT: a person changes to a new school, and a lens changes for a near page.
branches.cn: 调节线：人适应新学校，晶状体适应近处的书页。

branches.en: THE DEAL: two positions bend until they fit and an agreement appears.
branches.cn: 协议线：两个立场各弯一点，直到合上，协议随之出现。

branches.en: THE UNITS: the plural turns one act of fitting into countable rooms and services.
branches.cn: 单元线：复数把一次「安置」变成可以计数的房间与服务。

branches.en: THE CAPACITY: space to take people in, and deliberate changes so that more people fit.
branches.cn: 容量线：能装下人的空间，以及为了让更多人合进来而做的特意改动。

intro.en: Accommodation is a Latin verb turned noun, with the prefix, the measure root and a long noun ending.
intro.cn: accommodation 是由拉丁语动词转成的名词，由前缀、「尺度」词根和较长的名词后缀组成。

latinIntro.en: Latin modus, commodus, accommodare and accommodatio are all recorded members of one family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 modus、commodus、accommodare 与 accommodatio 都是同一词族中有记录的形式。

items.meaning: a fitting, a place made to fit
items.meaningCN: 使相合；量好尺寸的地方
items.exampleCN: 我们找到了便宜的住处。
它出现在 accommodare 中。
modus 是表示「尺度」的词根。
commodus 由 com- 与 modus 组合而成。
它构成动词 accommodare。
它构成 accommodation。

items.example: The hall can accommodate two hundred people.
items.exampleCN: 这个大厅能容纳两百人。
它构成 accommodating。
它构成 unaccommodating。

definition_zh: 陪伴；陪同；伴随；附有；配餐；伴奏；自弹自唱
definition_en: to go somewhere with someone, to happen or exist together with something, or to play music in support of a performer
core_image: 两个人并排走，一个人的步子跟着另一个人的步子
scene: 演出前的后台很安静，歌手在钢琴边等灯光亮起。A young pianist accompanied her on the old upright piano.
sceneCN: 这里 accompany 指「为演唱者伴奏」（第 6 个义项：用乐器为表演者伴奏）；句意为一位年轻钢琴手用那架旧立式钢琴为她伴奏。

pos.zh: 动词：陪伴；陪同；伴随；附有；伴奏

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「伴奏；伴随物」
由本词加表示人的后缀 -ist 构成，义为「伴奏者」
由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「附随的；同时发生的」
由否定前缀 un- 加过去分词构成，义为「无人陪同的；无伴奏的」

senses.title: To go somewhere with someone
senses.definition: to travel or go somewhere together with another person, as a companion
senses.definitionCN: 指作为同伴与另一个人一起走或去某处
senses.example: Her brother accompanied her to the airport.
senses.exampleCN: 她哥哥陪她去了机场。
senses.why: The Latin word began as 'one who shares bread'; sharing the road grows straight out of sharing a meal.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词原本指「一起分面包的人」；一起分过面包，就很自然地走到一起上路。

senses.title: To escort someone politely
senses.definition: to go with someone to a place or to the door, especially in order to be polite or to protect them
senses.definitionCN: 指陪某人走到某处或门口，尤指出于礼貌或保护
senses.example: The host accompanied us to the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 主人把我们送到大门口。
senses.why: A companion who walks a guest out turns the shared road into a small act of courtesy.
senses.whyCN: 陪客人走出去的同伴，把「共走一段路」变成了一种小小的礼节。

senses.title: To happen at the same time as
senses.definition: of an event, condition, or symptom, to occur together with something else
senses.definitionCN: 指事件、状况或症状与另一事物同时出现
senses.example: The fever is often accompanied by a sore throat.
senses.exampleCN: 发烧常常伴有喉咙痛。
senses.why: Walking together becomes happening together: two things keep the same pace without either one causing the other.
senses.whyCN: 「一起走」变成「一起发生」：两件事步调一致，但谁也不必然引起谁。

senses.title: To be supplied together with
senses.definition: of a document, object, or item, to be provided together with something else
senses.definitionCN: 指文件、物品或附件与另一事物一起提供
senses.example: The application must be accompanied by two photographs.
senses.exampleCN: 申请材料必须附上两张照片。
senses.why: The thing that travels with the main thing is a companion in the literal sense: it never arrives alone.
senses.whyCN: 与主体一起走的东西就是字面意义上的同伴：它从不单独到达。

senses.title: To be served with a food or drink
senses.definition: of a drink or dish, to be served together with a particular food because the two go well together
senses.definitionCN: 指某种饮料或菜肴与特定食物搭配供应，因为二者相配
senses.example: A light white wine accompanies the fish course.
senses.exampleCN: 这道鱼配一款清淡的白葡萄酒。
senses.why: At the table the companion is the dish or drink that keeps the main course company.
senses.whyCN: 在餐桌上，同伴就是陪着主菜的那道菜或那杯酒。

senses.title: To play music in support of a performer
senses.definition: to play an instrument while someone sings or plays the main part
senses.definitionCN: 指在别人演唱或演奏主旋律时用乐器伴奏
senses.example: A young pianist accompanied her on the old upright piano.
senses.exampleCN: 一位年轻钢琴手用那架旧立式钢琴为她伴奏。
senses.why: In music the supporter literally walks beside the soloist, note for note, without taking the lead.
senses.whyCN: 在音乐里，支持者确实与独奏者并肩而行，一个音一个音地跟着，却不抢主位。

senses.title: To accompany oneself
senses.definition: in the phrase accompany oneself, to sing while playing an instrument for one's own support
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 accompany oneself，指一边演唱一边用乐器为自己伴奏
senses.example: He accompanied himself on the guitar at the small bar.
senses.exampleCN: 他在小酒吧里抱着吉他自弹自唱。
senses.why: The companion and the soloist collapse into one person, but the two roles stay separate in the grammar.
senses.whyCN: 同伴与独唱者合成了一个人，但这两个角色在语法上仍然分开。

senses.title: To add a gesture alongside words
senses.definition: to do something at the same time as speaking or acting, so that the two support each other
senses.definitionCN: 指在说话或行动的同时做另一件事，使二者互相配合
senses.example: He accompanied the warning with a shake of his head.
senses.exampleCN: 他一边警告，一边摇了摇头。
senses.why: Any action that walks beside another action is a companion; a gesture can accompany a sentence.
senses.whyCN: 任何与另一动作并肩而行的动作都是同伴；一个手势可以陪伴一句话。

intro.en: Accompany goes back to a Latin phrase for sharing bread, and the word still means keeping someone company.
intro.cn: accompany 可追溯到拉丁语中「分面包」的说法，这个词至今仍表示与人为伴。

items.en: Panis meant 'bread'; it is generally connected with pascere 'to feed, graze', though the deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: panis 意为「面包」；一般认为与 pascere「喂养、放牧」有关，更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Com- 'with' plus panis formed companio, 'one who shares bread with another'.
items.cn: com-「与」加 panis 构成 companio，意为「与他人分面包的人」。

items.en: Old French compaign meant 'companion', and the verb acompaignier meant 'to join someone as a companion'.
items.cn: 古法语 compaign 意为「同伴」，动词 acompaignier 意为「作为同伴加入某人」。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the fifteenth century; the musical sense is recorded from the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入这个动词；音乐义从十八世纪起有记录。

items.en: The passive form be accompanied by became a fixed pattern for symptoms, documents, and sounds.
items.cn: 被动形式 be accompanied by 成为描述症状、文件与声音的固定说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same bread root; the near-meaning group lists other ways of going along with someone.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「面包」词根的一族词；近义组列出其他「与人同行」的说法。

entries.definition: The music or thing that goes with a main part.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「伴奏、伴随物」，指与主体相配的音乐或事物。

entries.definition: A musician who plays for a singer or a soloist.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「伴奏者」，指为歌手或独奏者伴奏的音乐家。

entries.definition: Without anyone or anything going along; also used of music with no accompaniment.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无人陪同的、无伴奏的」，指没有同伴或没有伴奏。

entries.definition: A person who spends time with you, sharing the same bread root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「同伴、伙伴」，与本词共享「面包」词根。

entries.definition: The state of being with others, or a business, also from the bread root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「陪伴、公司」，同样出自「面包」词根。

entries.definition: To go with someone to protect or guide them, more formal than accompany.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「护送、陪同」，比 accompany 更正式，带有保护或引导意味。

entries.definition: To go with someone as a servant or official helper, an old formal use.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「随行、侍候」，是很旧的正式用法，指作为随从或助手同行。

entries.definition: To travel with vehicles or ships in order to protect them.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「护送、护航」，指为车辆或船只护行。

entries.definition: To go with young people to keep them safe and well behaved.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「陪同监护」，指陪着年轻人以保证安全与规矩。

entries.definition: To play music behind a singer, an informal word for the musical sense.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「为……伴奏、在背后支持」，是音乐义的口语说法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real bread root and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子使用真实的「面包」词根，以及这个词常出现的搭配。

normal.en: panis is bread: a companion is someone you share bread with.
normal.cn: panis 是「面包」：companion 就是和你分面包的人。

normal.en: The same root gives companion, company and companionship.
normal.cn: 同一词根还给出 companion、company 与 companionship。

normal.en: To accompany someone is to keep them company on the road.
normal.cn: to accompany someone 就是在路上与某人作伴。

normal.en: Be accompanied by is the pattern for symptoms and documents.
normal.cn: be accompanied by 是症状与文件常用的句式。

normal.en: An accompanist is the player who walks beside the soloist.
normal.cn: accompanist 就是走在独奏者身旁的演奏者。

abstract.en: Two pairs of footprints in the same snow, one set always half a step behind.
abstract.cn: 同一片雪地上有两行脚印，其中一行总落后半步。

abstract.en: A companion can be a person, a fever, a photograph or a chord; what matters is that it never arrives alone.
abstract.cn: 同伴可以是一个人、一场发烧、一张照片或一个和弦；关键在于它从不单独到来。

abstract.en: To accompany is to lend your step to someone else's direction.
abstract.cn: 陪伴就是把自己的脚步借给别人的方向。

examples.en: Her brother accompanied her to the airport.
examples.cn: 她哥哥陪她去了机场。

examples.en: The fever is often accompanied by a sore throat.
examples.cn: 发烧常常伴有喉咙痛。

examples.en: He accompanied himself on the guitar at the small bar.
examples.cn: 他在小酒吧里抱着吉他自弹自唱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿康帕尼」——两个人并排走，一个跟着一个的步子：陪伴、伴奏。

root: 晚期拉丁语 companio「分面包的人」由 com-「与」加 panis「面包」构成；古法语 acompaignier「作伴」进入英语成为 accompany。更早的印欧词源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Accompany begins with two people sharing bread and walking the same road, then spreads to symptoms, documents, dishes, music, and even a gesture that follows a sentence.
sensesIntro.cn: accompany 从两个人分面包、同走一条路开始，随后扩展到症状、文件、菜肴、音乐，甚至扩展到跟着一句话出现的手势。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people walk side by side, one step keeping time with the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个人并排走，一个人的步子跟着另一个人的步子。

branches.en: THE PERSON: walking beside a friend, or politely seeing a guest out.
branches.cn: 人物线：走在朋友身旁，或礼貌地把客人送出门。

branches.en: THE EVENT: two things keep pace, such as a fever and a sore throat.
branches.cn: 事件线：两件事步调一致，例如发烧与喉咙痛。

branches.en: THE THING: the photograph with an application and the wine with a fish course.
branches.cn: 物品线：随申请附上的照片，以及配鱼的葡萄酒。

branches.en: THE MUSIC: a pianist beside a singer, or a singer playing for himself.
branches.cn: 音乐线：歌手身旁的钢琴手，或自己为自己弹唱的歌手。

branches.en: THE GESTURE: a shake of the head that goes along with a warning.
branches.cn: 动作线：跟着一句警告一起出现的摇头。

intro.en: Accompany entered English as a French verb, and English added familiar endings to build the family.
intro.cn: accompany 作为法语动词进入英语，英语再加上常见的后缀扩展出词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin noun panis and the Late Latin companio are recorded; the compound is transparent, the deeper root is not.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语名词 panis 与晚期拉丁语 companio 均有记录；复合结构清楚，更早的词根则不清楚。

items.meaning: to join someone as a companion

scene: 月底对账时，她把每一笔进出都念给丈夫听。She read every line of the account aloud to her husband.

senses.title: An arrangement with a bank
senses.definition: an arrangement in which a bank or similar organization keeps your money and records what you pay in and take out
senses.definitionCN: 由银行或类似机构替你保管钱财、记录存入与支出的一种安排
senses.example: I opened a savings account at the bank near my flat.
senses.exampleCN: 我在公寓附近的银行开了一个储蓄账户。
senses.why: The core image is a ledger line written under one name; a bank account is simply that line kept by an institution on your behalf.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是账簿上写着一个名字的一行；银行账户就是机构替你保管的那一行，所以「账户」直接从记账的动作里长出来。

senses.title: A record of money paid and owed
senses.definition: the record of money that has been received, spent, or is still owed, especially in business
senses.definitionCN: 收入、支出或尚未付清的钱款记录，尤用于商业往来
senses.example: The shopkeeper checked the account before closing up.
senses.exampleCN: 店主在打烊前核对了账目。
senses.why: The ledger itself is the core picture: setting down each sum in order is exactly what the older word for reckoning named.
senses.whyCN: 账簿本身就是核心画面：把每一笔钱按顺序记下来，正是这个表示「核算」的古词所指的动作。

senses.title: A spoken or written report
senses.definition: a description of an event or situation, given by someone who saw it or knows about it
senses.definitionCN: 由目睹或了解情况的人对事件、处境所作的描述
senses.example: By her account, the meeting ended before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 按她的说法，会议在中午前就结束了。
senses.why: To keep accounts is to set events down one by one; telling what happened is the same ordering act, so the ledger word also means a story told.
senses.whyCN: 记账是把事情一条条列清楚；讲述发生了什么也是同一种排序的动作，于是账簿的词也用来指讲出来的那一版说法。

senses.title: A reason or explanation
senses.definition: an explanation that makes something clear, especially one that answers for a fault or a difference
senses.definitionCN: 使某事变得清楚的说明，尤指为过失或差额作出的交代
senses.example: He could give no account of the missing money.
senses.exampleCN: 他说不清那笔钱去了哪里。
senses.why: An account has to balance; when the figures do not match, someone must supply the words that explain the gap, and those words become an account.
senses.whyCN: 账要能对得上；当数字对不上时，总得有人说出话来解释差额，这些话就成了「解释」。

senses.title: To form a share of a total
senses.definition: to be a particular part or proportion of a whole, especially of an amount or a total
senses.definitionCN: 构成整体中的某一部分或比例，尤指金额或总数中的一份
senses.example: Rent accounts for half of their monthly spending.
senses.exampleCN: 房租占他们每月开销的一半。
senses.why: Split a total into ledger lines and each line is a portion; saying how much one line takes up is the accounting verb turned into a statement of proportion.
senses.whyCN: 把总数拆成一行行账目，每一行都是一份；说清某一行占去多少，就是记账的动词变成了「占比」的说法。

senses.title: Credit; payment at a later date
senses.definition: an arrangement in which goods or services are supplied now and paid for later
senses.definitionCN: 先取得商品或服务、以后再付款的一种安排
senses.example: They bought the sofa on account and paid it off in May.
senses.exampleCN: 他们赊账买了那张沙发，五月才付清。
senses.why: A ledger can be written forward in time: take the goods now, put the debt on the line, settle it later. The record becomes a form of credit.
senses.whyCN: 账目可以往后记：现在拿走货物，把欠款记在这一行，以后再结清；记录本身就变成了一种赊欠。

senses.title: A client or business relationship
senses.definition: a customer, especially one that a company serves regularly and earns money from
senses.definitionCN: 客户，尤指公司长期服务并从中获利的对象
senses.example: The design firm lost its biggest account last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这家设计公司去年春天失去了最大的客户。
senses.why: One ledger line stands for one paying party; by transference the line comes to mean the person or company behind it.
senses.whyCN: 账簿上的一行代表一个付钱的一方；经由转喻，这一行就转而指它背后的那个人或公司。

senses.title: To regard someone as something
senses.definition: to judge or consider someone or something to be a certain thing, especially in a formal statement
senses.definitionCN: 判定或认为某人某物属于某种情况，尤用于正式表述
senses.example: The team was accounted a great success.
senses.exampleCN: 这支队伍被认为取得了巨大成功。
senses.why: Reckoning means putting each item into its proper column; to account a person brave or a plan sound is to file them under that heading.
senses.whyCN: 核算就是把每一项放进该放的栏目；把一个人记成勇敢、把一个方案记成稳妥，就是把它归入那一栏，于是有了「认为、视为」。

intro.en: Account comes from a French phrase meaning 'to a count', built on Latin computare 'to reckon'; the money sense and the story sense grew from the same act of counting.
intro.cn: account 来自古法语中表示「照着数一遍」的短语，源头是拉丁语 computare「核算」；钱的意义与叙述的意义都从同一个「数」的动作长出来。

items.en: Putare meant 'to reckon, consider, judge'. It is generally explained from an older sense 'to prune, trim', though how cutting came to mean judging is still discussed.
items.cn: putare 意为「估算、认为、判断」。一般认为它有更早的「修剪」义，但「修剪」如何过渡到「判断」仍有讨论。

items.en: Com- 'together' plus putare gave computare, 'to reckon together, calculate'; it is the direct source of both count and account.
items.cn: com-「一起」加 putare 构成 computare，意为「合起来核算、计算」，是 count 与 account 的直接源头。

items.en: The phrase a + conte, literally 'to a count', became acont 'a reckoning, an instalment'; the verb conter meant 'to count, to tell'.
items.cn: 短语 a + conte 字面是「照着数一遍」，合成 acont，意为「核算、分期付款」；动词 conter 意为「数、讲述」。

items.en: The noun is recorded from about 1300 for a reckoning of money; the verb 'to count, reckon' follows, and the sense 'explain' appears later.
items.cn: 名词约在 1300 年有记录，指钱财的核算；动词「数、核算」随后出现，「解释」义更晚才成形。

items.en: Banking gave the word its everyday 'bank account' sense, while trade gave 'on account' for credit and 'account' for a regular client.
items.cn: 银行业带来日常的「银行账户」义，商业往来则带来赊账的 on account，以及指长期客户的 account。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the derived family and the Latin relatives of to count; the near-meaning group gathers documents and reports that record money or events.
note.cn: 形近组收由本词派生的词族，以及同出「计算」一源的亲属词；近义组收记录钱财或事件的单据与报告。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real French phrase behind the word and the fixed phrases it appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子使用这个词背后真实的法语短语，以及它固定出现的搭配。

normal.en: The word is a plus count: a reckoning written down under a name.
normal.cn: 这个词就是 a 加 count：写在一个名字底下的一笔核算。

normal.en: Latin computare gives both count and account, so to account for something is to give the count that explains it.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 computare 同时给出 count 与 account，所以 account for 就是拿出能解释它的那笔核算。

normal.en: A bank account is a ledger line that an institution keeps for you.
normal.cn: 银行账户就是机构替你保管的一行账。

normal.en: On account means the goods are put on the ledger now and paid for later.
normal.cn: on account 意为货物先记在账上，钱以后再付。

normal.en: Take account of means to put something into your reckoning before you decide.
normal.cn: take account of 意为在下判断之前把某事物算进你的核算里。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger open on a counter, one line for each name.
abstract.cn: 想象一本摊在柜台上的账簿，每个名字占一行。

abstract.en: The same line can hold coins, a story or a reason, because all three are things set down in order.
abstract.cn: 同一行账可以装钱、装一段经历，也可以装一个理由，因为这三样都是被按顺序记下来的东西。

abstract.en: When the numbers do not add up, someone has to give an account of the gap.
abstract.cn: 当数字对不上时，总得有人为那点差额给出一个说法。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿康特」——阿康把每一笔都记在账本上，还要讲清来龙去脉：账户、账目、叙述、解释。

root: 古法语 à + conte「照着数一遍」合成 acont，源头是拉丁语 computare「核算」，由 com-「一起」+ putare「估算、认为」构成。putare 更早的「修剪」义一般认为成立，但由「修剪」到「判断」的过渡仍有讨论。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses come from one act of setting things down in order: a ledger line for money, the same order applied to events, to an explanation, to a share, to credit, to a client, and finally to a judgement.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都来自同一个「按顺序记下」的动作：为钱记一行，再把同样的顺序用到事件、解释、份额、赊欠、客户，最后用到对人的判断上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open ledger on a counter, one line for each name, every coin set down in order.
core.cn: 核心意象：柜台上摊开的账簿，每个名字一行，每一枚钱币都按顺序记下。

branches.en: MONEY KEPT: the ledger line becomes an account held with a bank, or a record of what is owed.
branches.cn: 钱之线：账簿上的一行变成银行替你保管的账户，或一笔应收应付的记录。

branches.en: STORY TOLD: counting events one by one produces a reported version of what happened.
branches.cn: 叙述线：把事件一件件数出来，就得到关于所发生之事的说法。

branches.en: GAP EXPLAINED: when the figures do not match, the account becomes the reason offered for the difference.
branches.cn: 解释线：当数字对不上时，account 就变成为差额给出的理由。

branches.en: PORTION AND CREDIT: one line can be a share of the total, or goods written down to be paid later.
branches.cn: 份额与赊欠线：一行账可以是总额中的一份，也可以是先记下、以后再付的货物。

branches.en: PEOPLE AND JUDGEMENT: a line stands for a regular client, and to account someone is to file them under a heading.
branches.cn: 人与评判线：一行账可以代表长期客户，而把某人归到某一栏，就是对他作出判断。

intro.en: Account is a French phrase frozen into one word, with Latin pieces underneath; English adds familiar endings to build the family.
intro.cn: account 是一个凝固成单词的法语短语，底下是拉丁语的构件；英语再用常见词尾扩展出这一词族。

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 putare 与 computare 均有文献记录，只有 putare 最早的语义演变尚有不确定之处。
